finding.title: Keep every linked WebGLProgram alive (and pin ShaderMaterial shader stages) so disposing a material never forces a relink
finding.description: three r184 counts how many materials use each program and destroys it when the last one is disposed (releaseProgram, three.module.js:8009-8025). The next material with the same key then links from scratch. Holtburger disposes materials on several steady-play paths: entity despawn of owned materials, eviction from the paletted-material cache, eviction from the VFX paletted-variant cache, dynLod's remove()+spawn() (render-perf-2), and far-terrain patch and per-landblock terrain ShaderMaterials on evict. Only a few warm populations are deliberately kept alive by never-disposed proxy materials (archetype warm, pool prewarm). asyncLink does not cover this case. (a) Its shared readySigs set draws a material straight through when its key fingerprint was 'seen linked', on the assumption that the draw is a program-cache hit. If three has destroyed that program since, the draw links synchronously, which is exactly the 1070 hitch the guard exists to prevent. (b) ShaderMaterials (terrain, particles, post passes) and shadow-depth materials are not covered by the guard and always link synchronously. (c) Even deferred relinks skip draws for a few frames and spend GPU-process link time again; on ANGLE/D3D11 the GPU process stalls 244-637 ms after big links (light_loops.js header). WebAC measured 14 of 63 program keys relinked on a two-town route; retention brought that to 0 and cut link-stall time from 5,351 ms to 945 ms. WebAC's version has a hole that holtburger must close. For a ShaderMaterial the program key contains WebGLShaderCache stage ids, and those ids are reissued once the last material with that shader source is disposed. A retained ShaderMaterial program is therefore never found again unless the stage is also kept alive.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/scene/ProgramRetention.ts:29-57: `retainNew()` walks `renderer.info.programs` and does `p.usedTimes++` once per new program (WeakSet), so `usedTimes` never returns to 0. Called after every render at scene/SceneManager.ts:34 and :277. Measurement in docs/performance-budgets.md:379-401: '14 of the 63 program keys were relinked … programs released 30 → 0, recompiled keys 14 → 0, link-stall time inside long play-phase frames 5,351 → 945 ms'.
finding.holtburger_evidence: No retention anywhere: rg for usedTimes finds only shader_prewarm.js:321, which treats `usedTimes<=0` as 'released'. Dispose sites: entities.js:3129-3159 `_disposeMaterialIfOwned` → `mat.dispose()`; materials.js:4175 paletted LRU `try { oldMat?.dispose?.(); }`; materials.js:3877 vfxPalettedVariants LRU dispose (these carry unique `__vfxSetKey` program keys); far_terrain.js:1518 `patch.mat.dispose()`; terrain.js:5733 per-landblock ShaderMaterial `ownMat.dispose()`. The assumption that breaks: async_link_guard.js:95-100 ('A fingerprint the guard has already seen linked … is a program-cache hit and draws at once') and :501 `if (d === 3 && … readySigs.has(…)) { d = 0; stats.sigKnown += 1; }`. Holtburger already knows about the refcount: bake_prewarm.js:166-170 ('disposing them would release the very programs this warmed') and pool_prewarm.js:38-41. landblock_lru.js:2080-2087 instruments the opposite hypothesis ('program cache may retain … disposed materials').
finding.decomp_evidence: n/a (three.js engine behaviour). Verified in holtburger's three r184 copy (apps/holtburger-web/node_modules/three/build/three.module.js): acquireProgram :7990-8005 and releaseProgram :8009-8025 (destroy at usedTimes 0); WebGLShaderCache.remove :7300-7314 deletes a stage at usedTimes 0; WebGLShaderStage gets `this.id = _id ++` at :7373-7381; getProgramCacheKey pushes customVertexShaderID/customFragmentShaderID for non-built-in materials at :7776-7779.
finding.proposed_change: Add scene3d/program_retention.js (default ON, `?programRetain=off` escape) and call it once per rAF after the composer render, in the same render-tail spot index.js:556-599 already samples `renderer.info.programs`. When `programs.length` differs from the retained count, give each new program one extra reference (`usedTimes++`) and record it in a WeakSet. That is the WebAC algorithm, about 30 lines; credit WebAC under AGPL. Add `__diag.programs = {retained, relinkedKeys}`: keep a Set of cacheKeys ever seen, and count a new program whose key was seen before as a relink. Ship this diag first so the 1070 can measure relinks on a Holtburg↔Yaraq round trip with retention on and off. For ShaderMaterials, also keep one parked clone per distinct vertexShader+fragmentShader pair. Compile it once via withWarmTarget against a 3-vertex proxy in a parked, never-disposed group (the bake_prewarm.js archetype-warm idiom), so the stage refcount never reaches 0 and the key stays stable. Optional safety: a soft cap of about 1024 retained programs, released least-recently-used first. JS only, no wasm rebuild.

verification.reasoning: I re-read three r184 in holtburger's node_modules (the importmap pins three@0.184.0, index.html:986). acquireProgram/releaseProgram are at three.module.js:7988-8025, and destroy happens at usedTimes 0. WebGLShaderCache.remove deletes a stage at usedTimes 0 (:7300-7312). WebGLShaderStage gets `this.id = _id ++` (:7375). getProgramCacheKey pushes customVertexShaderID/customFragmentShaderID when there is no shaderID (:7770-7779). info.programs is the live programCache.programs array (:16402). WebAC ProgramRetention.ts:29-57 is called from SceneManager.ts:34/:277, and docs/performance-budgets.md:379-401 reports 14 of 63 keys relinked, falling to 0 with retention. Holtburger has no retention: usedTimes appears only in shader_prewarm.js:317-321 and tests. It already relies on the refcount through parked never-disposed proxies (bake_prewarm.js:166-170, pool_prewarm.js:38-41), and landblock_lru.js:2080-2088 only snapshots program counts. The dispose sites are real: entities.js:3129 `_disposeMaterialIfOwned`, materials.js:4175 (paletted re-seat), materials.js:3877 (vfx variant LRU), far_terrain.js:1518 and terrain.js:5733. The comparer overstates its point (a). The readySigs shortcut (async_link_guard.js:501) only fires for d===3, a version move with a changed fingerprint on an EXISTING material. A brand-new material with no currentProgram returns d=1 and is always deferred and compiled off-frame. So for guarded Mesh*Materials, a released program costs a deferred relink: a few skipped frames (pop-in) plus repeated GPU-process link time, not a synchronous hitch. The synchronous relinks that remain are three cases. (i) The d===3 sigKnown draw-through, when the remembered sig's program has since been destroyed. (ii) Unguarded ShaderMaterials (asyncLinkEligible :145-154 admits only far patches and `__asyncLink` opt-ins). (iii) Shadow-depth materials: three draws them with scene=null (three.module.js:9573/:9587), so the guard's `scene === mainScene` test never applies, and they are disposed together with their source material (onMaterialDispose :9607-9625). Retention makes (i) and (iii) cache hits. It also holds, for the first time, the guard's documented assumption that a seen fingerprint is a cache hit. WebAC's ShaderMaterial hole is real: a retained ShaderMaterial program whose stage was freed is unreachable, so retaining it is a pure leak. Corrected citation: the decision logic is async_link_guard.js:276-309 and the shortcut is :501.
verification.corrected_change: Add scene3d/program_retention.js (default ON, `?programRetain=off` escape, url-flags.md row). Call retainNew(renderer) once per rAF after the composer render, beside recordRenderDiag in scene3d/index.js. Algorithm, with WebAC credited under AGPL: read `renderer.info.programs`. If the array OBJECT changed since the last call, reset the count and WeakSet; context restore re-creates programCache (three.module.js:16402), and WebAC's length-only check would miss new programs whose count matches the old one. If the length differs from the retained count, give each unseen program `usedTimes++` and add it to the WeakSet. Skip programs with `p.type === 'ShaderMaterial' || p.type === 'RawShaderMaterial'` (WebGLProgram.type = material.type, three.module.js:7249) unless their family is explicitly pinned. Built-in, onBeforeCompile-patched 'hb|' and depth/distance programs are keyed by shaderID and are safe to retain. Diag `__diag.programs = {retained, skippedShader, relinkedKeys, keysSeen}`: keep a Set of cacheKeys ever seen, and count a newly appearing program whose key was seen before as a relink. Ship the diag first and measure on the 1070 (Holtburg <-> Yaraq round trip, retain on/off). Only for ShaderMaterial families the diag shows relinking (per-LB terrain, water, particles), park one never-disposed clone per distinct vertexShader+fragmentShader string pair. Compile it once with withWarmTarget against a 3-vertex proxy in a parked group, the archetype-warm idiom. That keeps the stage's usedTimes >= 1, so the stage id and program key stay stable; then retain those programs too. Optional soft cap of about 1024 retained programs. JS only, no wasm.
verification.rynth_risk: none (render-tail hook only; rynth/** and plugins/rynth-* are untouched)
verification.test_plan: New tests/program_retention.test.mjs (node, targeted). Use a fake renderer whose info.programs is an array of {usedTimes:1, type, cacheKey}. Assert: (1) retainNew bumps each built-in program exactly once, and repeated calls are no-ops; (2) ShaderMaterial/RawShaderMaterial programs are skipped unless pinned; (3) simulating three's releaseProgram (decrement, splice at 0) never removes a retained program; (4) replacing the info.programs array (context restore) re-retains the new programs even when the length is unchanged; (5) relinkedKeys counts a key that disappears and reappears when retention is off. Live check on the 1070 with the diag: programs released → 0 and relinkedKeys → 0 on the route.

implementation.summary: I added scene3d/program_retention.js, which is on by default; `?programRetain=off` turns it off. Once per rendered frame it gives each WebGLProgram linked since the last call one extra reference (`usedTimes++`) and records it in a WeakSet, so three r184's releaseProgram never destroys it and the next material with that cache key gets the cached program instead of relinking. This is the WebAC ProgramRetention algorithm (credited, AGPL-3.0) with both holes closed. First, it tracks the identity of the `info.programs` array, so a context restore that creates a same-length array still gets re-retained. Second, it skips programs keyed by WebGLShaderStage ids (ShaderMaterial, RawShaderMaterial, or any custom-type subclass whose cacheKey starts with a number), because their keys change once the shader stage is freed. Those are only retained when the caller pins their stage pair (`pinStagePair` / `pinMaterialStages`) and keeps a parked material alive. The per-frame check compares the array object, its length and its last element, and does a full rescan every 240 calls. The rescan catches a program created and then swapped out of the last slot by a release in the same window. A soft cap of 1024 stops adding new retentions past that count. `window.__diag.programs` is a live stats object updated in place: retained, skippedShader, overCap, pinnedFamilies, keysSeen, relinks, relinkedKeys, relinkedBy, released, scans, contextResets. The diag counts relinks with retention off too, so `?programRetain=off` serves as the A/B baseline for the 1070 measurement. The hook is one call inside recordRenderDiag in scene3d/index.js, which all three render paths (portal-space, composer, direct) already pass through. JS only, no wasm.
implementation.url_flag_rows: | `programRetain`=off (default **ON**) | Keeps every linked WebGLProgram for the session (scene3d/program_retention.js, render-perf-1; after WebAC ProgramRetention.ts, AGPL-3.0). Each new program gets one extra `usedTimes` reference at the render tail (index.js recordRenderDiag), so three r184's releaseProgram never destroys it when its last material is disposed (entity despawn, paletted/VFX LRUs, shadow-depth clones), and the next material with that key hits the program cache instead of relinking. Stage-keyed programs (ShaderMaterial/RawShaderMaterial/custom-type subclasses) are skipped unless their stage pair is pinned, because their keys change once the stage is freed. Tracks `info.programs` array identity (context restore). Soft cap 1024. Diag `window.__diag.programs` {retained, skippedShader, overCap, keysSeen, relinks, relinkedKeys, relinkedBy, released, contextResets}; relinks are counted with the flag off too. Off = three's stock refcount lifetime. Pinned by tests/program_retention.test.mjs. | 1070, `?nosw=1`: Holtburg <-> Yaraq round trip (@telepoi hops plus some street walking), once default and once with `&programRetain=off`; read `__diag.programs` (and `__linkProbe.ledgerStats()` with `&linkProbe=on`) at the end of each. | ON: `relinks` 0 for built-in families (anything left appears only under ShaderMaterial names in `relinkedBy`), `released` close to 0, program count levels off instead of swinging; OFF shows nonzero relinks (the baseline). No visual difference; 0 console errors; `retained` stays well under 1024. |
implementation.eye_test: Optional, measurement only: this changes no visuals and needs no eye-test before shipping. On the 1070 (off-screen, `?nosw=1`), do a Holtburg <-> Yaraq round trip twice: once with the default URL and once with `&programRetain=off`. Add `&linkProbe=on` to both runs for the per-key ledger. At the end of each run, read `window.__diag.programs` and `__linkProbe.ledgerStats()`. Pass criteria: with retention on, `relinks` and `released` are 0, or close to it, for built-in families, and `ledgerStats().relinks` drops to about 0. Any remaining relinks show under ShaderMaterial family names in `relinkedBy` (e.g. terrain, water, particles); those are the candidates for parked-clone pinning. The world must look identical in both runs with 0 console errors. Also check that `retained` levels off in the low hundreds.
implementation.deviations: (1) Programs skipped are a superset of what the verifier specified. Besides `type === ShaderMaterial/RawShaderMaterial`, I skip any program whose cacheKey starts with a number. A built-in shaderID is a word ('physical', 'depth', ...); a numeric first field is a WebGLShaderStage id. This covers ShaderMaterial subclasses that set their own `type` (e.g. three/examples LineMaterial), which have the same stage-id hole. (2) The call is one line inside recordRenderDiag rather than separate lines next to each recordRenderDiag call. All three render paths (portal-space, composer, direct) already end there, the same way vfxGaugeEndFrame is hooked. (3) The change check is array identity + length + last element, plus a full sweep every 240 calls. WebAC checks length only, which misses a program created and then swapped out of the last slot by a release in the same window; test case 6 covers this. (4) The soft cap stops adding retentions once 1024 are held; it is not an LRU. three exposes no public releaseProgram, so dropping our extra reference from a program no material uses could never actually destroy it. (5) I did not wire parked-clone pinning for ShaderMaterial families, following the verifier's 'ship the diag first' order. The pin API (`pinStagePair`, `pinMaterialStages`) exists and is tested, but nothing calls it yet. (6) The diag has extra fields beyond {retained, skippedShader, relinkedKeys, keysSeen}: relinks, relinkedBy (capped at 64 labels plus '(other)'), released, overCap, pinnedFamilies, scans, contextResets. Programs re-created after a context restore are not counted as relinks; per-context state resets and `contextResets` increments instead.
implementation.follow_ups: (a) After merging, run `node scripts/gen-modulepreload.mjs` so index.html's generated modulepreload block includes ./scene3d/program_retention.js. I did not edit index.html: it is outside my lane and the block is generated. (b) Once the 1070 diag names the ShaderMaterial families that relink (`__diag.programs.relinkedBy`), give each one a parked, never-disposed clone compiled with withWarmTarget against a 3-vertex proxy (the bake_prewarm archetype-warm idiom), then call `getProgramRetention().pinMaterialStages(renderer, clone)`. Pins are per context: re-pin after a context restore. (c) ui/ac_paperdoll_viewport.js and ui/ac_dye_viewport.js each have their own WebGLRenderer and program cache. WebAC measured paperdoll relinks; those could each get their own `createProgramRetention()` instance. (d) Retention makes the program cache last longer. If a customProgramCacheKey collision exists (two patch sets sharing one key), it now lasts the whole session instead of possibly clearing itself once every material with that key is disposed. It is already order-dependent today, so not a new bug, but worth keeping in mind during the eye-test. (e) The area_missed_notes items (duplicate full-detail statics LOD levels, dynLod dropping back to full detail past the last band, LOD ignoring placement scale) belong with render-perf-2/3 and are not addressed here.

finding.title: dynLod re-parses Setup/GfxObj/DegradeInfo for every entity twice a second and respawns on level changes that look identical
finding.description: The T9 dynamic-LOD tick is on by default and runs every 0.5 s. It fires one async wasm call to fetch_entity_degrade_for_distance per entity. `_lodOriginalSetup` is set to the spawn setupId for every entity, so the '// no degrade chain captured' skip never skips anything. Inside the wasm function, the uncached resolve_did_degrade runs twice: once inside the prefetch walk closure and once after it. Each run unpacks the SetupModel, and for a single-part setup unpacks the whole GfxObj (vertices and polygons) just to read did_degrade. The function then unpacks the GfxObjDegradeInfo again. Multi-part setups can never return a substitute (lib.rs returns 0 when parts.len() != 1), and a memoised resolve_did_degrade_cached already exists but is not used here. A town with a few hundred entities therefore pays hundreds of record parses in one burst every 0.5 s. When the returned id changes, _respawnForLod tears down and rebuilds the whole rig: mixer, actions and owned materials, which feeds render-perf-1's relinks. The comparison is by band gfx id, and 0 ('no substitute') is distinct from a level-0 id that is the base part's own GfxObj, so a respawn can produce exactly the same geometry. The code's own note records the resulting thrash: a 'Pumpkin Buffer' 11.5 m away respawned 20 times in 10 s. Retail selects the level with a pure function over a chain loaded once, swaps the drawn GfxObj in place, and beyond 50 m outdoors uses the land-cell centre's 2-D distance, so the level only changes when the viewer or the object crosses a cell.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/models/DegradeLod.ts:525 `private chains = new LruMap<number, DegradeChain | null>(4096)` and :579-616 `chainFor()` parse each chain once per GfxObj. :568-571 `levelFor()` is a synchronous pure selection. :658-725 `updateParts()` runs per frame with no DAT access; beyond MAX_CELL_2D_DEGRADE_DISTANCE it uses `landCellViewerDistance` (:58, :79-85). Levels are swapped in place through per-level holders (:461, :731-790), with no despawn. The instanced path does the same: terrain/SceneryInstancePool.ts:224-243 `updateLod` / :338-345 `selectLevel`.
finding.holtburger_evidence: entities.js:2034-2039 `DYN_LOD_ON = … get("dynLod")?.toLowerCase() !== "off"` (default on); :2046 `DYN_LOD_INTERVAL_S = 0.5`; :4270 `const lodOriginalSetup = setupId;` → :4584 `inst._lodOriginalSetup = lodOriginalSetup;`; :15641 `if (!inst._lodOriginalSetup) continue; // no degrade chain captured` (never true); :15684-15697 `Promise.resolve(lodFetch(inst._lodOriginalSetup, distance))` per entity, then `_respawnForLod` (:15711) when `sub !== inst._lodSub`. Thrash note at :4317-4325. src/lib.rs:15611-15615 `ensure_walk_prefetched(…, |s| { let _ = resolve_did_degrade(s, setup_id); })` then `let degrade_id = resolve_did_degrade(source.as_ref(), setup_id);` (uncached); :15628 `GfxObjDegradeInfo::unpack(&bytes)` on every call; :10665 `if setup.parts.len() != 1 { return 0; }`; the memoised variant at :10715 `resolve_did_degrade_cached` is unused here.
finding.decomp_evidence: CPhysicsPart::LoadGfxObjArray (acclient.c:314892, per PERF-LOG) loads the chain once. GfxObjDegradeInfo::get_degrade at acclient.c:332356-332430 is a pure function of (distance, deg_mul). CPhysicsObj::UpdateViewerDistance at :317913-317960 uses one object distance when the 2-D distance² ≥ object_distance_2dsq. RenderDeviceD3D::UpdateObjCell at :458101-458140 passes the cell's distance to every object in the cell beyond 50.0. CLandCell::GetViewerDistance at :355104-355118 is the 2-D distance (z zeroed) to the cell position. The UpdateObjCell decompile loses the st0 return value; the reading matches WebAC's x87 analysis.
finding.proposed_change: (1) Rust, apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs: add `fetch_entity_degrade_chain(setup_id)`, returning the parsed level list (gfx, mode, min, ideal, max) or empty. Build it on resolve_did_degrade_cached plus a small memo of GfxObjDegradeInfo keyed by chain id. Native test with the existing fixtures. (2) entities.js: at spawn, fetch the chain once per setupId (JS Map memo). Set `_lodOriginalSetup = 0` when the chain is empty or the setup has several parts, so the tick skips those entities. (3) The tick selects the level synchronously with a shared retail get_degrade (render-perf-3); no wasm call per tick. (4) Compare resolved GfxObj ids and treat 'level gfx == base part gfx' as 0, so transitions to the same geometry never respawn. (5) Beyond 50 m, use the land-cell-centre 2-D distance (floor(x/24)+0.5 in AC coordinates). This adds retail's natural hysteresis and removes the thrash class. (6) Follow-up: swap part 0's geometry in place, the way the ReplaceObject hook does, instead of remove()+spawn(). Rebuild wasm for step 1. Keep the `?dynLod=off` escape.

verification.reasoning: Most perf claims hold, but the comparer's line numbers in lib.rs are stale. The function is fetch_entity_degrade_for_distance_inner at src/lib.rs:15858-15905. resolve_did_degrade (uncached) runs inside the ensure_walk_prefetched closure (:15879-15882; run_walk_loop always runs the walk at least once against a RecordingSource, prefetch.rs:311-321) and again at :15883. GfxObjDegradeInfo::unpack runs on every call (:15895), and the band-window pick is at :15899-15904. resolve_did_degrade returns 0 for multi-part setups (:10665) after unpacking the SetupModel, so creatures (most entities) pay two SetupModel parses per tick for an answer that is always 0. The memoised resolve_did_degrade_cached (:10715) is unused here. JS: DYN_LOD_ON defaults on (entities.js:2034-2043), DYN_LOD_INTERVAL_S = 0.5 (:2046), `lodOriginalSetup = setupId` (:4270, stored :4584), and the `!inst._lodOriginalSetup` skip (:15641) never fires. One async wasm call per entity per tick (:15684-15697). The thrash claim is OUT OF DATE. The 'Pumpkin Buffer' 20-respawns note documents a bug fixed in 9665230d (2026-10-11): _respawnForLod passes the tick's band as meta._lodForcedSub (:15717-15718), and the spawn uses it instead of the 25 m-bucket memo (:4318-4330). What still stands: (a) a respawn to identical geometry. The spawn threads a band pick as a part-0 model change (:4353-4365, :4379-4388), and holtburger's real-byte fixture for 0x11000001 (crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/degrade_info.rs:66-80) shows bands 0 and 1 are the base GfxObj 0x0100376A. So crossing min_dist0 (10 m) does a full remove()+spawn() (rig, mixer and owned materials, which feeds render-perf-1) for the same mesh. (b) Past the last real band the loop falls through to `Ok(0)` (:15904), so an entity flips back to FULL detail, with a respawn, at the last band's max_dist (about 200 m). That is a new point the comparer only hinted at. Retail selects levels with a pure function over a chain loaded once (get_degrade acclient.c:332356-332432) and swaps in place inside the part array (CPhysicsPart::UpdateViewerDistance :315171-315190, gfxobj[deg_level]). The beyond-50 m cell distance (RenderDeviceD3D::UpdateObjCell :458101-458140, CLandCell::GetViewerDistance :355104-355118) is read correctly, but it is a refinement, not needed for the fix.
verification.corrected_change: Split it so the perf half carries no visual risk. Phase A (no visual change, behind the existing dynLod flag): in Rust fetch_entity_degrade_for_distance_inner, use resolve_did_degrade_cached in both the walk closure and the final call. Memoise the parsed degrade levels by chain id, in a small thread_local HashMap with a cap like DID_DEGRADE_MEMO's, storing only on a clean read. Return 0 when the picked band's gfx_obj_id equals the setup's part-0 GfxObj, or the model id itself for 0x01, so 'same geometry' and 'base' compare equal. This also covers the spawns.js batch path through fetch_entity_degrade_for_distance_batch. Add a cheap export `entity_degrade_chain_id(setup_id) -> u32` built on resolve_did_degrade_cached. In JS, memoise it per setupId and set `inst._lodOriginalSetup = 0` when it is 0 (multi-part or no chain), so the tick skips those entities entirely. Needs a wasm rebuild (orchestrator). Phase B (render, new flag such as `?dynLodRetail`, 1070 eye test): fetch the chain levels once per chain id and pick synchronously with part_degrade.js selectDegradeLevel at deg_mul RETAIL_DEG_MUL = 1 (render-perf-4), distance divided by the root's scale. Map the picked level's gfx to 0 when it equals base part 0. Respawn only when the resolved gfx changes. Never map a NULL/INVALID level to 'hide' (the visuals rule): clamp to the last drawable level, which also removes the full-detail flip past the last band. Later follow-up: swap part 0's geometry in place instead of remove()+spawn().
verification.rynth_risk: none directly. Fewer LOD respawns means fewer lodRespawn selection releases, which can only help a bot that holds a target. Do not touch rynth/** and do not change picking.js.
verification.test_plan: Rust native tests in lib.rs (cfg(test)) on a pure helper `pick_entity_degrade(levels, base_gfx, distance) -> u32`, extracted from the inner fn: the 0x11000001 bytes from degrade_info.rs give 0 at 5 m, 0 (same gfx as base) at 12 m and 30 m, and no full-detail flip beyond the last band in the Phase B variant. resolve_did_degrade_cached is hit on the second call (counting source). Node test tests/dyn_lod_tick.test.mjs: a stub EntityManager-like loop with a counting fake lodFetch. Assert multi-part setups (chain id 0) are queried zero times after spawn, a sub equal to the current _lodSub never calls _respawnForLod, and the existing tests/lod_respawn_selection test still passes unedited.

implementation.summary: Phase A only (perf, no intended visual change). In Rust (apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs), fetch_entity_degrade_for_distance_inner used to run the uncached resolve_did_degrade twice per call and unpack GfxObjDegradeInfo every time. It now tries a memo-only fast path first (no record read, no prefetch round). On a miss it runs a single prefetch walk whose closure performs the whole cached pick. Three new memos back this: the existing DID_DEGRADE_MEMO, now read through a new resolve_did_degrade_cached_checked; a new DEGRADE_BASE_GFX_MEMO (setup to its part-0 GfxObj); and DEGRADE_LEVELS_MEMO (chain id to parsed levels). All three only store clean reads and are cleared in model_tri_cache_clear_all. A pure pick_entity_degrade(levels, base_gfx, distance) keeps the old first-band [min,max) pick but returns 0 when the band names the entity's own base GfxObj. So 'same geometry' and 'full detail' now compare equal, and crossing 0x11000001's 10 m edge no longer remove()+spawn()s onto the identical mesh. The batch export inherits all of this. A new additive async export entity_degrade_chain_id(setup_id) returns the chain id (0 = no chain or a multi-part setup). It rejects on a non-resident record so JS never memoises a miss as 'no chain'. In JS, the new scene3d/lod_chain_memo.js memoises that probe per setupId, sharing one in-flight query. EntityManager._gateLodChain (called in _spawnImpl right after the T9 LOD fields are stamped, and only when DYN_LOD_ON) zeroes _lodOriginalSetup for chainless setups, so the tick's existing skip finally fires. finding.title: Degrade thresholds in both default-on LOD paths are not retail's get_degrade (no 50 m offset; min_dist used as the swap point)
finding.description: Retail get_degrade computes d' = max(|d| − s_rDegradeDistance (50.0), 0). It then takes the first level i with d' < ideal_i + (max_i − ideal_i)·deg_mul, and the last level when the loop runs off the end. Holtburger uses two different, non-retail rules. (a) dynLod (Rust) returns the first band whose [min_dist, max_dist) contains the raw distance. There is no 50 m offset, so it swaps at 10-25 m where retail stays at level 0 out to 50 m plus at least ideal_0. Beyond the last real band it returns 0, which means the full-detail original. (b) The statics THREE.LOD adds one level per band at that band's min_dist; when min_dist is 0 it falls back to 100 m·(i+1) and forces the list ascending. Its comment says 'the exact retail threshold isn't preserved in the DAT', but get_degrade plus s_rDegradeDistance define it exactly. Example: WebAC's EoL fixture chain 0x1100001C has levels (min, ideal, max) of (10, 25, 50), (25, 50, 100), (50, 100, 200) and an INVALID level. Holtburger's statics LOD shows the coarsest level, 0x10037A7, from 50 m. Retail shows it from 100 m at deg_mul 0, or 150 m at deg_mul 1. So holtburger draws coarser geometry than retail across roughly 50-150 m: a retail-faithful fix is also a quality upgrade. Scope: 0x01 GfxObj statics and single-part setups only, since multi-part setups get no chain (lib.rs:10665).

implementation.summary: I added an opt-in `?retailDegrade=on` flag (exact `=== "on"`, default OFF) to scene3d/statics.js. When on, the statics THREE.LOD switch distances follow retail GfxObjDegradeInfo::get_degrade (acclient.c:332356), which I re-read in the decomp. The rule is d' = max(d/scale − 50, 0) (Render::s_rDegradeDistance, :45516). Each level's threshold is T_i = ideal + (max − ideal)·deg_mul, with deg_mul = part_degrade.js RETAIL_DEG_MUL (1.0); deg_mul < 0 uses min instead. Level i first draws at (50 + max_{j<i} T_j)·placementScale, or at 0 m when that max is 0. A level that can never be reached is dropped, except the last one, because retail's walk always ends on it. A new pure export, `retailBandSwapDistances(levels, baseGfx, degMul, scale)`, returns those levels plus a band→LOD-level table. With the flag on, fetchDegradedGeometries keeps the whole chain and does not clone a level that names the same GfxObj and billboard class as the level before it (the base model counts as level 0). NULL (gfx 0) levels never hide anything: the previous level keeps drawing. The singleton builder multiplies the switch distances by the placement scale, matching retail's divide by gfxobj_scale.z; the instanced builder uses scale 1. When a surface's level list would end up empty, it keeps one level parked at Number.MAX_VALUE (never drawn), so the node stays a THREE.LOD and the draw path matches the flag-off build. With the flag off, the code path and outputs are unchanged, and the new test pins the legacy bandSwapDistances results. For the 0x11000001-shaped chain, the change means full detail out to 150 m instead of L2 from 50 m.

finding.title: Retail ships Automatic Degrades on, so deg_mul climbs to 1.0 above 25 fps; holtburger pins 0 and calls it 'retail's neutral point'
finding.description: Holtburger's partDegrade, and any port of render-perf-3, needs a deg_mul value. part_degrade.js holds it at 0 and calls that retail's neutral point. Retail's static initialiser sets auto_update_deg_mul = true, and it is registered as the 'Automatic degrades' preference. Render::CalcDegLevel runs every frame. Above 1.25 × max_framerate (20) = 25 fps, its very-high weight is 1 and every other weight is 0, so deg_mul rises 0.1 per frame and clamps at 1.0 within about 10 frames. get_degrade reads deg_mul whenever auto mode is on. On any machine holtburger targets, retail therefore selects levels against max_dist, not ideal_dist. Consequences: (a) once `?partDegrade` ships, it would hide human body parts at 50 + 84 = 134 m; retail at deg_mul 1 hides them at 50 + max_dist of that level, which is farther, so NPCs would pop out earlier than retail. (b) The thresholds in render-perf-3 should use deg_mul = 1. PERF-LOG lists 'deg_mul auto-tune' as open lead (4). WebAC supplies the new evidence (the defaults plus the controller math) and a ready port.

finding.title: Experiment: the tunnel warm only compiles; it never draws, so geometry, VAO and first-draw costs still land on the first camera turn
finding.description: Holtburger's tunnel-time warm (`?tunnelWorldWarm`) and the bake prewarms only call renderer.compile. Every object still pays its first-draw costs during play: buffer upload (static-batch-c buckets upload whole), VAO and attribute setup, and shadow depth-material creation. Holtburger's own untraced census of the first 12 s street sweep counted 118 MB of buffer uploads and 117 MB of texture uploads, with 1,887 objects drawn for the first time. A worst frame of about 1 s remains unattributed in both lightLoops arms (open lead 3). Pre-uploading textures alone was a measured negative result, so the untested remainder is buffer upload plus per-object first-draw setup. WebAC pays exactly these while the portal cover is up: initTexture, then one tiny render per frame at 4 yaw headings plus one looking down, and during play one unlit override draw of each newly streamed subtree. Its M3 Max table shows turning-phase hitches over 50 ms going to 0 with warm + fixed light count + play-time upload. Speculative for the 1070; worth one A/B.

The new `?lodCollapseDup` flag is default ON, with `=off` as the escape. In scene3d/statics.js, `fetchDegradedGeometries` now plans each (model, surface) level list before it clones anything (`planLodDupCollapse`). A level is dropped without being cloned when its geometry is the same as the level just before it. Band 0 matches the base surface group only when it has the same gfxId and byte-identical attributes. Band i matches band i-1 when both come from the same fetched source. Every surviving level keeps the exact swap distance `bandSwapDistances` gave it over the full list, so the next real level switches at the same distance as before. To keep the default look identical: lists with a billboard band (degradeMode >= 2) are left alone, because `tagBillboardLod` picks `levels[1]` by index. A list where every level is a duplicate keeps its first level, so the node stays a THREE.LOD and does not move onto the static batch/atlas path. implementation.deviations:
The verifier's corrected_change targets the tunnel sweep (static-batch-c `_INIT_VERTS` first, then an opt-in `?tunnelSweep=on`). The orchestrator told me not to implement it, so I did neither. Inside MISSED-1 I tightened the literal rule ("gfxId equals the base modelId or the previous level's gfxId") so the default look stays exactly the same:
(1) Band 0 collapses into the base only when the bytes are identical, not just the gfxId. `?canopySoften` (default ON, 0.65) bends the base normals of wind-responsive models, while band clones of the same GfxObj are not softened. Collapsing those self bands would change tree shading from about 10 m out. Band 1 = band 0 still collapses for those models.
(2) "Previous level" means the level just before it in the same surface list. A `[X, self]` chain is not collapsed, because self would then show X's mesh (220 models).
(3) Lists with a billboard band are left as they are, because `tagBillboardLod` orients `levels[1]` by index (833 of 4,131 chain models).
(4) An all-duplicate list keeps its first level so the node stays a THREE.LOD. A plain Mesh would become eligible for staticBatch/atlas/pool, which is a different draw path.
(5) Survivors are given their resolved full-list swap distances. Otherwise bumped distances (e.g. 24.001) and index-based fallback distances (100·(i+1)) would shift.
The set of fetched gfx ids is unchanged: the base id is still fetched, because keep-first lists need it and the wasm decode is memoized. The saving is clones, LOD levels, InstancedMesh leaves and GPU buffers.
implementation.follow_ups:
(a) 1,080 non-billboard all-duplicate models still carry one duplicate level, for example single-band self chains. Making them plain Meshes would remove it, but it changes batch/atlas eligibility, so it needs an eye-test plus a perf A/B.
(b) Pre-existing bug: `tagBillboardLod` hardcodes `billboardLevel = 1`. In a chain like [self (mode 1), X (mode 5)] the tick orients the self clone with X's mode instead of orienting X. Fixing it changes visuals, so it needs a flag and an eye-test. This is also why billboard lists are excluded here.
(c) Look question for the owner: degraded clones of the same GfxObj skip canopy softening. Trees switch from softened to flat-normal shading at band 0's min_dist (about 10–15 m). If softening were applied to self bands, those bands would also collapse.
(d) `?lodBandDiag` now sees fewer level transitions (identical levels are gone). This affects diagnostics only.
(e) Area notes MISSED-2 (dynLod falls back to full detail past the last band) and MISSED-3 (statics LOD ignores placement scale; retail divides the distance by gfxobj_scale.z) are untouched.
(f) The tunnel sweep is still open. The verifier says to do PERF-LOG lead (1), right-sizing static-batch-c, first.
(g) DAT survey (scratch script over ~/ac_base_dats/client_portal.dat): 4,131 chain-carrying GfxObjs, 13,501 mode-1 bands, 259 mode-2, 573 mode-5, 11 mode-4. Among non-billboard chains: 3,623 adjacent duplicates out of 8,079 levels, 456 of them band-to-band.

finding.title: Fading entities keep the ClipMap alpha test, so clip-map parts vanish mid-fade instead of fading
finding.description: Retail SetSurface has a branch for a part whose CMaterial has alpha (any fade): the alpha test goes OFF, the blend is forced to SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA and depth writes go off. Holtburger's four opacity owners only multiply `opacity`, set `transparent=true` and set `depthWrite=false`. They leave `alphaTest` at the retail ClipMap ref (100/255 paletted, 200/255 DDS). In three r184, `diffuseColor = vec4(diffuse, opacity) * texel` and `if (diffuseColor.a < alphaTest) discard;`. A DDS clip-map part (ref 0.784) is therefore discarded entirely once opacity drops below 0.784, which is 22% into a fade-out; a paletted one disappears below 0.39. Retail fades the whole part smoothly with its cut-outs intact (alpha-0 texels still blend to nothing). Paths affected: PhysicsDesc/UpdateObject translucency (e.g. a ghost spawned at T=0.5 loses every DDS clip-map part), Transparent(20/7) hook ramps such as portal Hide/UnHide fades, the default-on retailCamZoom near-fade/in-head fade of the local player, and the opt-in ethereal ghost. There are 721 ClipMap surfaces (per holtburger's own census); recoloured clip-maps include dolls and Virindi.

MaterialFactory.ts:193-196 surfaceMaterialState(materialHasAlpha) does the same for a fading part: `{ blend: true, src: SrcAlpha, dst: InvSrcAlpha, alphaTest: false, depthWrite: false }`.

No `alphaTest = 0` exists on any fade path (rg over scene3d).
finding.decomp_evidence: acclient.c:454529-454540 D3DPolyRender::SetSurface: `v13 = <current CMaterial>; if ( v13 == 0.0 || !*(_DWORD *)(LODWORD(v13) + 8) || v11 && singlePassDetailinga != 1 ) {...} else { v9 = 5; v10 = 6; surfacea = 1; singlePassDetailinga = 0; curr_texturea = 0; }`. Offset +8 is CMaterial::has_alpha (acclient.h:31753-31756). Line 454544 `SetAlphaTestEnable(v4, singlePassDetailinga)` so the test is OFF; line 454550 `SetDepthBufferMode(..., curr_texturea)` so depth writes are off. CPhysicsPart::SetTranslucency acclient.c:315488 writes the material alpha via CopyMaterial + CMaterial::SetTranslucencySimple.
finding.proposed_change: Add one helper to materials.js, e.g. `applyFadedAlphaState(mat)` / `restoreAuthoredAlphaState(mat)`. On the first fade it snapshots the authored `{alphaTest, blending, blendSrc, blendDst, transparent, depthWrite}` into `userData.__authoredAlpha`. While faded it sets `alphaTest = 0`, forces `blending = NormalBlending` when the authored state was opaque or alpha-tested (this covers the `?clipMapOpaque=off` ONE/INVSRCALPHA arm), and sets `transparent = true` and `depthWrite = false`. Call it from the four owners (entities.js _applyObjectTranslucencyToEntity, setLocalPlayerCameraOpacity, _applyRampValueToMaterial, _applyEtherealToEntity) whenever their factor is below 1. three bumps material.version itself when alphaTest crosses 0, so the USE_ALPHATEST program swap happens once per fade, not every frame. Ship it default-ON with a `?fadeAlphaParity=off` escape. Add a node test: a clip-map material faded to opacity 0.5 must end with alphaTest 0 and its authored ref restored afterwards.

implementation.deviations:
1. Where the snapshot is taken. I take it in each owner just before its first write, and in `_applyMaterialRamp` for the Transparent hook path, instead of inside `_getOrCloneEntityMaterial`. Two reasons:
   - tests/luminous_night_clone.test.mjs and tests/luminous_hook.test.mjs splice the bodies of `_getOrCloneEntityMaterial` and `_applyRampValueToMaterial` into a `new Function` that only has fixed identifiers in scope. A new imported call inside either body would throw a ReferenceError in those unedited tests.
   - `_tickMaterialHooks` changes materials without going through the getter.
   For the same reason, the hook's snapshot and sync live in a new `_applyMaterialRamp(hookType, mat, value)` wrapper. Its three call sites (spawn tween plus the two tick calls) replace the direct `_applyRampValueToMaterial` calls.
2. Record lifetime. The record is dropped once the material is no longer faded and is taken again at the next fade, instead of being kept forever. If it were kept, any in-place change to the authored state between fades would later be overwritten by a stale snapshot. Examples: weapon_fx `_copyAll` adopting a new cache base after the grey fallback, or a texture re-seat. As a further guard, the restore only puts alphaTest and blending back if they still hold the values the fade wrote.
3. The old `transparent = opacity < 1.0` and `flooredValue > 0` writes are kept, not deleted. `syncFadeAlpha` runs after them and overrides them. This keeps `?fadeAlphaParity=off` byte-identical to the old path.
4. The snapshot holds {opacity, transparent, depthWrite, alphaTest, blending}. I left out blendSrc, blendDst and blendEquation because a fade never writes them (NormalBlending ignores them). Restoring `blending` alone brings back the CustomBlending arm, which test 2c checks. Opacity is not restored either: it stays composed by the owners, as both verifiers required.
5. The verifier's aside that "CustomBlending ONE/INVSRCALPHA under ?clipMapOpaque=off keeps its factors" contradicts both its own condition (`alphaTest > 0 || !transparent`) and retail. That arm is the ClipMap arm. Retail sets singlePassDetailinga = 1 there and then takes the has_alpha branch, which forces 5/6 (acclient.c:454495-454540). I implemented the retail behaviour: NormalBlending while faded, original factors restored afterwards.

finding.title: Fade restore paths recompute `transparent` from opacity, so Alpha/Translucent(T=0) surfaces turn opaque after a fade cycle (every first-person toggle)
finding.description: When a fade ends, holtburger re-derives the blend flag from the opacity value instead of restoring the authored state. finding.title: Per-entity clones of luminous materials drop out of the lumNight registry and freeze their glow at clone time
finding.description: `?lumNight` (default ON, full-night scale 0.25) dims ambient-like Surface luminosity at night by rewriting `emissiveIntensity` on every tracked material. Only the cache-owned material is registered. `_getOrCloneEntityMaterial` clones it whenever an entity needs a private material: object translucency, Transparent/Luminous/Diffuse hooks, TextureVelocity scroll, camera fade, or a weaponFx-owned material. three's Material.copy JSON-copies userData, so the clone carries `hbLumBase`. registerLuminousMaterial therefore refuses it (`if (mat.userData.hbLumBase !== undefined) return false;`), and it is never added to `_refs`. A luminous item or creature cloned at noon glows at full strength all night (4x its untouched peers); one cloned at night stays dim through the day.

finding.title: The three surface-flag ladders diverge from SetSurface on combined bits (ClipMap+Alpha/Additive, Translucent+Alpha+Additive, pure Additive)
finding.description: Holtburger decodes the Surface type with an if/else ladder that takes the first matching arm. It is copied three times (the materials.js legacy cache path, the flag-off unified decoder, and the entities.js recoloured path, which they note have drifted before). Retail SetSurface composes the bits instead, and holtburger differs in four ways. finding.title: Luminous(8/9) hooks overwrite a surface's own luminosity, but retail always draws a luminous surface with its own glow
finding.description: In retail a part's material emissive (set by SetLuminosity hooks, or by SetLighting for selection) applies only to surfaces whose own `luminosity` is 0. RenderMeshSubset swaps the SURFACE luminosity into the material's Emissive for each draw of a luminous surface and restores it afterwards. Holtburger's ramp writes `emissive = value` and `emissiveIntensity = 1.0` on every entity surface. A Luminous hook ramping to 0 on an object with base-luminous surfaces (crystals, gems, glowing trim) therefore turns their glow off, and a ramp to 1 over-brightens a 0.3-luminosity surface. Retail keeps both exactly as authored. The same rule is needed by the selection blink (lighting-materials-6) and avoids the lumNight conflict in lighting-materials-3.

URL: the usual 1070 dev URL plus `&selectionFlash=on&nosw=1`. Run it off-screen or headless on :9333 per the runbook. Each check is listed with what to look for:
(1) Left-click a textured NPC or monster. It should go to texel fullbright at once, not wash to white. Then dim at about 0.2 s, bright at 0.4 s, dim at 0.6 s, and look normal again at 0.8 s.
(2) Double-click a door or NPC. The flash restarts.
(3) Tab or keyboard target cycling, and a Rynth SelectObject. There must be NO flash.
(4) Click a creature or player holding a weapon. The weapon must not flash, and glowing gems or crystals keep their glow.
(5) Click a target, then sweep the mouse off it at once. The flash should end immediately (retail cancels on a mouse-over re-find of something else).
(6) Drag an inventory item onto an NPC. The NPC flashes, but the selection or target bar does not change because of the drop.
(7) After a flash ends, compare the clicked object in shade against its neighbours. A brighter-in-shadow look afterwards is the pre-existing `_getOrCloneEntityMaterial` clone dropping the CSM patch (see follow-ups), not the flash itself.
(8) The first click on a new kind of object may skip a frame while the async link guard compiles the emissiveMap variant. Any multi-second vanish or freeze is a fail.
(9) Bare URL without the flag: confirm nothing flashes.
implementation.deviations:
- Flag name `selectionFlash` with an exact `=on` opt-in, per the orchestrator. The verifier proposed `?selectionLight`.
- The snapshot lives in a module WeakMap, not in `userData.__preSelLight`. three's Material.copy JSON-copies userData, and an emissiveMap Texture stored there would be serialised. luminous_hook.js uses a WeakMap for the same reason.
- There is no separate `Use` call in the double-click branches. The second press of a double-click passes through the same picking.js point as the Select call, and that call re-lights and re-arms the flash. Retail's sr_Use find does exactly the same thing (same SetLighting(0.99, 1.0), flip count 1, +0.2 s), so the visible result is the same.
- Added retail's cancel: a MouseOver find of a different object, or of nothing, restores the blinking object (RecvNotice_SmartBoxObjectFound restores whenever the found id changes while m_cFlipCount is non-zero). A click on empty space and a drop on nothing do the same. The verifier's "MouseOver does nothing" still holds for the idle state and for the same object.
- LOW uses a linear 0.35 × the authored colour, the codebase's convention for the Diffuse hook and the Surface diffuse tint. WebAC converts it gamma to linear (about 0.1).
- Untextured surfaces use HIGH emissive = their own colour × 0.99, since there is no map to modulate.

1. `_getOrCloneEntityMaterial` (entities.js) clones with a plain `.clone()`. 4. The mouse-over re-find runs on pointermove (throttled to 50 ms). Retail re-finds every frame, so a target that walks out from under a still cursor keeps blinking here.
5. The restore puts back the pre-flash state. Retail RestoreLighting resets to the GfxObj defaults. If a Diffuse or Luminous hook tween finishes during the 0.8 s flash, the restore overwrites its final value.
6. A claimed dying rig stands in for its corpse guid (pick instByRoot), but the flash lights `entityMap.get(corpseGuid)`. During the handoff it may light the hidden corpse rig, not the drawn one.

finding.description: Retail draws a second, high-frequency detail pass over building shells (DrawBuilding) and env-cell walls (DrawEnvCell), using the REGION's detail surfaces at terrain_desc index 1 (building) and 2 (environment). In the EoL region both are 0x05001787 at tiling 4, so detail UV = 4 x base UV. Holtburger's object detail patch only runs when the Surface Detail bit is set, which happens on 0 retail surfaces, or under `?forceDetail` with procedural category tiles. It rides the building floor-bias and EnvCell baked-light material variants (one program per kind, shared uniforms). New wasm export `fetchRegionDetailSurfaces`; a pkg without it leaves the pass off. Cost while on: patched building surfaces skip the statics atlas and the draw pools, so building draw calls go up. Not applied under `?buildingFloorBias=off` or `?vertexBake=off`. Exact opt-in: only `=on` (case-insensitive) enables it. | Holtburg: stand within ~10 m of a cottage wall and the Town Network/meeting-hall interior, then a dungeon corridor; A/B against the bare URL | ON: a fine, high-frequency grain on walls, floors and ceilings (about ±5 %), with no overall tint or brightness shift and no seams, black or white surfaces, NaN sparkles or z-fight changes. Props and furniture inside cells, statics and terrain look identical to OFF. Console shows no `[materials] fetchRegionDetailSurfaces failed`. FPS drop at most a few percent. OFF: pixel-identical to the pre-change client. |
implementation.eye_test: Do this after the wasm rebuild, on the 1070 off-screen via CDP. A: `index.html?nosw=1`. B: `index.html?nosw=1&envDetailTex=on`. In B, check in the console that `liveScene3d.materialCache.envDetailOn === true` and that there is no `fetchRegionDetailSurfaces failed` warning. Compare A and B close-ups (5-10 m) of a Holtburg cottage exterior wall, a building interior (EnvCell), and a dungeon corridor (`@telepoi` to any dungeon). Pass: B shows a subtle high-frequency grain on shell and cell walls, floors and ceilings, with the same average brightness and colour as A. Props and furniture inside cells, outdoor statics, trees and terrain are unchanged. There are no black or white surfaces, seams, sparkles or flicker. The draw-call or FPS delta is acceptable, since building shells are unbatched under the flag. Also confirm the grain does not read as noise against BC7, normal-map or POM surfaces; the verifier flagged this as the main quality risk.
implementation.deviations: 1) Variant strategy: the verifier asked for separate per-kind variant clones. Instead, the patch is installed in place on the existing per-surface building floor-bias clone (getCachedFloorBias, whose only caller is buildings.js) and the EnvCell baked-light clone (getCachedCellBaked, whose only caller is cells.js). This goes through MaterialCache.applyEnvDetail, called only from buildings.js and cells.js. It reuses those maps' re-seat, re-point, evict and dispose lifecycle instead of adding a new variant map at five lifecycle sites. The trade-off: the shared base material is used under `?buildingFloorBias=off`, under `?vertexBake=off`, and with a pkg that lacks the baked-light attribute, so those arms get no detail. 2) Fold math: the verifier's `outgoing *= 1 + detail.rgb*Lapprox - detail.a` is kept, but the factor is formed in gamma space, as retail blended in gamma. L is recovered as clamp(outgoing/albedo)^(1/2.2) and applied as f^2.2 to linear light. The node test checks this against the retail blend equation to within 1e-6. 3) Atlas and pools: these were not in the verifier's plan but are required, because the statics atlas (`?buildingBatch`, default on) and the draw pools swap in bucket materials that would drop the patch. Patched building surfaces therefore skip pools and atlas, and patched cells are not offered to the pools. 4) Export shape: instead of `{gid, tiling, rgba}` per kind, the export returns the unique decoded textures (takeTextures) plus per-kind slice, tiling and GID, so the shared 0x05001787 is decoded once. 5) The verifier's optional tie to the high quality presets was not done. 6) The Rust test builds synthetic TMTerrainDesc lists rather than a whole Region struct; the list-index semantics are pinned with out-of-order terrain_type values.
implementation.follow_ups:
- Before any default flip, the atlas would need a detail-aware building bucket family, or a detail patch on the bucket material. Without it the flag disables building batching for patched shells.
- The `?buildingFloorBias=off`, `?vertexBake=off` and `?drawPools` arms get no detail or stay legacy. Decide whether that is acceptable.
- Optionally tie the pass to the high/ultra quality presets, mirroring retail presets 4-5 (Render::SetOverallGraphicsQuality).
- The detail GID and tiling (0x05001787, tiling 4) come from WebAC and the old fixture; they were not checked against DAT bytes. The JS reads the live Region, so this only affects the expectation in the docs.
- Existing issue found while doing this, needs separate verification: the floor-bias, cell-baked and static-bias clones come from `base.clone()`. three r184's Material.copy drops onBeforeCompile but keeps userData, so these clones keep the base's csmEnabled/pomEnabled/lightClampRetail flags in their program key without carrying those patches. Building shells and EnvCell walls may therefore render without CSM/POM/lightClamp (makeOwnedVariant documents the same class of problem).
- Two failures seen in other suites are not caused by this change: harness/test_build_shell.mjs (app modulepreload count) and test_f7_8_surface_bitfield.mjs M3b (from lighting-materials-4's additive fog default).

finding.title: The Setup light 'key' is LIGHTINFO.type, not a part index; retail lights ride the OBJECT frame (lights are parented to parts, and keys >= 1 drop on fused statics)
finding.description: Holtburger (following DRW/ACE's Dictionary<int, LightInfo>) treats the int before each Setup LightInfo as the part the light is 'rigidly attached to'. The retail decomp shows it is read into LIGHTINFO+0, which the PDB names `type`: 0 is point, 1 directional, 2 spot. Retail dispatches on it in the static vertex bake and in config_hardware_light, and positions every light at Frame::combine(OBJECT frame, LightInfo.offset). Retail sets the object frame through CPartArray::SetFrame → LIGHTLIST::set_frame, with no part transform and no object scale involved. Consequences in holtburger: (a) entity Setup lights are parented to `inst.parts[key]`, so they ride the animated part-0 or part-N frame and the rig scale; (b) on fused statics only a 'part 0' entry exists, so any light with key >= 1 is silently dropped (lighting.js 'No matching part ... Drop'); (c) vertex_bake.rs approximates the type with a cone_angle > 0 proxy even though the real type is parsed, as the HashMap key. ACE's Dictionary.Add means keys are unique per Setup, so multi-light Setups would carry keys 0, 1, 2. Whether any exist is unverified, and a census is needed before acting.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/effects/ObjectLights.ts:21-24: 'The lights follow the OBJECT frame, not a part (CPartArray::SetFrame @ 00519310 → LIGHTLIST::set_frame @ 00517c60), and are placed at Frame::combine(object frame, LightInfo.offset) ... the object's scale does not enter.' Lines 85-120: ObjectLightCarrier copies the owner's world matrix.
finding.holtburger_evidence: crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/setup_model.rs:446-447 `let key = i32::read_le(reader)?; lights.insert(key, LightInfo::read_le(reader)?);`. apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:17222-17254 'The key (the HashMap's i32) IS the Setup part index the light is attached to'. scene3d/entities.js:13347-13376 `const partGroup = inst.parts[targetPartIndex]; ... partGroup.add(light);`. scene3d/lighting.js:2760-2768 matches lights to `partIndex` and at 2843-2848 drops a light with no matching part; fused statics register only `partIndex: 0` (2609, 2695). lib.rs:23023-23031 vertex bake uses `sl.cone_angle > 0.0` as the type proxy.
finding.decomp_evidence: acclient.c:336056-336058 CSetup::UnPack light loop: `*(_DWORD *)v82 = *(_DWORD *)*v4; ... Frame::UnPack((Frame *)(v82 + 4) ...); RGBColor::UnPack(v82 + 80) ...` into the 104-byte LIGHTINFO {int type; Frame offset; ...} (acclient.h:31688-31697). acclient.c:326766 CPartArray::SetFrame → `LIGHTLIST::set_frame(v3, frame)` (325029) copies the object frame into each lightobj.global_offset. Line 346873 `Render::add_static_light(v3->lightinfo, ..., &v3->global_offset)`. Lines 454985-455003 static bake: `if ( local_light_info.type ) { if ( type == 1 ) directional } else calc_point_light`.
finding.proposed_change: Before changing anything, have the orchestrator census client_portal.dat Setups: the count with more than one light and the distribution of the leading int. If every key is 0, the only fix is (a): parent entity and building Setup lights to the object root, or to a carrier that copies the root's world matrix without scale, as WebAC's ObjectLightCarrier does, instead of `inst.parts[key]`. If keys of 1 or more exist, also rename `SetupLight.part_index` to `light_type`, stop dropping those lights in lighting.js, and let vertex_bake.rs dispatch on the real type (0 point, 1 directional, otherwise no static contribution) instead of the cone_angle proxy.

verification.reasoning:
Decomp, verified:
- CSetup::UnPack's light loop (acclient.c:336049-336066) reads the leading int into LIGHTINFO+0, then Frame at +4, RGBColor at +80 and floats at +92/+96/+100. The struct is 104 bytes. acclient.h:31688-31697 names +0 `int type`.
- The static bake (454985-455003) dispatches `if (type) { if (type == 1) directional } else calc_point_light`.
- CPartArray::SetFrame (found by symbol) calls LIGHTLIST::set_frame(frame) (325029), which copies the OBJECT frame into each lightobj.global_offset.
So the decomp contradicts holtburger's reading of the key as 'part index'.

Holtburger, verified:
- setup_model.rs:442-447 parses the int as a HashMap key.
- entities.js:13347-13353 parents the light to `inst.parts[sl.partIndex]` and skips it when the part is missing.
- lighting.js:2760-2768 matches lights by partIndex. Fused statics register only partIndex 0 (2609, 2646, 2695), so key >= 1 lights are dropped (2843-2848).
- The vertex bake uses a cone_angle proxy.

Citation fixes: SetupLight and its doc are at lib.rs:17569-17590, and the proxy is at lib.rs:23866-23880, not 17222-17254 / 23023-23031.

What stays unproven:
- The real impact needs a census. ACE's UnpackableExtensions.cs:212-222 uses Dictionary.Add, so keys are unique per Setup, and holtburger's HashMap::insert would silently overwrite duplicates.
- lib.rs:23874 notes all 285 venue lights are point lights.
- WebAC itself still parses the int as a map key (dat-parser SetupModel.ts:193-198); its evidence is only the object-frame attachment.

For key = 0 lights the visible difference is part-0 frame/animation and rig scale versus the object frame. That is likely small.
verification.corrected_change:

- If every key is 0: change only the parenting. Attach entity and building Setup lights to the object root, or to a carrier that copies the root's world position and rotation without scale (as WebAC's ObjectLightCarrier does), instead of `inst.parts[key]`.
- If keys >= 1 exist: also rename `SetupLight.part_index` to `light_type`, stop dropping those lights in lighting.js, and make the vertex_bake dispatch on type (0 point, 1 directional, else no static contribution) instead of the cone_angle proxy. Consider replacing the HashMap with a Vec so duplicate keys are not lost.

finding.title: Scenery frequency gate ignores the object index: every ObjectDesc in a Scene is gated by the same noise value (retail uses cellMat*(23399+j))
finding.description: Retail draws an independent noise value for each ObjectDesc j in a Scene. holtburger's bake reuses the j=0 value for every object, so the objects in a scene appear or vanish together instead of independently. Which trees, rocks and bushes exist differs from retail wherever freq < 1 and j > 0. In the end-of-retail Scene census (/mnt/wbterminal2/buildbox-2026-07-27/census/scenes.json: 179 scenes, 990 non-weenie rows), 821 rows have j > 0 and 551 of those have freq < 1, so their gate is wrong. In the shipped bake, 83% of a 14.9k-placement sample (every 60th LB file) has source_obj_idx > 0. The same wrong set feeds the client's scenery colliders (USE_SCENERY_COLLISION = true). The live ACE server builds its physics scenery with the correct formula, so client collision and server physics disagree about where trees stand (monster and missile collisions, for example). This re-raises a deliberate decision with NEW evidence. The bake's doc calls the missing index a 'deliberate retail bug' and 'the contract the client and server both depend on' (scenery-cross-check.rs:6-11). The decomp shows the index term exists. ACE's own Entity/Landblock.cs:197 comments out the only caller of the ported code (`//LoadMeshes(objects);`), and :334 says 'This isn't used by ACE'. The 'decomp-pinned' golden test copies the dead ACE formula, so it cannot catch this.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/terrain/SceneryGenerator.ts:324-331 computes per-object noise with the index: `const innerJ = (Math.imul(Math.imul(globalCellX, globalCellY) | 0, 1360117743) + 1888038839) | 0; const objHash = Math.imul((23399 + j) | 0, innerJ) | 0; const noiseRaw = ((cellXMat + cellYMat - objHash) | 0) >>> 0; ... if (noise >= obj.freq) continue;`
finding.holtburger_evidence: crates/holtburger-scenery-bake/src/lib.rs:505 `let (cell_x_mat, cell_y_mat, cell_mat) = cell_mats_per_object(...)`; :512 `let noise = object_noise(cell_x_mat, cell_y_mat, cell_mat);` (j is never passed); :515 is the gate. noise.rs:88-93 `cell_x_mat.wrapping_add(cell_y_mat).wrapping_sub(cell_mat.wrapping_mul(23_399))`. tests/golden_decomp.rs:104-106 `decomp_object_noise` uses the same j-less formula and calls it decomp-derived. apps/holtburger-tools/src/bin/scenery-cross-check.rs:6-11 describes 'the `23399` frequency multiplier with no object-index term' as a deliberate retail bug. dist/scenery/bake-source.sha256 contains `bake-mode	ace-compat`. These placements also feed the colliders (apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs ~20540-20700, populate_scenery_colliders_for_landblock_impl; holtburger-core system.rs:1785 `const USE_SCENERY_COLLISION: bool = true;`).
finding.decomp_evidence: CLandBlock::get_land_scenes, acclient.c:352530. At :352662 `v17 = 23399 * v38;` (v38 = 1360117743*x*y + 1888038839). At :352668 `obj_id.id = v16 + v44 - v17;`, which is the gate compared against freq. At the loop tail, :352729 `v17 = v38 + scene_id;` and :352731 `scene_id += v38;`, so object j uses cellMat*(23399+j). ACE's live physics agrees: ~/ace-server/Source/ACE.Server/Physics/Common/Landblock.cs:226 `cellMat * (23399 + j)`, and :36 `UseSceneFiles = true`. The ported code is dead in ACE: ~/ace-server/Source/ACE.Server/Entity/Scenery.cs:59 has the j-less form, but Entity/Landblock.cs:197 `//LoadMeshes(objects);` and :334 'This isn't used by ACE'.
finding.proposed_change: Add `BakeMode::Retail` in crates/holtburger-scenery-bake/src/lib.rs. Pass j into the noise: `cell_x_mat + cell_y_mat - cell_mat * (23399 + j)`, all u32 wrapping, or mirror the decomp's running accumulator. Make it the scenery-bake CLI default (apps/holtburger-tools/src/bin/scenery-bake.rs `--mode`) and keep `ace-compat` selectable. Fix the oracle: decomp_object_noise in tests/golden_decomp.rs must take j, with new golden values computed by hand from acclient.c:352662-352731. These tests are not Rynth tests, so editing them is allowed. Rewrite the scenery-cross-check doc so the 'expected divergence' classes are no longer called retail behaviour. Ship it together with terrain-scenery-2/3/4 in ONE re-bake: orchestrator only, capped-build, then `scripts/dist_ssd.py stage --activate`. Client code is unchanged: it reads the JSONL, and the per-LB placements-hash sidecars regenerate. Re-extract the rynthnav geom files (src="scenery") afterwards so nav obstacles match. That is a data refresh only; no Rynth code changes.

verification.reasoning:

finding.title: Scenery frame orientation: yaw sign mirrored vs retail Frame::set_heading, BaseLoc orientation discarded, ObjAlign (align != 0) not implemented
finding.description: Retail builds each scenery frame in one of two ways. GetObjFrame copies BaseLoc (orientation included), and only when max_rot > 0 calls Frame::set_heading(noise*max_rot). set_heading is a compass heading (clockwise): euler_set_rotate(asin(fwd.z), 0, -heading), and it keeps the base's forward-axis pitch. With align != 0, ObjAlign instead uses set_heading(get_heading(-N)) of the walkable plane. holtburger emits `(cos(r/2),0,0,sin(r/2))` with r = +noise*max_rot. That is the opposite rotation sense, because LandblockInfo statics render the DAT quaternion directly in the same AC z-up frame. Every rotated scenery instance therefore faces the mirror of its retail heading. For the 211 of 990 census rows with a partial range (0 < max_rot < 359, e.g. 7-85 degrees), the whole range lands on the wrong side of the authored base. Rows with max_rot == 0 and a non-identity base (4) get identity, the 8 pitch/roll rows lose their tilt, and the 32 align rows do not face down-slope. Partly re-raised: W1b/W1c (3d-render-completeness-wave-3-2026-05-29.md:14) were deferred as LOW on the 0.69% pitch figure. The NEW evidence is the sign mirror, which affects every rotated placement, and WebAC brings a ready, decomp-matching set_heading port. Collision note: retail-faithful frames stay yaw-only except for the 8 pitched rows, so cylsphere_to_world's yaw-only assumption still holds for 99%+ of rows.

verification.reasoning:
The decomp confirms the frame paths.

ObjectDesc::GetObjFrame (acclient.c:462660) copies base_loc, sets the origin, and only `if (max_rot > 0.0)` calls Frame::set_heading(noise*max_rot).

ObjectDesc::ObjAlign (:462708) copies base_loc and calls set_heading(get_heading(-plane->N)). The branch is selected by the align field at +100 (:352703-352706).

Frame::set_heading (:357692) builds direction (sin d, cos d, m_fl2gv[5]) and calls set_vector_heading (:357668) → euler_set_rotate(asin(z), 0, -fmod(450 - heading_angle, 360)). euler_set_rotate (:357589) is Shoemake's static-XYZ Eul_ToQuat. I checked it term by term: for x = y = 0 it yields q = (cos(z/2), 0, 0, sin(z/2)).

With the compass convention, set_heading(d) gives z = -d, so q = (cos(d/2), 0, 0, -sin(d/2)). ACE live agrees: AFrame.cs:179-216 set_heading → set_vector_heading uses Atan2(Y, X) with zRot = -(zDeg % 360), and Physics/Common/ObjectDesc.cs RotateObj/ObjAlign call frame.set_heading.

holtburger emits (cos(r/2), 0, 0, +sin(r/2)) (lib.rs:577-585, qx = qy = 0 at :630-631), copying dead ACE Scenery.cs `CreateFromYawPitchRoll(0, 0, +r)`. The scenery JSONL quaternion passes straight through (src/lib.rs:4444 `qz: rec.qz`) into the same statics.js:203-216 applyPlacementOrientation path that renders LandblockInfo DAT quaternions (frame_to_placement lib.rs:3730/3756 `qz: q.z`). So the rotation sense is mirrored relative to retail for every max_rot > 0 placement. obj.align is never read by the bake.

- Hex-Rays prints the arguments as `atan2(normalized.x, normalized.y)` (:357683) and `atan2(fwd.x, fwd.y)` in Frame::get_heading (:357410). A literal transcription gives yaw = d - 90°, which contradicts the '450 -' math-angle-to-compass formula and AC's heading-0 = north convention. The port must use atan2(y, x) as ACE and WebAC (SceneryGenerator.ts:49, :70) do, not 'transcribe from acclient.c' verbatim.

implementation.summary: BakeMode::Retail now gives each scenery object the frame retail builds for it. The bake follows acclient.c CLandBlock::get_land_scenes (:352703-352706). If align != 0 it uses ObjectDesc::ObjAlign, which calls set_heading(get_heading(-N)) with N the walkable triangle's normal, so the object faces up the slope. Otherwise it uses ObjectDesc::GetObjFrame: base_loc is copied whole, and only when max_rot > 0 does it call Frame::set_heading(noise*max_rot), with the heading in compass DEGREES. The new module src/orientation.rs ports Frame::set_heading, set_vector_heading, euler_set_rotate (Shoemake XYZs, order 0), set_rotate/IsValid, normalize_check_small and AC1Legacy::Vector3::get_heading. It uses atan2(y, x), as ACE AFrame does, not the swapped arguments Hex-Rays prints. noise.rs gains rotate_obj_retail, which returns degrees and has no DEG_TO_RAD factor. The bake now ships the full quaternion. qx/qy can be non-zero for pitched bases, and a heading d becomes (cos d/2, 0, 0, -sin d/2), the mirror of AceCompat. The within_block query and PlacementXform both receive that quaternion: PlacementXform gains qw..qz plus orientation(), and its rotation_rad is now the frame's yaw (yaw_about_z). aabb.rs adds transform_mesh_to_aabb3_quat, and the scenery-bake CLI uses it for --mode retail only. AceCompat and Strict are byte-identical: the same rotate_obj yaw, qx = qy = 0.0 and the same AABB call. No default, CLI default, dist or bake was changed, and nothing was compiled; Rust is left for the orchestrator.

implementation.deviations:
- **PlacementXform keeps rotation_rad.** The verifier said to pass the quaternion instead of rotation_rad. I kept the field and added qw/qx/qy/qz plus orientation(). That keeps AceCompat closures, and existing tests that read px.rotation_rad, bit-identical. Under Retail, rotation_rad is set to the frame's yaw (yaw_about_z) instead of ACE's mirrored RotateObj value, so a stale yaw-only closure still builds a correctly-turned box.
- **AABB uses the quaternion in Retail only.** The scenery-bake CLI uses transform_mesh_to_aabb3_quat for Retail and keeps transform_mesh_to_aabb3 for AceCompat/Strict.
- **Precision.** x87 intermediates are computed in f64 and narrowed to f32 wherever the decomp stores a float (the retail.rs convention); extended precision is not emulated.
- **No sign canonicalisation.** Retail's quaternion sign is kept as-is: headings in (180, 360) give qw < 0, which is the same rotation. The heading-0 test therefore asserts identity up to signed zero, and the other tests check the rotation (the forward axis) rather than raw components.
- **Pitch test.** It asserts the faithful pitch asin(fwd_z/sqrt(1+fwd_z²)), about 9.85° for a 10° base, not asin(fwd_z), because set_vector_heading normalises (sin d, cos d, fwd_z) before taking asin.
- **No WebAC code lifted.** Everything was re-derived from acclient.c and ACE AFrame.cs (WebAC only as a cross-check), so there is no attribution comment.
- **cylsphere_to_world doc not corrected.** It lives in holtburger-world, outside lane K; see follow_ups.
implementation.follow_ups:
- **cylsphere_to_world doc.** `crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/scenery.rs:142-148` wrongly says the bake always emits qx == qy == 0 and that retail builds the frame "from a Z rotation alone". The code already uses rotate_vector with the full quaternion, so only the doc needs fixing. Under Retail the 8 pitched rows are off by at most 2°.
- **ObjectDesc doc.** `crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/object_desc.rs`: max_rotation is documented as "(radians per ACE)" but it is DEGREES; ACE and retail convert it themselves. Its align/orient docs are vague: align selects ObjAlign.
- **golden_decomp.rs header.** It calls DEG_TO_RAD 0.017453303 a "decomp literal". Retail GetObjFrame has no DEG_TO_RAD (the degrees go straight to set_heading); that factor is ACE Scenery.cs's.
- **No A/B serving path yet.** The A/B needs a URL flag (or a dist-copy procedure) to serve a parallel Retail scenery dir. statics.js SCENERY_BASE_URL is hardcoded, and init_scenery_base_url has no URL-flag reader. This is a JS lane item.
- **Gate1.** scripts/gate1/diff-completeness.mjs scenery leg (verifier note 2): a Retail bake will diverge from the ACE C# probe by design, so either run that leg against `--mode ace-compat` or re-point it to Retail goldens.

finding.title: Every DayGroup reads as a storm: the weather scan treats the always-visible moon SetupModel (0x02000714 + PES 0x330007DB) as rain droplets
finding.description: scanWeatherSkyObjects marks a visible sky object as a 'droplet model' (is_storm=true, has_droplets=true) when it is any 0x02 SetupModel AND either its pesObjectId is non-zero OR it has props bit 0x08. Retail Region 0x13000000 puts the moon's physics-script proxy, SetupModel 0x02000714, in all 20 DayGroups. It has properties 0x00, begin_time==end_time==0 (the always-visible sentinel), and default_pes_object_id 0x330007DB. Holtburger's own code says so in three places: region.rs:1455 ("Sunny SkyObject[6] is 0x02000714 paired with default_pes_object_id 0x330007DB"), sky_dome.js:560 ("the only sky PES chains are the moon's 0x330007DB (in all 20 DayGroups") and docs/sky-i-probe-2026-05-11.md:268 (begin==end==0, so visible). sky.rs:1002 sets visible=true whenever begin==end, and :1092 passes the PES through. As a result weatherForState returns is_storm=true on Sunny and Clear days too. cloud_volume.js:401-404 then applies the storm cloud look (Cb tower, 10x ground haze) on every DayGroup under ?clouds=on, which is the owner's rig, and weather_state's wetness inputs see a permanent storm. The fog and weather-off paths only hide this: with weatherOff, loop.js forces is_storm=false. Retail defines a weather sky object purely by properties & 0x4. GameSky::MakeObject creates it only while LScape::weather_enabled, and GameSky::Draw gates it the same way. Holtburger's own dropWeatherSkyObjects already uses that bit (SKY_OBJ_WEATHER = 0x04). The Rainy objects all carry it: streaks 0x01004C42/44 have props 0x04/0x05, and the rain/lightning Setups 0x02000588/589/BA6 have props 0x0D. Round 2 treated is_storm as already correct ('is_storm already comes from real sky objects (W4)'), so this has not been reported before. I could not decode DAT bytes in this read-only phase. Confidence rests on the three consistent in-repo statements plus the decomp rule.

finding.proposed_change: In scene3d/daygroup_weather.js scanWeatherSkyObjects, decide weather by the retail bit only: `isWeather = (props & 0x04) !== 0`. Then set `is_storm = isWeather`, `has_droplets = isWeather && isSetupModel`, and `streak_gfx_id` = the first non-Setup weather gfx. Drop the `pesId !== 0` / SetupModel heuristic. Add a test case to tests/visual_options.test.mjs (or a new daygroup_weather test): `sky(0x00, 0x02000714, 0x330007DB)` alone gives is_storm false, and RAIN `sky(0x0d, 0x02000588, 0x33000428)` still gives true. Live check (orchestrator): on a Sunny day group, `__sessionHandle.getSkyObjectStates().map(o=>[o.gfxObjectId.toString(16),o.pesObjectId.toString(16),o.properties,o.visible])` should list 0x2000714 / 0x330007db / 0 / true, and is_storm should then read false.

verification.reasoning:
I re-read apps/holtburger-web/scene3d/daygroup_weather.js:144-153. The code is `isPhysicsBound = pesId !== 0 || (props & SKY_PROP_PHYSICS_SCRIPT) !== 0; isDropletModel = isSetupModel && isPhysicsBound; if (isWeatherStreak || isDropletModel) out.is_storm = true`. The moon proxy's data is confirmed by holtburger's own real-DAT note in scene3d/sky_glow.js:3-5: "moon SkyObject (Setup 0x02000714, PES 0x330007DB, properties 0, begin == end == 0) in ALL 20 DayGroups". sky_dome.js:560, region.rs:1455 and docs/sky-i-probe-2026-05-11.md:268 agree. crates/holtburger-world/src/sky.rs:1002 sets `always_visible = begin == end`, and :1010-1016 returns visible=true for it. :1092-1093 passes properties and pes through. pkg d.ts exposes pesObjectId, properties and visible.

So every DayGroup snapshot carries a visible Setup with pes != 0, and the scan returns is_storm=true every day. weatherForState (:196) then replaces the table value with that scan result.

The retail rule is confirmed in acclient.c. GameSky::MakeObject (:308434) has `if ( id.id && (!weather || LScape::weather_enabled) )`. GameSky::Draw (:308512) has `(LScape::weather_enabled || !(v8 & 4))`. Neither checks the PES or the Setup type. WebAC SkyboxRenderer.ts:678 (`isWeather = (props & 0x4) !== 0`) and :642 match, and :612-613 calls 0x2000714→0x330007db 'the always-on sky particle spawner'.

The code contradicts its own comment. daygroup_weather.js:107 says the droplet test is `props & 0x08`, but the code ORs in `pesId !== 0`, and that OR is what lets the moon in. sky.rs:94-97 wrongly says the props=0x00 objects, including 0x02000714, have 'No PhysicsScript'.

No test catches it. The fixtures in tests/visual_options.test.mjs:55-59 never include the moon.

The effects are wider than the comparer listed. Beyond cloud_volume.js:401-404 (storm look under ?clouds=on, which is opt-in), is_storm drives:
- weather_inputs.js:161-167: wetness, plus stormness=1.
- particle_env_gates.js:106/128: calm=0, which suppresses pollen and fireflies (both default-on via visualAll).
- terrainDustDevil.js:95: returns 0 during a storm.
- terrain_snow.js:328.

It is not a duplicate. round2-findings.json:407 explicitly treated is_storm as correct ('already comes from real sky objects (W4)'), and the scan file has no commits since W4 (git log).

implementation.summary: The storm scan (scene3d/daygroup_weather.js scanWeatherSkyObjects) counts any visible SetupModel with a non-zero pesObjectId as rain droplets. The moon proxy (Setup 0x02000714, PES 0x330007DB, props 0x00, begin == end == 0) is in all 20 retail DayGroups, so every DayGroup reads as a storm. I confirmed retail's rule in acclient.c: CreateDeletePhysicsObjects passes `props & 4` as MakeObject's `weather` argument, and MakeObject and Draw gate on that bit alone. Per the orchestrator, the retail rule is opt-in only, with `?stormScan=retail` (exact value).
