In retail mode, props & 0x04 alone makes a storm: a weather Setup sets has_droplets, and the first non-Setup weather object sets streak_gfx_id. The default legacy path is unchanged and still runs the same code, and weatherForState's signature is unchanged, so loop.js needs no edit. I also fixed the wrong comments. The daygroup_weather.js header now gives the retail rule and the bits GameSky actually reads, including that 0x08 only places weather objects in GameSky::UpdatePosition. In sky.rs, the props=0x00 entry no longer says 'No PhysicsScript' (the moon proxy carries PES 0x330007DB), and the bit 0x04 and 0x08 doc comments now cite the retail readers. finding.title: AdminEnvirons fog override is incomplete and partly wrong: BlackFog is grey instead of black, wrong fog start, no ambient override, no ~20 s fade-in, sky not fogged
finding.description: Holtburger maps EnvironChange 1-6 to a fog colour and fogMax and applies them instantly with near = 0.1*far. Retail CPlayerSystem::Handle_Admin__Environs differs in five ways. (a) BlackFog/BlackFog2 (5/6): the fog colour is 0x64000000 = BLACK, and 0x969696 is the AMBIENT colour, so holtburger renders 'BlackFog' as a grey fog. (b) Every option sets m_override_fog_min = 0 (holtburger uses far*0.1). (c) Every option also sets an ambient override that REPLACES the landscape ambient: Red 0x960000@0.4, Blue 0x320096@0.3, White 0x646464@0.4, Green 0x1E6400@0.3, Black 0x969696@0.8. Under BlackFog retail lights the world bright grey inside black fog. Holtburger has no ambient change. (d) LScape::UseTime blends the day fog and ambient toward the override by m_override_transition, which starts at 0 and gains +0.04 on every fog tick (0.8 s) and every light tick. The admin fog therefore rolls in over about 20 s, and Clear snaps back. Holtburger snaps on and off. (e) GameSky::Draw enables fog on the sky pass while m_override_enabled, so the sky turns the fog colour (additive sun/moon glows excepted) and before-sky cloud bands (props&2) are hidden. In holtburger a bright takram sky stays above a 50 m red fog wall. Round 2 dismissed AdminEnvirons as 'already handled' and only shipped the radar blank. finding.title: Distance fog uses plane depth instead of retail range (radial) fog, so the horizon-fog invariant fails at the screen sides; WebAC's global ShaderChunk patch removes the stated reason for not switching
finding.description: Retail sets D3DRS_RANGEFOGENABLE=TRUE with linear vertex fog, so fog is a function of eye-to-vertex distance. Holtburger's terrain fog tail, and three's stock <fog_vertex> used by statics/models, use view-plane depth -mvPos.z. holtburger documented this as a deliberate choice: 'matching three matters more than matching retail ... a corner-of-screen radial difference is not [visible]'. That difference is large under holtburger's own 2026-10-07 horizon fog. computeFogBand anchors near = 0.62*E and far = 0.95*E (E = drawn edge) to hide the streaming edge. The main camera has a 60 degree vertical FOV (index.js:1583), so at 16:9 the half-horizontal FOV is about 45.7 degrees. A terrain point at the drawn edge on the frame's side has view depth E*cos(45.7) = 0.698*E. That gives smoothstep((0.698-0.62)/0.33) = 0.14, so the edge is only about 14 % fogged where the design needs 100 %. For a square ring the same failure appears when facing a diagonal. Plane fog also shifts with camera yaw: distant trees gain and lose fog as you turn. Radial distance fixes both, and it is the retail metric. WebAC removes the consistency objection by patching THREE.ShaderChunk.fog_vertex once at startup, so every stock material becomes radial together. Holtburger only needs to give its two custom terrain shaders the same metric. Keep holtburger's smoothstep curve. Retail's linear curve (D3DFOG_LINEAR) can be a separate opt-in, because it changes the tuned ramp.

When the camera faces along an axis, every ray inside the 45.7° half-FOV hits the far face (plane depth = E, fully fogged) or the side face at plane depth ≥ 0.976E, so plane fog is essentially exact there.

The leak is real at off-axis yaws:
- Facing diagonally, the screen-side ray hits a side face at radial ≈E, plane depth 0.698E, which gives smoothstep ≈ 0.14.
- At 22.5° yaw it gives ≈ 0.35.
So the near-ring cutoff (statics/scenery end, LOD seam) shows at the frame sides for a large share of headings. The far ring to 8.5·192 m stays fogged even at the sides (plane 1139 m > 1003 m).

The 'consistency' objection in url-flags.md:1837 is answered by patching THREE.ShaderChunk.fog_vertex globally together with the two terrain shaders. That is a NEW argument made after the 2026-10-07 horizon fog landed, so re-raising this is legitimate. Takram aerial perspective is already distance-based, so radial fog would also agree with AP.

Two caveats. Radial distance is always ≥ plane depth, so it adds haze toward the frame sides at EVERY yaw. That changes the owner-tuned 0.62 'keep the mid-field forest in colour' look and may need horizonFogNear re-tuned. Default-ON without a 1070 eye-test is therefore premature. Retail's linear curve should stay a separate opt-in, as the comparer says.

finding.title: Retail single light tick is reset by LScape::SetDay; holtburger runs two independent 15 s ticks that are never reset, so toggling Always Daylight leaves noon sky over night-lit ground for up to 15 s
finding.description: Retail has one landscape light clock, LScape::next_light_tick. LScape::SetDay, called for the Always-Daylight option at login (OnInitialize), on every option change and by /day, zeroes next_tick AND next_light_tick, so the very next frame re-lights the landscape. Holtburger has two separate 15 s quantisers. One is the terrain Gouraud term (loop.js _acTerrainGouraud on performance.now). The other is the terrain pebbles (terrain_rock.js on frameCtx.tSec, seeded when the pool is built). Neither is reset when always_daylight.js pins or unpins the sky clock. So when the option toggles, the takram sky, sun and fog jump to Midsong at once while the ground Gouraud and pebbles keep the old night or day light for up to 15 s, and the reverse on unpin. The two ticks also have unrelated phases, so pebbles and the ground step at different moments. That contradicts terrain_rock.js's own comment that 'Pebbles step with the ground they sit on'. Retail steps the whole landscape together.

A single next_light_tick drives all landscape lighting (:1462-1470). Test: tests/verify-always-daylight.ts.

It is reset only by the devtools setters at :1347/:1352. scene3d/terrain_rock.js:986 `nextLightTick: -Infinity`, :999-1001 its own 15 s tick, :1290 driven by `frameCtx.tSec`, :1033 invalidateLight() has no callers. scene3d/always_daylight.js:66-85 pins/unpins via setSkyTimeOverride with no light-tick reset. index.html:6388 calls it per net pump.

finding.proposed_change: Export a tiny shared light-tick clock from loop.js, or a new scene3d/retail_light_tick.js: `{ due(nowSec), reset() }` using one nextLightTick on performance.now. Have tickTerrainSunDir and terrain_rock's _pushLight both consult it. The rock pool reuses the terrain epoch: re-push when `epoch` changed instead of keeping its own timer. Call reset() from always_daylight.js on each on/off EDGE (retail SetDay), from the /day handler if present, and on EnteredWorld. Node test: toggling the option produces a light push on the next tick, and terrain and rock epochs advance together.

holtburger has two independent 15 s quantisers:

implementation.summary: The landscape now has one retail light clock, matching LScape::next_light_tick (acclient.c:307222, 15 s). It lives in the new pure module scene3d/retail_light_tick.js. Both consumers use it: the terrain Gouraud term (loop.js tickTerrainSunDir) and the pebble field (terrain_rock.js). sync() returns the light epoch, and whichever consumer runs first in a frame advances it. finding.title: Sky evaluated twice in wasm per sky tick (getSkyState + getSkyObjectStates), with per-tick un-freed SkyObjectState wrappers
finding.description: Round 2 said per-frame sky evaluation was 'already consolidated to one call'. In fact two remain. SkyLightingController.tick calls getSkyState(), which runs the full evaluate_sky_now() (lighting plus every sky object, building a Vec) and throws the objects away. tickWeatherState then calls getSkyObjectStates(), which runs evaluate_sky_now() a second time and returns about 7 freshly allocated SkyObjectState wasm objects. JS never calls .free() on them, so they live in the wasm heap until FinalizationRegistry runs after a GC. Both run on every RP3 sky tick. The only consumer of the object array is the weather scan, which needs to change only on a DayGroup change or a sky-object visibility edge. Retail's split cadence (GetSky per frame; fog every tick_size 0.8 s; lighting every light_tick_size 15 s) shows how little of this needs per-frame work. The win is small, a few microseconds plus GC churn per tick, and it is cheap to take.

Fog and light evaluation run on the retail tick cadence: `if (this.nextTick <= this.tickClock) { this.nextTick = this.skyDesc.tickSize + this.tickClock; if (this.nextLightTick < this.tickClock) { this.lightTick(true); ...} this.fogTick(true); }`.

Each call to evaluate_sky_now (:21226) builds the full objects Vec. scene3d/sky_lighting.js:122 `state = session.getSkyState();`. scene3d/loop.js:1499-1501 `skyObjects = handle.getSkyObjectStates();` runs every sky tick with no free(). pkg/holtburger_web.js:13298 `SkyObjectStateFinalization.register(obj, ...)`.

implementation.summary:
I confirmed the finding against the current code. The weather tick (loop.js tickWeatherState) calls handle.getSkyObjectStates() on every RP3 sky tick, about 10 Hz. Each call returns about 7 fresh wasm SkyObjectState wrappers that nothing frees, so they wait for the FinalizationRegistry after a GC (pkg/holtburger_web.js:13298). sky_lighting.js already frees its getSkyState() result.

A new pure module, scene3d/sky_object_free.js, adds freeSkyObjectStates(list). It frees each wrapper once, skips entries that have no free method, and swallows a throwing free from an already-freed wrapper. It also adds an escape flag helper, skyObjectFreeEnabled, where ?skyObjFree=off, 0 or false turns freeing off; it is on by default.

tickWeatherState keeps its single getSkyObjectStates() call. It captures the original array as `fetched` before the weather-off filter, which builds a new array over the same wrappers. The rest of the body is wrapped in try/finally, and the finally frees `fetched` after the storm scan and both sky-dome hosts have run. All of those consumers read the fields synchronously and keep no wrapper; updateSkyParticleChains copies the pes id into a number before its async import.

getSkyState and getSkyObjectStates keep their exact names and shapes, so RynthSuite is unaffected. Nothing visible changes.

F4: the scan result survives the free. F5: flag. F6: source scan finds one getSkyObjectStates() call and the free in a finally after both hosts. F6b: getSkyState/getSkyObjectStates and the rynth webhost mapping are unchanged.
6/6 pass (V5 source-scans tickWeatherState and still finds every pinned string, in order, inside its 4000-char slice)
12 groups ok, 0 failed (imports scene3d/loop.js, so the new import resolves under node)
all 4 checks passed (safety check; no rynth-imported module was touched)

finding.title: PhysicsDesc DefaultScript is played at spawn — retail only stores it, so breath creatures and some weapons fire their attack effect the moment they appear
finding.description:
`?defaultScriptSpawn` is DEFAULT ON (the reader is `!== "off"`). For every non-projectile entity it resolves the wire PhysicsDesc default_script (a PScriptType plus intensity) through the object's PhysicsScriptTable and plays it on spawn. Retail's set_description only copies default_script and its intensity onto the CPhysicsObj. play_default_script has exactly three callers: DefaultScriptHook::Execute, DefaultScriptPartHook::Execute and ACCWeenieObject::DoCollision (ScriptedCollision missiles). At creation retail plays only the Setup's default_script_id, from InitDefaults.

The A11-S5 rationale in the code comment ("ACE-era content authors DefaultScript as the ambient spawn effect") is contradicted by the content. I censused every didStats key 30 (PropertyDataId.PhysicsScript) in the LSD dump, which is the property ACE sends as the PhysicsDesc DefaultScript, and none of the values is an ambient effect:
- 618 Creatures carry Breathe*: Olthoi Soldier 0x56, Rynthid Minion 0x57, Shuthis Moarsman 0x54, Emergent Rust Gromnus 0x55.
- 47 melee weapons, 14 bows and 2 orbs carry BreatheLightning (e.g. Tanae's Tewhate of the Forests, Renegade Bow).
- 11 'Enhanced Assault' weapons carry Create 0x58.
- 80 spell projectiles carry Destroy or ProjectileCollision.
- In addition, ACE House.cs:77 stamps RestrictionEffectBlue on every House object.

Retail PhysicsScriptTables do map these types (the canonical-table data lists Breathe 0x54-0x57 in 9 tables each and RestrictionEffect in 9). So in holtburger every breath creature puffs its breath as it streams in, and those weapons fire their lightning or create burst on spawn. Houses may also flash the blue restriction effect, but I could not verify whether house tables carry that entry.

There is a second consequence, which holtburger already documented and fixed for missiles only (PROJECTILE_DEFAULT_SCRIPT_SPAWN_SKIP): this arm races the Setup default_script arm for the single `_particleChainsAttached` slot. An object with a real Setup ambient script (a flame aura, for example) can lose it to a one-shot breath, depending on which async resolve lands first.

New evidence relative to the earlier rounds: the ledgers never questioned the spawn arm, and the LSD census disproves its premise. docs/url-flags.md:1251 also still says "Default OFF" for this flag.

I re-read the code and the finding holds. In holtburger, entities.js:2295-2306 defines DEFAULT_SCRIPT_SPAWN_ON as `!== "off"`, so it is default-ON. The spawn arm at entities.js:5768-5796 gates on `DEFAULT_SCRIPT_SPAWN_ON && pesId === 0 && !(PROJECTILE_DEFAULT_SCRIPT_SPAWN_SKIP_ON && inst._isProjectile === true) && !this._particleChainsAttached.has(guid)`, then calls `_resolveDefaultScriptDid` (entities.js:8143-8173), which does GetScript(raw PScriptType, intensity) through the entity's table, and plays the result at spawn.

The Setup-default arm (entities.js:5812-5845) is guarded by the same `_particleChainsAttached` check after its own async resolve. So whichever resolve lands first wins the slot, and the race is real.

The hook 17 and hook 18 fallbacks (entities.js:17660, 17726) are also gated on DEFAULT_SCRIPT_SPAWN_ON.

finding.title: DefaultScriptPart hook (18) plays the animating object's own default script at the part; retail plays the HELD child's default script on the child (weapon swing effects)
finding.description:
Retail `play_default_script(part_index)` walks the object's CHILDLIST and finds the child whose part_number == part_index, i.e. the wielded weapon, shield or orb mounted on that part. It resolves the CHILD's own default_script and intensity through the CHILD's PhysicsScriptTable and plays the result on the child. If nothing is held there, nothing plays.

holtburger (W4.7) treats part_index only as an anchor. It plays the wielder's own raw 0x33 physicsScriptDid, or the wielder's resolved PScriptType default, attached at that part.

The LSD census from finding 1 shows what this misses. 47 melee weapons, 14 bows and 2 orbs carry BreatheLightning as their PhysicsDesc default, and 11 'Enhanced Assault' weapons carry Create. That is the content model for a weapon effect the wielder's attack or draw animation triggers through hook 18. In holtburger those effects never fire on the swing: a player has no default script, so the hook resolves nothing. Because of finding 1 they fire once at spawn instead. The reverse also happens: a creature with a Breathe default whose motion uses hook 18 would breathe from a part where retail plays nothing.

How many animations carry hook 18 has not been measured, so a DAT census should come before flipping the default. The retail rule itself is unambiguous in the decomp, and WebAC implements and tests it.

finding.title: Interior (EnvCell) static default-script emitters ignore their cell's visibility; retail degrades out particles whose cell is not in view
finding.description:
In retail, ShouldDrawParticles is false when the emitter object's cell is null or not in view (cell->IsInView), not only when it is beyond degrade_distance. UpdateParticles then takes its degraded branch: nothing is drawn, persistent emitters freeze their particles' ages, and finite emitters record emissions without making them.

holtburger's interior braziers, torches and fountains are anchored directly in `staticsGroup`, which the code itself describes as "always visible". The interior items carry no cell id, and RP6 tests only frustum, the 220 m cap and the opt-in degrade radius. As a result every interior emitter in front of the camera and within 220 m keeps its full per-particle update and still writes instances, even when cells.js has hidden its cell container because the cell is outside the PVS/BFS visible set or was rejected by the occlusion culler. In dungeons and occluded building interiors that is wasted simulation and instance work; depth testing usually hides the result, but not always, for example through portal-punch gaps. The comment at statics.js:5031-5035 lists exactly this cell-container gate as a pending follow-up. WebAC gates static emitters on the anchor's effective visibility every frame.

The fix needs no new lifecycle code: RP6's culled path already implements retail's degraded semantics (PLIFECYCLE-2 freeze and virtual emission, thaw on re-entry).

finding.title: The instanced particle path still clones a full THREE.Material per particle slot just to carry one opacity float
finding.description:
Since 2026-10-06 instancing has been default ON for additive and alpha emitters in both managers. On that path the slot meshes are kept out of the scene graph and are read back only as transform and opacity carriers. meshFactory still gives EVERY slot its own material, though: either a pooled clone or `baseMaterial.clone()`. A three Material clone runs the constructor (new uuid, about 60 fields), copy(), and a JSON round-trip of userData. The clone exists only so particle.js setTranslucency can write `mesh.material.opacity`, which `_appendInstances` reads back. The clone is never rendered; the bucket uses its own material derived from `_instBaseMat`.

With lazy slots each emitter still pre-builds min(maxParticles, initial+6, at least 6) slots. The census quoted in particle_emitter.js counts 3,873 static emitters at Holtburg alone, so tens of thousands of Material objects (plus Mesh carriers) stay live to hold one float each. Every emitter creation, for example on each spell cast, pays that many clones. The per-slot material pool was added precisely because this churn caused the "sustained-combat cast stutter".

WebAC keeps per-particle state in typed arrays plus a pooled record and feeds opacity through an InstancedBufferAttribute, with no per-particle Object3D or Material. Its one-InstancedMesh-per-system draw layout is worse than holtburger's per-gfxobj buckets, so only the state layout is worth taking.

finding.holtburger_evidence: scene3d/particles/particle_manager.js:1653-1668: `const useInst = this._instancing && particleInstancingEnabled() && ...; onMeshActive: useInst ? _NOOP : undefined` ("keep slot meshes OUT of the scene graph (they stay pure transform/opacity carriers)"). :1679-1681, unconditional: `const mat = baseMaterial ? (this._takePooledMaterial(poolKey) || baseMaterial.clone()) : null;`. :2223: `const op = m.material?.opacity ?? 1;`. :316-319: "The per-slot meshes are still built and still driven by particle.js ... used purely as transform+opacity carriers". particle.js:156-167: setTranslucency writes `mesh.material.opacity`. particle_emitter.js:21-37: the 3,873-emitter census and SLOT_PREALLOC_MIN = 6. particle_manager.js:1836-1852: on instanced attach failure the code falls back to the per-mesh path.
finding.decomp_evidence: n/a (renderer efficiency; no retail counterpart)
finding.proposed_change:
1. When `useInst`, build slot meshes with the shared `baseMaterial`, which is never rendered while the slots are off-graph.
2. Carry opacity per slot instead of in the material. setTranslucency also writes `mesh.userData.__op`, or the Particle keeps `this.opacity`, and `_appendInstances` reads that value.
3. Clone lazily only if the bucket attach fails and the emitter falls back to the per-mesh path (the catch at :1844-1852): swap clones onto the existing slots there.
4. Make `_reclaimSlotMaterial`, `_forEachParticleMaterial` and the additive-fog switch skip the shared, cache-owned base.
5. Keep `?particleInstancing=off` byte-identical.

Measure JS heap and emitter-creation milliseconds during a cast storm before and after. A larger follow-up (effort L) would replace the Mesh carriers with per-emitter Float32Arrays, using WebAC's layout and keeping holtburger's bucket draws.

finding.title: Each newly emitted particle is drawn for one frame near the world origin: Particle.init's first update uses parentOffset (an ACE port bug)
finding.description:
particle.js:419-423 follows ACE Particle.cs:118 and runs the spawn-time update() with `parentOffset` (the hook's offset frame) as the parent frame. Retail Particle::Init ends with `Particle::Update(..., &this->start_frame)`.

emitParticle runs inside updateParticles, after the per-particle update loop, so the new mesh keeps that position for the current frame. The position is parentOffset.origin + offset in staticsGroup/entitiesGroup space, and that space is absolute AC world coordinates, so the particle sits near the map's SW corner, off screen. `_appendInstances` then writes it into the bucket at that spot. For the spin types (GR) the orientation is also taken from the offset frame.

The effects:
- Every particle shows up one frame late.
- Per-metre trails that emit one particle per frame, such as the cast-hand trail 0x32000109, are always missing their head segment.
- The ?fxMotion velocity estimator sees a kilometre-scale jump that particle_fx.js:1314 has to throw away.

At 60 fps this is subtle. At 15-30 fps on weaker hardware the trail head visibly lags the hand. WebAC recomputes every live particle, including the one just emitted, from its frame after emitting.

finding.title: Indoors, rigs in undrawn cells still render and can be clicked/hovered through walls
finding.description: Retail draws an object only through the cells the portal walk reached. PView::DrawCells ends by calling DrawObjCellForDummies for each cell_draw_list entry, which draws that cell's shadow parts, and mouse selection (Render::GfxObjUnderSelectionRay) runs only inside that draw. So a monster in a room no portal view reaches is neither drawn nor selectable. Holtburger's entity render cull is frustum + distance + GPU occlusion, but the occlusion culler is disarmed indoors, and nothing ties a rig to the cell-visibility set that drives the cell containers. In a dungeon or building interior this means: (a) every frustum-visible rig in neighbouring rooms behind solid walls is submitted, at about 40 part draws per humanoid; (b) picking only checks root.visible, so clicking or hovering a wall selects or tooltips the monster behind it, either through a polygon hit or through the generous selection-5 drawing-sphere fallback. WebAC fixed exactly this (DECOMP.interior-objects-culled).

DrawObjCellForDummies(cell_draw_list[i-1])`. 458143-458156 DrawObjCellForDummies -> DrawObjCell (the cell's CShadowParts, sorted). 379997-380023 Render::GfxObjUnderSelectionRay records hits only for the part currently being drawn (check_curr_object); it is called from the mesh draw path at 458247/458282, so undrawn objects cannot be selected.
finding.proposed_change: entities.js tickEntityRenderVisibility: when the viewer is indoors (scene3d._currentCellIndoor), AND `want` with 'the rig's cell is drawn this frame'. Store the full cell id in noteEntityLandcell (add `inst._wireCellId = cellId >>> 0`; keep _wireCellIdx for the seal). Hide a rig whose cell is an EnvCell (low16 >= 0x100) when that cell's container in scene3d.cellContainers3d is resident and has visible === false this frame. Retail draws an object in every cell its shadow overlaps, so keep the rig if its 6 m cull sphere touches the AABB of any visible cell (the cell AABB index already exists). Fail open for: unknown or stale cell, non-resident container, the local player, attached children, and light owners (the existing exemptions). Picking needs no change because it already skips !visible roots. Prefer the wasm physics cell per object if it can be exposed, which avoids the KIND_POSITION lag noted in PARITY-STATUS. Escape flag `?cellObjectCull=off`. Add a node test next to the FCULL tests with a hidden-container case. Measure draws/frame in a populated dungeon.

implementation.summary: Added an opt-in indoor cell check, `?rigCellGate=on`, to the entity render cull. Retail only draws, and only lets you select, objects in the cells its portal walk reached (PView::DrawCells → DrawObjCellForDummies, acclient.c:461450; Render::GfxObjUnderSelectionRay :379997). Our cull had no cell check and the occlusion culler is off indoors, so rigs in undrawn rooms were still drawn and could be clicked or hovered through walls. A new pure module, scene3d/rig_cell_gate.js, holds `rigCellHidden`. It hides a rig only when its cell's container is loaded and hidden this frame, or when the rig is in an outdoor landcell and the walk's outside-view count is exactly 0 (the area MISSED-2 clause, under the same flag). It also requires that the rig's 6 m cull sphere touches no AABB of a drawn EnvCell, because retail puts an object in every cell its sphere overlaps (CPhysicsObj::add_shadows_to_cells). Anything unknown leaves the rig drawn. tickEntityRenderVisibility applies the check after the frustum and distance tests, and only when `_currentCellIndoor && _indoorSplitArmed`. The existing exemptions (local player, attached children, light owners) are unchanged. Picking needed no change because it already skips hidden roots. The full cell id is now stored in cells.js noteEntityLandcell (`_wireCellId`) and at spawn (`_spawnCellId`). The wire cell takes priority over the spawn cell. With the flag on, tickPortalSeal publishes the walk's outside-view count before the punch clip. With the flag off nothing is written and nothing is gated, so the default path behaves exactly as before.

implementation.deviations:
1. Flag: per the orchestrator, this is an opt-in `?rigCellGate=on` (exact match), not the verifier's `?cellObjectCull=off` escape. The MISSED-2 outdoor-rig clause (the verifier's optional step 6) is implemented under the same flag.
2. The pure helper is in a new leaf module, scene3d/rig_cell_gate.js, instead of cells.js. This keeps entities.js from pulling in cells.js's 77-module import graph, which matters for node tests that import or splice entities.js. cells.js imports the leaf only for the flag.
3. `rigCellHidden` takes positional arguments (cellId, registry, drawnCellBoxes, center, radius, outsideViewCount) instead of an object, so the per-rig call allocates nothing, following the FCULL zero-allocation convention.
4. There is no JS cell AABB index; the finding's "already exists" only holds inside the wasm. Drawn-cell AABBs are measured from each container's scene graph (Box3.setFromObject brought back into the AC frame), cached per container and child count. The drawn set is `scene3d._lastCellVisibleSet`, re-checked against each container's live `.visible`. A drawn cell whose bounds cannot be measured leaves every rig drawn for that frame.
5. A registered but detached (warm-parked) container counts as not resident, so its rigs stay drawn. The particle cell gate does the opposite and treats it as hidden; rigs stay conservative, as the finding's fail-open list asks.
6. The outside-view count is the raw `getPViewOutsidePortals` count taken in tickPortalSeal before the punch near-plane/straddle clip, so a doorway the camera stands in still counts as an outside view. It is null (rigs stay drawn) when the seal pass is absent, the pkg is stale or something throws.
7. The cell check runs after the frustum and distance tests and before the occlusion check, which is disarmed indoors anyway.
8. Draws per frame were not measured, because browsers are not allowed for this lane; that is in eye_test.

(a) Merge the url-flags.md row. Until then, scripts/lint-url-flags.mjs reports rigCellGate as UNDOCUMENTED (it only fails under --strict).
(b) The verifier's 6 m sphere is very conservative: a rig is hidden only if it is more than 6 m from every drawn cell's AABB. Retail uses the object's own sphere for shadow cells, so a per-setup sorting sphere would let the check fire more often.
(c) Area MISSED-1: indoors, the drawn set is the portal walk plus the depth-1 BFS, so every neighbour room is always drawn and the check only removes rigs two or more portals away. Narrowing that union is a separate perf item that needs a doorway-straddle eye test.
(d) Area MISSED-3: retail clips each cell's objects to that cell's portal_view, so a rig in a drawn neighbour room is still pickable through the wall in front of it.
(e) With `?drawPools` (DEV), envcell surfaces move into pools, so a container may hold only props. Its measured box may then be too small, or empty, which leaves rigs drawn. An additive wasm `getCellAabb(cellId)` export (the AABBs already exist in the wasm scene) would give robust bounds.
(f) The finding also suggests using the wasm physics cell per object instead of the lagging KIND_POSITION cell. The sphere-overlap test absorbs most of that lag for now.
(g) Not checked: what the selection brackets / target indicator do when the currently selected rig becomes hidden by this check. Nameplates are children of the rig root, so they hide with it.

finding.title: Indoors, sky and landscape draw every frame even when the walk reaches no outside portal
finding.description: Retail draws the sky and landscape from inside a cell only when the portal walk produced a visible outside portal. LScape::draw (= GameSky::Draw + the landscape blocks + weather) and the Z-wipe both sit inside PView::DrawCells' `if (this->outside_view.view_count)`. Holtburger already computes exactly that set in wasm (getPViewOutsidePortals), but uses it only to feed the doorway seal. The indoor world pass is instead gated by static per-cell tests: the sky by the viewer cell's SeenOutside bit, and terrain/buildings/statics by 'this dungeon's landblock has any outdoor portal'. So in any room of a town building with no door or window in view, and anywhere inside a dungeon that has a mouth, holtburger draws the full terrain + other-landblock buildings + sky pass, then wipes depth and overdraws it with the room. That pass is pure submission cost. It also means any crack in the cell geometry shows terrain or sky where retail shows the cleared background. Not in the duplicate ledgers.

WebAC itself applies this per sealed (non-SeenOutside) cell, which is the same static approximation holtburger uses for the sky.

In atmosphere_pipeline's armed-indoor branch, when the count is 0, disable worldMaskPass + depthClearPass and force skyBlocked (plus sky glow and horizon passes) for that frame; the layer-1 cells pass and room shell stay. Fail open (draw the world) in three cases: while the viewer's render-set cells are not all resident; for 2 frames after the count drops to 0; and when the camera is within ~1 m of an outdoor portal plane of its own cell, so a doorway straddling the near plane cannot black out. implementation.deviations:
1. BFS clause narrowed to cells in view. Only BFS-only drawn cells whose AABB is in the view frustum count (the same tick's `getRenderSetWithFrustum` set). The depth-1 BFS is the DAT-baked PVS (visible_cells edges, lib.rs ~26675), which in a town building includes the front room with the door. The verifier's literal clause would therefore keep the gate off in practically every building room, including the "Holtburg back room" it is meant to measure. A cell outside the frustum cannot put its doorway on screen. With no frustum set, every BFS-only cell is tested, as the verifier specified.

2. Stale-count handling. I accepted the one-frame staleness instead of moving the computation after cameraSwitcher.tick, because loop.js is not in this lane. The 2-tick zero rule only protects the transition into skipping. To cover a doorway turning into view during the stale frame, I added a second `getPViewOutsidePortals` walk through a frustum widened in clip x/y by 0.75. It runs only when the raw count is 0 and must also return 0. Widening is monotone: same near plane, larger initial view window.

3. Near-portal clause. It is measured as the distance from the camera to the vertex AABB of every outdoor portal of any cell within a 1.5 m box around the camera. The box is queried through the existing `getVisiblePortalApertures` export using an orthographic MVP. This is a superset of "the viewer cell's planes", needs no new wasm export, and the AABB distance never exceeds the true distance, so it errs toward drawing the world.

4. Empty layer mask. The skip uses layer mask 0 rather than "an unused layer", so no object passes `layers.test`, not even one with an all-layers mask. The world RenderPass is never disabled; it clears colour and depth because the sky pass is off. This is pinned by test L7, which renders through the real pipeline, and by L8.

5. Sky glow and haze. I did not touch sky_dome.js (outside this lane). Sky-glow particles are layer-0 world-pass objects, so the empty mask drops them, and their anchor is already hidden for any indoor viewer. Layered haze and fog keep reading sky_dome's own flag, so room geometry tinting does not flicker as the gate toggles.

6. Seal off on skip frames. On a skip frame the seal is forced off as a defensive measure; it has no apertures when the count is 0 anyway.
implementation.follow_ups:
- **Staleness:** move the gate tick (or tickPortalSeal) after cameraSwitcher.tick in loop.js. That removes the one-frame staleness and makes the wide second walk unnecessary.
- **Direct-render fallback:** the fallback in index.js (~2880) does its own indoor split and ignores the gate, so it fails open; it could honour `scene3d._indoorLandscapeGate.skip`.
- **Buildings are skipped too:** with the default-on `?statAtlas`/`?buildingBatch`, building shells are untagged cross-LB batches that stay on layer 0, so a skip frame does not draw them. Retail does the same (buildings are drawn inside LScape::draw), but the eye test must confirm rooms are complete from EnvCell geometry alone. The meeting-hall gap where cellContainers3d is empty is covered by the residency clause.
- **BFS union (area_missed_notes #1):** the drawn set is the walk plus the depth-1 BFS, which is the full DAT PVS. Narrowing it to the walk would also let the gate fire next to doorway rooms that are out of view.
- **Orchestrator merges:** the url-flags.md row and the harness row are in this report for the orchestrator to merge.

finding.title: Portal-space fades are retail FOV zooms, not a far-plane shrink + black overlay
finding.description: Retail's TUNNEL_FADEOUT and WORLD_FADEIN override the SmartBox view-plane distance: SetOverrideFovDistance (m_fViewDistFOV), whose default is 1/tan(fov/2). That value is consumed only as an FOV by Render::set_vdst -> SetFOVInternal, both in RenderNormalMode (the world) and in the tunnel's CreatureMode viewport (UseSmartboxFOV). Lerping it toward 0.001 widens the projection to almost 180°: the tunnel recedes to a point, and the world then zooms in from a point over 1 s, with no darkening. Holtburger's header calls it 'the tunnel's far plane (smartbox view distance)'. It shrinks the tunnel camera's far plane, so the tunnel stays intact and then pops to black near the end. It then fades the world in under a black quad, describing that as an approximation that avoids 'changing the main camera's far plane'. But the retail mechanism never touches zfar. The state machine, AnimLevel table and timings are otherwise exact, so this is the one visible deviation left in the sequence. Not in the ledgers (streaming-teleport-3 is about the reveal gate only).

finding.decomp_evidence: acclient.c:143073-143077 SetOverrideFovDistance sets m_bUseViewDistance/m_fViewDistFOV. 143080-143089 GetOverrideFovDistance default = `1.0 / tan(m_fGameFOV / (aspect - 0.1) * 0.5)`. 144891-144899 RenderNormalMode: `if (m_bUseViewDistance) Render::set_vdst(m_fViewDistFOV); else SetFOVRad(...)`. 143942-143952 CreatureMode (UseSmartboxFOV) does the same for the tunnel viewport. 378875-378897 set_vdst -> SetFOVInternal(2·atan) and znear = vdst·0.25 when vdst < 0.4. 453039-453050 PrimD3DRender::SetFOVInternal -> D3DXMatrixPerspectiveFovLH(fov, aspect, znear, Render::zfar): zfar untouched. 262494-262556 gmSmartBoxUI::UseTime states 5/6 lerp vdist gameVDist<->0.001 along GetAnimLevel. Decompiler caveat: the printed atan2 operand order would give π−fov at gameVDist (a pop at the end); FPATAN order gives 2·atan(1/vdst), which is the identity at gameVDist and ≈180° at 0.001. Either reading changes FOV only.
finding.proposed_change: portal_space.js: replace tunnelFarFrac/worldOverlayAlpha with a view-distance ratio. vdist(t) = TUNNEL_FADEOUT: gameVDist + (0.001 − gameVDist)·AnimLevel(t)/1024; WORLD_FADEIN: 0.001 + (gameVDist − 0.001)·AnimLevel(t)/1024, with gameVDist = 1. Compute fov' = 2·atan(tan(fov/2)·1/vdist), capped at 179°. Apply it to _tunnelCam.fov during TUNNEL_FADEOUT and keep its far plane fixed. Apply it to the main camera's projection during WORLD_FADEIN in place of the black quad, restoring at OFF (one updateProjectionMatrix per frame). Expect a draw spike on the reveal frames, because at 179° everything in front is in the frustum (retail had the same); CSM/culling follow the camera automatically. Keep QUICK_FADE_OUT for the quick login mode. Flag `?portalFovFade` (=off keeps today's far-plane/black-quad arm). Extend test_portal_space_sequencer.mjs with the ratio curve.

implementation.summary: I added the retail FOV-zoom portal fades behind the opt-in `?portalFovFade=on` flag. Without the flag, the tunnel's far-plane shrink and the black world quad run exactly as before. The new sequencer method `viewDistFov(fovDeg)` ports gmSmartBoxUI::UseTime states 5/6 (acclient.c:262497-262527). It returns null outside TUNNEL_FADEOUT / WORLD_FADEIN. Inside them it uses g = 1/tan(fovV/2), lerps the view distance g↔0.001 along GetAnimLevel (state 5 runs over `s.fadeOut`, so the 0.25 s quick login fade also works), then applies Render::set_vdst's fov = 2·atan(1/vdist), capped at 179°. These two pure helpers are exported as `viewDistForFov` and `fovForViewDist`. With the flag on, `renderPortalSpaceFrame` widens the tunnel camera's fov and keeps its far plane at the game far. During WORLD_FADEIN, `tickPortalSpace` (which runs after the camera tick and before the render) writes the zoomed fov to the active world camera once per frame and calls updateProjectionMatrix. The camera keeps that fov between frames, so the cell PVS and frustum-cull passes at the start of the next tick see the zoomed (wider) view. The game fov is put back at OFF, on endPortalSpace teardown, and when a new tunnel starts. If a resize or the FOV slider changes the fov mid-fade, that new value becomes the base. The black quad is skipped while the zoom holds; a top-down ortho camera still gets the quad. CSM guard: while the zoom holds, `camera.userData.csmFitFov` stores the game fov, and csm.js `_fitFov` fits the cascades from that value instead of camera.fov. Without it, the cascades stretched about 18x at 170°. With no `csmFitFov` set, csm.js behaves as before. The diag now publishes `__portalSpace.fovFade {on, world, base, tunnel}`.

implementation.deviations:
1. The verifier asked me to extend test_portal_space_sequencer.mjs. The hard rules forbid editing existing tests, so all the test_plan items went into the new tests/portal_fov_fade.test.mjs instead. It tests the sequencer curve (null outside states 5/6, base fov at t=0, monotonic rise to 179, the WORLD_FADEIN mirror, and the quick fade using s.fadeOut). It also tests module-level behaviour with fake renderer/camera objects, and adds the static assert the verifier requested.
2. The CSM guard needed a small edit to scene3d/csm.js, which is outside this lane's file list. The function `_fitFov(camera)` replaces `camera.fov` in three places (projChanged, the `_lastCamFov` cache, `_frustumCornersWorld`). It only changes anything when `camera.userData.csmFitFov` is set, which happens only under the flag during the 1 s fade-in. csm.js had no other uncommitted edits at the time.
3. As the verifier asked (write the fov once per frame, restore at OFF), the world camera keeps the zoomed fov between frames instead of being restored after every draw. I kept that deliberately: cells.js tickCellVisibility3D and culling.js tickFrustumCull run earlier in the next tick and need the zoomed frustum. If the fov were restored after each draw, they would cull at the game fov and leave statics, entities and cells missing at the screen edges during the zoom. That is why the CSM is guarded through userData rather than by restoring the camera.

6. I left adaptive_render_scale.js unchanged (not my lane). It only lowers the render scale when the GPU-behind probe says the GPU is behind, or on two consecutive frames over 165 ms. It also holds off for 30 s after boot, so the CPU-side draw spike from the wide frustum on the reveal frames should not trigger it. The eye test checks this.

finding.title: Retail 'Environment Detail Textures' pass on EnvCell walls and building shells is missing
finding.description: In retail EoL, DrawEnvCell and DrawBuilding set Render::curr_detail_surface (environment/building detail surface, tiling, SRCBLEND DESTCOLOR / DESTBLEND INVSRCALPHA) around the cell-structure and building-part draws only, not the objects inside cells. RenderMeshSubset then draws each subset a second time with the region's detail texture at UV0 × curr_detail_tiling. It is enabled at quality 4-5 and by default (byte_81EF95 = 1). On the EoL region, TerrainDesc[1] (building) and TerrainDesc[2] (environment) are 0x05001787 at tiling 4. Per pixel: out = texel·L·(1 + detail.rgb·L − detail.a), roughly mean-neutral high-frequency grain. Holtburger has no such pass. Its only non-terrain detail path keys on the Surface Detail bit (0x20000), which no DAT surface carries: retail sets that bit only on the custom surface GenerateDetailSurface builds. That path then composites modern PNG tiles, not the DAT texture. Related insight, no change proposed: the decomp also shows EoL never draws a landscape detail texture. Every SetDetailTexturing call passes landscape = 0, and byte_81EF94 is 0 at every quality level. So terrain.js's 'retail-global' terrain detail is an enhancement, not retail; its comment should say so.

finding.title: Retail skipNoTexture rule (untextured subsets not drawn on buildings/EnvCells) not ported
finding.description: In D3DPolyRender::DrawMesh, skipNoTexture = 1 drops every subset whose surface is untextured (`(type & 6) == 0`) while drawing a building (ObjBuildingOrBuildingPart, set by DrawBuilding) or an EnvCell (DrawEnvCell passes isEnvCell = 1). Ordinary objects keep their untextured surfaces. Retail's ConstructMesh does NOT skip NoPos polygons; it uses UV index 0. Holtburger has the opposite rule: it skips every NoPos polygon on every GfxObj and EnvCell, never tests the surface type, and renders solid-colour surfaces as 1×1 colour textures. Doorway portal faces are NoPos and untextured, so both rules hide them, which is why holtburger's doors look right. The residue is untextured polygons that have UVs. WebAC's DAT-backed tests name candidates retail never draws: the 0x010014C3 Training Academy doorway slab (solid blue 0x080006FD), the black 0x080000DF seam faces of building 0x01002286, and the pink 0x08000B79/0x08000B7A faces that make up all of the 0xB2AA cells. Whether holtburger draws them depends on their stippling, which I could not check without loading DATs, so this needs a census first.

finding.title: The ±12 boundary-portal reject is tested in landblock space (mod 24), not the polygon's local frame
finding.description: Retail's DrawPortalPolyInternal skips a portal polygon when all its vertices have x == +12, or all x == −12, or all y == ±12, using exact float compares on the polygon's own vertices. Those vertices are in the frame pushed for the draw: the EnvCell frame for the indoor seal (DrawCells pushes cell->pos), and the building part frame for the outdoor punch (DrawPortal). Holtburger applies the test to the world/landblock-space aperture vertices, as 'coordinate is a multiple of 24 (±1e-3)'. That only matches retail when the cell or building origin sits at a landcell centre and its rotation is a multiple of 90°. A rotated or off-centre building gets its boundary portals punched/sealed when retail skips them. Conversely, a portal lying on a world 24 m line that is not at local ±12 is skipped when retail draws it. WebAC applies the guard to the part-local vertices.

implementation.summary: Census only, as the orchestrator asked; no behaviour change. I added an #[ignore]d Rust census, crates/holtburger-dat/tests/portal_boundary_reject_census.rs. For every outdoor-facing EnvCell portal it compares three things: retail's exact ±12 test on the CellStruct-local vertices (the seal), the web client's world mod-24 test on the f32 vertices the wasm builds (a port of isLandCellBoundaryPoly), and retail's exact test on the building GfxObj's own portal polygon (the punch). The punch polygon is linked to its EnvCell portal through the drawing-BSP PortalPoly and BuildInfo.portals[portal_index]. I measured it on ~/ac_base_dats with the same predicates, using the read-only tools/dat-patch Python reader (31 s). Of 16,997 outdoor portals, retail skips 2,163 and the JS test skips 2,545; they disagree on 412. In 374 the JS test skips a portal retail draws because its 1e-3 tolerance treats local 12.0001 as 12; 366 of these are in Environments 0x0D0005B4-C0, and the dominant case is a wall portal with f32 12.0001 on some vertices. In 23 more the JS test skips a portal retail draws: 19 off-centre cells whose portal lies on a world 24 m line, and 4 polygons spanning both ±12 walls, which the JS test accepts because it only asks each vertex to be on SOME line. In 15 retail skips an off-centre cell's ±12 wall that the JS test keeps. None of the 412 involves a non-right-angle yaw, so the finding's 'rotated building' theory is not where the divergence is. The building-GfxObj-local test agrees with the CellStruct-local test on all 16,937 linked building portals, so a CellStruct-local exact test is faithful for both punch and seal; the census asserts that (bld_vs_cell_local == 0). I also checked the JS numbers against the real portal_clip.js function on all 16,997 portals: 2,545 skips, 412 disagreements, 0 mismatches with the port. Finally I rewrote the isLandCellBoundaryPoly doc comment and the wallOffset comment to drop the claim that mod-24 is the same as retail's ±12 and to cite the census; the diff is comment-only.

finding.title: Ghost entities: the wasm visibility set keeps objects ACE has stopped tracking (3x3 OR 384 m, no SeenOutside/dungeon rule)
finding.description: The 25 s out-of-visibility prune (maintPrune, default on) only arms for entities outside `current_visible_world_guids`. That set is the player's 3x3 landblocks UNION anything within 384 m, with no cell rule. ACE's visible set is narrower. Outdoors (or in a SeenOutside cell) it is the current landblock plus its loaded adjacents, excluding objects that sit in non-SeenOutside env cells. In a sealed env cell it is only the current cell plus its VisibleCells. Dungeon landblocks have no adjacents at all. ACE drops an object from KnownObjects 25 s after it leaves that set and then sends nothing more about it: no UpdatePosition, no DeleteObject when it dies or despawns, no re-create until it re-enters. Holtburger therefore keeps ghosts that never time out. (a) Entities in Chebyshev-2 landblocks within 192-384 m of the player stay frozen at their last pose. A dead monster never becomes a corpse, an NPC re-minted by a landblock reload shows twice, and a player who recalled still stands there. (b) In a sealed dungeon, everything in the 3x3 (adjacent dungeon landblocks, non-visible rooms, the outdoor objects of the same landblock) is kept. Entities draw to the frustum far plane (culling.js CULL_DIST_SQ = Infinity), so band-(a) ghosts are visible. They also feed radar, Tab-cycling and bot target lists. The JS reaper is no backstop: it keeps anything within 8 landblocks (17x17). WebAC hit exactly this (BUG.ghost-objects, 2026-10-11: an agent attacked a phantom Mite Sentry for a minute) and fixed it with a retail ObjectMaint port. Holtburger's own TODO at liveness.rs:137-144 names the fix, and the scene already holds the per-cell SeenOutside bits it needs. Not in any comparison ledger. NETSYNC-4 only made the existing prune reach JS.

implementation.summary:
I added an ACE-parity visibility predicate to the wasm world's out-of-visibility prune in liveness.rs. It sits behind a strict opt-in flag, `?aceObjMaint=on`, and with the flag absent the prune behaves exactly as before. With the flag on:
- **Outdoor player:** an entity stays visible if its landblock is the player's or an adjacent one, and it is outdoors or in a SeenOutside EnvCell. An unloaded SeenOutside bit counts as visible. An entity in the same landblock whose EnvCell lists the player's cell in its VisibleCells also stays (ACE `EnvCell.IsVisibleIndoors`).
- **Player in an EnvCell:** visible means the player's own cell or one of its visibility neighbours (portals plus the DAT `visible_cells`). If the player's cell is SeenOutside, anything within one landblock also stays. That matches `EnvCell.IsVisibleIndoors`, which does not filter on the object's own cell.
- **Fallback:** if the player's EnvCell record is not loaded yet (the native CLI never loads one), the old 3x3-or-384 m predicate runs unchanged.
- **Deadline:** 30 s under the flag, 25 s by default. ACE only expires its queue on a player cell change or on the ~5 s player Heartbeat, so it forgets an object 25-30 s after it leaves; pruning late is harmless, pruning early is not.

This removes both ghost bands: entities in landblocks two away that are still within 384 m, and unseen rooms or adjacent landblocks around a sealed dungeon cell. I also added `SpatialScene::cell_seen_outside_opt`, which returns an `Option` instead of folding an unloaded bit to false, and wired the flag through lib.rs, LoopFlags and the two world-creation sites, following the openSeaWall pattern. The JS reaper and ghostRigSweep are unchanged.

implementation.eye_test:
This is a live behaviour soak, not a visual check; laptop headless with `?nullRender=1` is fine. URL: `?aceObjMaint=on&nosw=1` with a fresh wasm build. Steps:
1. Confirm the console line `[maint] aceObjMaint ON`.
2. Outdoors at Holtburg: note nearby creatures and NPCs, then @teleloc or walk two landblocks away (still inside 384 m). Wait 35 s. Their rigs should be removed by KIND_REMOVE (wasm entity count drops; no `[ghost-rig]` lines needed). Return: they re-create normally.
3. Dungeon: stand in a room, have a monster in a room not visible from it (or kill one there), move away, wait 35 s, return. Expect no frozen ghost; a living monster re-creates.
4. Fight a monster while moving between building or dungeon rooms for over 60 s. It must never disappear while ACE is still updating it. Watch for a monster that is attacking you but has no rig.
5. Repeat step 4 with the flag off to confirm the default is unchanged.
implementation.deviations:
1. Following the orchestrator note, the whole change sits behind the opt-in `?aceObjMaint=on`. The 30 s deadline applies only under the flag; the default keeps 25 s and the conservative predicate, so the default path is unchanged.
2. The predicate is the union of ACE's GetVisibleObjects (run on the player's cell change) and ObjCell.IsVisible / EnvCell.IsVisibleIndoors (run on the object's cell change in handle_visible_obj); ACE keeps whichever ran last and re-runs neither while both stand still. The verifier's clause (4) would prune entities in non-SeenOutside cells for a player in a SeenOutside cell, but IsVisibleIndoors keeps them known in ACE (SeenOutside(P) and block distance <= 1, with no check on the object's cell). That is the dangerous prune-earlier-than-ACE case, so for a SeenOutside player cell any entity within one landblock stays. Also, for an outdoor player, a same-landblock non-SeenOutside EnvCell whose VisibleCells list the player's cell is kept. Both changes are strictly more conservative than the verifier's version.
3. The carrier flag is a field on `EntityLifecycleStore` (liveness.rs, Default false) instead of a new WorldState field in types.rs. This keeps the Rust edit inside the lane's liveness.rs.
4. The lane listed only specific lib.rs items, but the opt-in flag needed plumbing in lib.rs (parse fn, read site, LoopFlags), session/mod.rs, session/messages/login.rs and session/commands/lifecycle.rs. All are small additive edits following the openSeaWall/objectBlobQueue pattern.

finding.title: Ship a default shard-record budget using WebAC's time-protected LRU and low-water trim (the fix for the 24 MB thrash that kept it unbounded)
finding.description: `V2Source::shards`, the DAT-record cache, runs unbounded by default in both wasm instances. The 1070 census (OOM handoff §8) measured it at +226 MB of the +248 MB wasm allocLive growth over six town hops: 307 MB, of which 234 MB is main and 73 MB is the worker. The handoff values a budget at about 200 MB. It was never shipped for two reasons. A 24 MB budget caused ~280 MB of evict-and-refetch churn. And shard_cache.rs:48-53 documents a residual: protection lasts only one locked insert round, so a record the walk just hydrated can be evicted before the caller's re-walk reads it, which spends the finite starved-retry ladders. WebAC's DatStore answers exactly that. A unit read or landed in the last 120 s is never evicted, so the cap is soft during a burst. When over the cap it trims oldest-first down to 85% in one batch, not one victim per insert. And its LRU is an insertion-ordered Map, so touch is O(1) and eviction O(evicted). Holtburger's `evict_to_budget` runs `min_by_key` over the whole map for every victim. With ~9k entries at steady state that is a full scan per insert once a budget is armed. A time floor closes the hydrate-to-re-walk window by construction. The budget then only has to exceed the last ~1-2 minutes of working set (one area), not every town visited. That lets a moderate default (for example 96 MB main / 48 MB worker) cut the converged 307 MB roughly in half without thrash. This is new evidence and a ready design for an item holtburger left as an unarmed opt-in. It is not in the comparison ledgers.

Keep round protection for oversize single rounds. Replace the per-victim scan with an ordered structure (for example a `BTreeMap<u64 tick, K>` alongside the HashMap, or the `lru`/`indexmap` crates if they are already in the lockfile) so eviction is O(evicted · log n). Protection lasts only begin_round/end_round (one locked insert batch). evict_to_budget runs `.min_by_key(last_use)` over the whole map once per victim and has no time floor or low-water mark. manifest_source.rs:138-150 returns usize::MAX unless __hbShardBudgetBytes is set, and bake_worker_client.js:93-109 leaves it unset. url-flags.md:618 records the 24 MB thrash (~280 MB of refetch churn). The WebAC citations are accurate: DatStore.ts:64 cap, :76 120 s floor, :78 0.85, :704-718 touch, :724-750 evictIfOverCap. The open item is not a duplicate: OOM handoff §8 and 2026-10-07-pre-4.8-code-review.md:84 still owe an ABAB. What falls is the payoff claim. The handoff (docs/2026-08-05-1070-black-flicker-and-renderer-oom-handoff.md:350-357) shows the store CONVERGES (+92, +76, +41, +6, +2, +9 MB) and concludes '307 MB is the working set' and 'a tidy-up, not the crash fix' (:390-391, :496, :581). That is worth landing behind the existing opt-in flag so the owed ABAB can test a sane design.

finding.title: Model decode counts catalog-proven absences as misses: dangling refs spend the starved-retry ladder and never memoize, while transient failures get only 3 tries before a permanent partial bake
finding.description: The statics and buildings bakers treat `decodeMisses > 0` as starvation. They un-mark the landblock and retry up to 3 times (2.5 s guard cooldown each), then accept the partial bake permanently for as long as the landblock stays resident. statics.js says the cap exists because a permanently absent record is "indistinguishable from starvation at this layer". But the wasm can tell the two apart. The surface path's `DecodeAuditSource` already counts only misses where `!key_known_absent(key)`, which is catalog-authoritative. The model path's `MissCountingSource` (triangulate_model_counted → ModelMesh.decodeMisses / BuildingPlacement.decode_misses) counts every Err. That has three costs. (1) Any model with a dangling DAT ref (part, degrade or surface id absent from the catalog) is marked starved on every bake: 3 wasted retry cycles and a loud partial-bake warning per landblock. (2) Such a model can never enter MODEL_TRI_CACHE (memo inserts require misses == 0) or statGeomCache, so it is re-triangulated on every bake. (3) Real transient failures (a wifi drop, a tunnel reconnect, the 666 kbps link) get only ~3 × (3 immediate back-to-back round tries + 2.5 s), roughly 10 s. After that the missing buildings and props stay missing until the player leaves the area. WebAC's rule is the opposite split. Absence is known from the manifest, so a read of a nonexistent file is not a miss. A real miss is tracked per key, and the block is rebuilt when those files land: "never rely on null meaning 'doesn't exist'". Not in the ledgers.
finding.webac_evidence: docs/dat-streaming.md:42 ("needs either 'fetch before build' or 'rebuild on arrival'. It must never rely on null meaning 'doesn't exist'"). packages/renderer/src/world/LandblockObjectStreamer.ts:336-366 `trackedSteps`: `if (missed) settled.push(s)` … `Promise.all(settled).then(() => this.rebuildBlock(blockX, blockY))`. packages/renderer/src/dat/streaming/RetryOnArrival.ts:17-36 (re-run once the missed keys are resident, bounded). DatStore.ts:431 `ensure` skips absent files. DatStore.ts:830-831 retries back off 250/500/1000 ms.
finding.holtburger_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:10299-10333 `MissCountingSource::get_file_by_key`: `if r.is_err() { self.misses.fetch_add(1, ..) }` (no known-absent check), used by `triangulate_model_counted` :10487-10498. Contrast lib.rs:13065-13101 `DecodeAuditSource`: `if r.is_err() && !self.inner.key_known_absent(key)`. scene3d/statics.js:1064-1082 ("PERMANENTLY undecodable … indistinguishable from starvation at this layer", `STATICS_STARVED_RETRY_CAP = 3`). :2383-2408 ("accepting PARTIAL bake after 3 starved retries"). scene3d/buildings.js:484 and :895-908 (same pattern). stream_bake_guard.js:24 `STREAM_BAKE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_MS = 2500`. src/prefetch.rs:239 and :531-555: 3 round tries back to back with no delay.
finding.decomp_evidence: Retail never builds incomplete: DBObj::Get blocks until the file is local, and CellManager::PreFetchCells (acclient.c:146528) holds the client until cells are present. That is why WebAC rebuilds on arrival rather than accepting a partial build.
finding.proposed_change: (1) Rust: give `MissCountingSource` the same rule as DecodeAuditSource (count only `!key_known_absent`) and also count proven-absent keys separately. Expose `decodeMissesAbsent` next to `decodeMisses` on ModelMesh and BuildingPlacement. A non-resident catalog proves nothing, so those keys stay transient. That alone stops dangling refs from spending retries, and the memo gate (`misses == 0`) then admits models whose only gaps are proven absences, which is correct because nothing more will ever arrive. (2) JS statics.js/buildings.js: with transient misses only, replace the hard cap of 3 with exponential backoff while the landblock stays in the ring, for example 2.5 → 5 → 10 → 20 → 40 s capped at 60 s, re-armed when the landblock is re-fired. Optionally make it arrival-driven: the source publishes a 'failed keys drained' epoch in `__hbShardCache` and the guard re-fires starved landblocks when it moves. (3) Add a 250/500/1000 ms backoff between `PREFETCH_ROUND_TRIES` in prefetch.rs and batch_walk.rs. Tests: a lib.rs native test with a MockSource whose catalog proves one part absent expects misses == 0 and absent == 1. tests/ gets a statics starved-retry test that confirms a transient-starved landblock is still retried after the 3rd attempt.

It also does not forward key_known_absent at all, so wrapped code sees the trait default false. DecodeAuditSource (lib.rs:13298-13342) counts only `r.is_err() && !inner.key_known_absent(key)` and forwards the method. MissCountingSource feeds the memo gate (triangulate_model_uncached, lib.rs:10829 `complete = misses == 0`), ModelMesh.decode_misses (lib.rs:17212-17242) and BuildingPlacement.decode_misses (lib.rs:17443-17488). The JS ladders are as cited: statics.js:1068-1085 and :2387-2414 (cap 3, then the partial bake is accepted), buildings.js:484 and :893-912, stream_bake_guard.js:25 at 2500 ms. prefetch.rs:239 and :531-555 retry rounds back to back with no delay. Absent keys are skipped silently in prefetch Step C (manifest_source.rs:851, 'catalog has no entry → silent skip'), so a dangling ref only reaches the decode-miss counter, as claimed. Not in the ledgers. What weakens it: (1) There is no evidence that dangling refs exist in end-of-retail statics or buildings. rg finds no 'accepting PARTIAL' or 'decode INCOMPLETE' observation in any doc, and lib.rs:11725-11729 says the old 'absent' evidence was really our synthetic 0x08F0 tex-swap aliases. So the 3-wasted-retries and never-memoized costs are hypothetical, though cheap to fix. (2) WebAC is not more robust on transient failures. LandblockObjectStreamer.ts:365 keeps the partial build on a failed fetch (`/* failed fetch: keep what was built */`), RetryOnArrival.ts:18 caps runs at MAX_ARRIVAL_RETRIES = 4, and DatStore.ts:830-845 throws after 250/500/1000 ms retries. The proposed exponential-backoff-forever ladder is therefore the comparer's own design, not a WebAC lesson. The decomp aside (retail blocks on local DAT reads) is true but not decisive. The WebAC citations (dat-streaming.md:42, LandblockObjectStreamer.ts:336-366, RetryOnArrival.ts:17-36) are accurate.

I made two changes, following the orchestrator's split (part 3 skipped).

Part (1), lib.rs `MissCountingSource`: a failed read now counts as a miss only when the catalog cannot prove the record absent, the same rule `DecodeAuditSource` already uses. The wrapper also forwards `key_known_absent` (area note MISSED-1), so the R-7 surface negative-cache gate works again for relief priming that runs inside it. Both memos are cleared on `init_resource_source` re-init, so a memo admitted on a catalog proof cannot outlive that catalog. Keys that cannot be proven absent (catalog not loaded, v1 / convention-URL mode) still count as misses. Escape flag: `?provenAbsentExempt=off`.

Part (2): a failure-only pause before a failed prefetch round's 2nd and 3rd attempts (250 ms, then 750 ms). Compile-time asserts tie the schedule length to both loops' 3 tries.

Final geometry stays the same, because a proven-absent record never arrives on either path. I added native Rust tests (not run here) and a JS source-contract test (run, passing). The existing `interior_stab_batch` source contract also still passes.

finding.title: Service worker persists content-addressed bodies unverified and ignores cache:'reload', so a hash mismatch can never self-heal (and the pack lane's reload retry is defeated once SW_V3 flips)
finding.description: Shard URLs are `shards/{prefix2}/{sha256}.bin`. Both Rust Step E and the shard-fetch worker sha-verify every body, and a mismatch fails the key. But the service worker's fetch handler stores every 200 'basic' response for a content-addressed path with `cache.put` without checking it, and serves cache-first forever. It never looks at `event.request.cache`. Every retry of a mismatched key therefore gets the same bad bytes back from Cache Storage, in this session and in all later ones. serve.py's `immutable, max-age=31536000` does the same through the HTTP cache under `?nosw=1`. Neither the Rust shard path nor the shard worker uses any cache-busting mode on retry. pack_fetch_controller.js was designed for this class (D-03.5: "mismatch => ONE cache: 'reload' retry … a truncated/corrupt HTTP-cache body"). But once SW_V3 adds /packs/ to the content-addressed set, the SW will answer that reload request from Cache Storage and the designed retry cannot work. Getting a wrong 200 body in is uncommon (static SSD dist, TLS tunnel), but the failure is permanent and the fix is small. WebAC verifies size and sha before persisting, re-verifies cache hits, falls through to the network and replaces the entry on mismatch, and fetches with `cache: 'no-store'` because its object cache is the cache.

implementation.summary: The service worker now checks content-addressed bodies before it caches them. For `shards/` (and `packs/` + `index/` once SW_V3 is on) it returns the network response to the page at once. Under waitUntil it hashes a clone with crypto.subtle and calls `cache.put` on a second clone only when the sha256 prefix equals the hash in the file name. A name that does not parse, or a sandbox with no digest engine, keeps the old put; a body that cannot be read in full is never cached. A content-addressed request with `cache:'reload'` or `'no-store'` now skips `cache.match`, goes to the network (past the immutable HTTP cache) and overwrites the entry on a verified 200. This also means the pack lane's D-03.5 reload retry will keep working after SW_V3 flips. The shard fetch worker remembers each URL whose body failed its sha check (at most 4096) and sends that URL's next request with `cache:'reload'`, keeping its priority. The mark is used once per failure and set again if the body mismatches again. On the Rust side, Step E (holtburger-resource-http manifest_source.rs) marks a mismatched URL in a thread-local ReloadSet (shard_route.rs). `fetch_shard_bytes` takes the mark and, on the direct path (no registered fetcher, e.g. the bake worker's wasm instance or `?shardFetchWorker=off`), fetches with `cache:'reload'` through the new private `fetch_bytes_with_init`. No default behaviour changes unless a hash mismatch happens. Nothing visual changes.

finding.title: Discovery walks use level barriers (each round waits for its slowest fetch); pipeline them and lift the 32-wide page cap on HTTP/2
finding.description: Every keyed or batch walk runs: discovery → `prefetch(misses).await` → discovery again. Inside `prefetch_impl` the round is `join_all(fetches).await`, and only afterwards does Step E insert the bodies. So no record that landed early is readable, and none of its children can be requested, until the slowest fetch of that depth level returns. Model and interior chains are 5-6 levels deep (Setup → part GfxObj → Surface → SurfaceTexture → RenderSurface → Palette, plus MotionTable → Animation), so a cold player-blocking walk pays roughly depth × the tail TTFB of each round. The academy work measured shard delivery p90 at about 0.2 s, and tunnel and edge links have fatter tails. WebAC hit the same wall ("every dependent wave waited for its slowest edge miss") and fixed it with a pipelined walk plus 96 concurrent streams. On an HTTP/2 edge, cold login gates went from 11.5 s to 4.6 s and teleports from 8.0-9.7 s to 4.0 s. Holtburger's page-wide fetch total of 32 (split main/worker 0.75/0.25) was tuned against HTTP/1.1's 6 connections per origin. Over the Cloudflare tunnel (HTTP/2 or 3) that leaves most of a 100-stream connection idle. Caveat: the SPEC plans to retire this lane for world content in favour of baked-closure packs (pass-03 S1.4). But `?packSource` is DEV, the live dist ships no packs, and the legacy lane remains for equipment, other players' appearance and admin spawns, so this pays off now and afterwards.

DatStore.ts:66-74 `DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT = 96` ("48 left half the connection idle"). docs/dat-streaming.md:567-596 (§6.7 A/B: 11.5 → 4.6 s cold login gate, 8.0 → 4.0 s teleport; with one file held, >60% of the closure lands vs 15/473 before).

finding.decomp_evidence: n/a (fetch scheduling). Retail's synchronous DBObj::Get has no waves.
finding.proposed_change: (1) manifest_source.rs `prefetch_impl`: drive Step D with `FuturesUnordered` and verify-and-insert each body as it completes, keeping begin_round/end_round around the whole drain. Add a `prefetch_progressive(keys, min_fraction, settle_ms)` that returns once, say, 60% of the keys have landed or 100 ms after the first completion. Stragglers stay in `shard_inflight`, so the next round latches onto them rather than refetching. (2) batch_walk.rs/prefetch.rs: use it in the round loop. The stall guard must treat 'same miss set but some still in flight' as wait-for-in-flight, not stalled, and the round cap should count discoveries with a slightly higher ceiling. Keep `?walkPace` so each extra discovery runs in its own task; surfaceWalkLite already keeps discoveries cheap. Put it behind a default-on flag with an `=off` escape. (3) index.html before `applyFetchConcurrencySplit`: read `performance.getEntriesByName(MANIFEST_URL)[0]?.nextHopProtocol`, and for 'h2'/'h3' raise the unauthored total from 32 to about 64-96, leaving HTTP/1.1 at 32. Measure with the existing coldload-1009 harness (interior walls time, `__diag.shardFetch()`) on the tunnel and on tailnet HTTP/1.1, interleaved ABAB.

The WebAC citations are accurate (DatClosure.ts:94-121 pipelined visit, DatStore.ts:66-74 96 streams, dat-streaming.md:567-596 A/B). The transfer to holtburger is weak, though. (1) WebAC's gains come from cold Cloudflare-to-R2 edge misses at 0.4-0.6 s TTFB each, 'whatever its size' (dat-streaming.md §6.7). Holtburger serves a local SSD dist through serve.py. The owner's own link is raw tailnet HTTP/1.1 ('owner: no Cloudflare', HANDOFF-charselect-coldload-2026-10-09.md:17,:81-82). There the cold load is queue-bound behind Chrome's 6 connections ('1,154 in flight', ~100 req/s), and the handoff concludes 'Fewer requests (packs, §6.2) is the only real lever' (:89-96). Neither pipelining nor a higher cap fixes HTTP/1.1 queueing. (2) A holtburger discovery is not WebAC's cheap cached-edge visit but a full dry-run re-decode of the closure (discovery_round re-walks via the walk closure). A progressive 60%-landed prefetch multiplies main-thread discovery passes, the exact jank ?walkPace exists to contain. (3) Inserting per completion breaks shard_cache's documented 'rounds never interleave' protection invariant (shard_cache.rs:57-62), which would need redesign. What stands: on an h2/h3 route (the public Cloudflare tunnel), 32 page-wide fetches is probably conservative, and holtburger already detects the protocol (tex_upgrade_queue.js:202-217 _defaultProtocol via nextHopProtocol). An h2-aware total is cheap and measurable. The pipelined-walk redesign is not justified on current evidence.

finding.title: Missiles fly through creatures and the local player: the sweep skips creatures because of a misread of retail missile_ignore
finding.description: holtburger's local missile sweep (physupd-1) only tests buildings, EnvCell shells, cell statics and BSP entities (doors). Its header says that is retail, because missile_ignore 'skips non-target creatures'. That is wrong for the client. Retail missile_ignore ignores a creature only when OBJECTINFO.targetID != 0, and the client only ever sets targetID to 0. So on retail every non-ethereal, non-missile creature stops a missile locally, including the target and the local player. In holtburger a bolt flies into and through its target and only stops when ACE's impact (SetState + VectorUpdate) arrives. At Flame Bolt speed (MaximumVelocity 15 m/s) or arrow speed (20–30 m/s), with ~50–150 ms one-way latency, it travels 1–4 m past the target, so the Explode plays behind the target. Monster arrows and bolts also pass through the player. ACE's own SpellProjectile.cs comment describes the client colliding with the target locally (the 'ghost projectile' case). Re-raised with new evidence: round 1 listed the creature sweep as a follow-up, but holtburger's stated reason for skipping it is refuted by the decomp. WebAC also has a ready design (sweepCylinders/sweepSpheres plus the local player's cylinder). Note: ACE's server sets TargetID = ProjectileTarget, so the server's bolt passes non-target creatures while the retail client stopped it on any creature in its path. That is how retail looked, and it should be kept.

implementation.summary: Missiles now stop on the solid objects in their path, not only on walls and doors. The new object layer covers creatures, other players, the local player, chests and props, matching retail. In the decomp, OBJECTINFO::missile_ignore (acclient.c:314070) exempts a creature only when targetID != 0, and the client only ever sets targetID = 0 (:311603, :312155). I added a new Rust module, crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/missile_sweep.rs, with `WorldState::sweep_missile_against_objects`. It reuses `obj_collider_for_entity` (client body pose, obj_scale, Setup shapes, and the setup_radii cylinder for unparsed Setups). It tests cylspheres first, otherwise spheres, using the existing CCylSphere and CSphere sweep functions with the Z-slab check on wall hits. A start inside a body counts as a t=0 hit only when moving inward, which fixes the far-root exit that would otherwise read as a false hit. It skips the missile itself, MISSILE and ETHEREAL objects, parented objects, contained or no-landblock objects, and HAS_PHYSICS_BSP objects (the existing door layer handles those). An ETHEREAL missile stops only on STATIC objects (retail obstruction_ethereal). A new additive wasm export `sweepSphereAgainstObjects` reads the missile's own state. In projectile_sweep.js the new layer is guarded by typeof, an ETHEREAL missile now skips the door layer, and the wrong missile_ignore comment is rewritten. The local player is exempt for the whole flight when the missile spawned within 4 m of them. This is decided once, at the first sweep, and covers our own launches while running or fast-casting. Escape: `?missileObjSweep=off` turns off both the object layer and the ETHEREAL rule.

Then run forward while casting bolts. Read `window.__projectileStops()` each time. | The bolt bursts at the FIRST body in its path: cause `client-sweep:sweepSphereAgainstObjects`, clientM ≈ distance to that body, no fly-through.
