finding.title: Retail Link Status numbers missing: no packet-loss ratio, and the ping RTT has one send-time slot shared by three keepalive drivers
finding.description: holtburger's link indicator already follows retail (5/20/40 s tiers, 0.75 s flash). Its tooltip shows only 'Ping N ms' and the age of the last packet. Retail's Link Status panel (gmLinkStatusUI::Update) shows packet loss to 2 decimals, computed by CLinkStatusAverages: 2 × (NAKed + retransmitted) / (received + sent), summed over 40 snapshots taken every 2 s. It also shows a ping it requests when the panel opens and every 120 s after. The session already has everything needed: it counts packets sent and received, and it answers NAKs in retransmit_sequences. The ping RTT is also unreliable. PING_SEND_INSTANT is a single Option<Instant> stamped by three independent senders: the 2.5 s setInterval, the 2 s keepalive worker, and the 5 s recv-loop arm (via ForceKeepalive). An overlapping second stamp makes the first PingResponse measure from the wrong send, and the second finds the slot empty. In ?netWorker mode, the worker's own 2.5 s pings never stamp the main-thread slot at all.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/network/src/LinkStatusAverages.ts:1-130 is a port: UShortAverager(40), heartbeat every 2000 ms (:116), and getAveragePacketLoss returns `ratio + ratio` (:101-106). Add 'Packet loss N%' to the linkstatus tooltip. For the RTT, replace the single slot with a VecDeque<Instant> of outstanding PingRequest send times: push on every send from any driver, pop_front on each PingResponse (ACE answers PingRequests in order). verification.reasoning: The RTT single-slot issue is confirmed. PING_SEND_INSTANT is at lib.rs:19384, not :18897. It is stamped by the 5 s arm (lib.rs:48779) and by ForceKeepalive (session/commands/lifecycle.rs:73), and ForceKeepalive is driven by both the 2.5 s setInterval (index.html:4527-4535) and the 2 s keepalive worker (:4552-4561). It is taken on each PingResponse (session/messages/game_event.rs:1157-1168). The worker's own pings (net_worker.rs:416-430) never stamp it, yet their responses consume the main-thread stamp. Unlike the comparer's framing, the RTT is not tooltip-only: linkTierFor (status-indicators.js:130-154) downgrades a 'good' tier above 1000 or 3000 ms. The retail feature gap is confirmed: gmLinkStatusUI::Update (acclient.c:226356) shows PacketLoss to 2 dp and requests a ping every 120 s, and CLinkStatusAverages::GetAveragePacketLoss (acclient.c:373794) computes 2·(NAKed+retransmitted)/(received+sent). The comparer's 'NAKed = 0' is right: ClientNet::AddToPerfCounter (acclient.c:370154) feeds nPktsNAKed from counter 6 (AcksReceivedCounter, acclient.h:4860), which has no increment site. The proposed FIFO fix is unsafe. ACE drops GameActions while session.Player == null (InboundMessageManager.HandleGameAction, around :124-133), and holtburger deliberately pings during EnteringWorld (lifecycle.rs comment). Unanswered entries would stay in a FIFO, later responses would be measured from older sends, the RTT would be inflated, and the indicator could go falsely yellow or red. The single slot heals itself on the next stamp; a FIFO would not. Value is low: this is a diagnostic. Not a duplicate.
verification.corrected_change: RTT: keep a single in-flight stamp, but only stamp when the slot is empty or older than about 5 s, and only in LoopState::InWorld (pings in EnteringWorld are never answered). Stamp from every main-thread sender. In worker mode, have the worker own the RTT: it records its own send times, computes the RTT when it sees a PingResponse, and posts it on a new RX kind; the main thread stops stamping in proxy mode. Packet loss: add Rust counters in holtburger-session (packets_sent including retransmits in send_raw_packet, packets_retransmitted in retransmit_sequences, packets_received after a valid checksum) and a 40-slot ring with a 2 s snapshot. Expose sessionPacketLossPct (direct) or an RX kind (worker). Add 'Packet loss N%' to the linkstatus tooltip. Keep JS as a display layer.
verification.rynth_risk: None. Rynth reads sessionLastRecvAgeMs (supervisor.cjs:201), not the ping RTT or tooltip text.
verification.test_plan: Pull the ping bookkeeping into a small Rust struct with native unit tests: overlapping sends credit the first send; an unanswered EnteringWorld ping does not inflate the next RTT; a stale stamp expires. Unit-test the 40-slot averager against the retail formula (2·retx/(recv+sent)). Node test: extend apps/holtburger-web/test_status_indicators.mjs through __test (status-indicators.js:764) for the tooltip line, and assert linkTierFor is unchanged for the existing inputs.

implementation.summary: I fixed the ping RTT measurement, added retail's packet-loss figure, and added a 'Packet loss N.NN%' line to the link-status tooltip, all within the partial scope the verifier set. Packet counting is a port of retail CLinkStatusAverages in the new holtburger-session/src/link_status.rs, which the Session now owns as `pub link_status`. It counts every sent packet including retransmits (send_raw_packet), every packet re-sent for a server NAK (retransmit_sequences) and every checksum-valid packet received (process_inbound_packet). It keeps a 40-sample u16 ring per counter, takes a heartbeat every 2 s on those same paths, and computes loss as 2*(NAKed+retx)/(recv+sent); NAKed stays 0, as in retail. For the RTT, the single PING_SEND_INSTANT slot that every send overwrote is replaced by PING_ROUND_TRIP in the new wasm-crate module src/ping_round_trip.rs (gated wasm32 OR test). The first ping in flight keeps the stamp, a stamp is only taken for in-world pings, a stale stamp is replaced after 10 s, and the response takes the stamp. Both main-thread drivers (the 5 s arm and ForceKeepalive) stamp after a successful send, and only in direct mode. Under ?netWorker the worker owns the RTT clock: it stamps its own pings and the forwarded ones, finds PlayerCreate and PingResponse by their opcodes, and posts a new RX_KIND_LINK_STATUS=3 message (RTT plus loss) on every keepalive tick and every measured round trip. JS forwards that to the new SessionHandle.netWorkerLinkStatus method, guarded with typeof, so no new static wasm import is needed. sessionPacketLossPct reads a thread-local that direct mode refreshes after every recv_message. linkTierFor is unchanged; the tooltip only shows the loss line once the link has received something.

implementation.deviations:
(1) The stale-stamp window is 10 s, not the verifier's "about 5 s". Pings go out every 1-2.5 s, so the window is also the largest RTT the clock can report. At 5 s, a real 6-8 s C2S delay would be re-stamped and shown as a short "good" RTT. 10 s keeps the linkTierFor 3 s "bad" bar reachable. Stuck stamps still clear on the next response, and only in-world pings are stamped. Test a_slow_link_still_measures_slow pins this.
(2) Ping bookkeeping lives in the wasm crate (apps/holtburger-web/src/ping_round_trip.rs, gated wasm32 OR test, tested natively) rather than in holtburger-session. It peeks game-message opcodes (PlayerCreate/PingResponse/PingRequest), and the session crate's ARCHITECTURE.md says "No Game Logic". The packet counters and averager are pure transport, so they live in holtburger-session as the verifier asked.
(3) The test plan said to extend test_status_indicators.mjs; the hard rules forbid editing existing tests. I added tests/link_status_packet_loss.test.mjs and exposed linkTooltipDetail and linkLossFact through __test. L3 asserts linkTierFor is unchanged for the existing inputs.
(4) The worker-to-main relay is a SessionHandle method (netWorkerLinkStatus), called from net_worker_client.js behind a typeof guard, instead of a new free wasm export. A static named import of a missing export would break module linking on a stale pkg/ and break the existing stub loader in net_worker_disconnect_kind.test.mjs.
(5) The tooltip prints retail's figure exactly: GetPacketLossPercentage is the doubled ratio, printed to 2 dp followed by "%" with no x100, matching gmLinkStatusUI::Update and WebAC.
(6) No URL flag. This is a HUD tooltip plus a more accurate RTT feeding the existing indicator tier; nothing in world rendering changes, and neither the verifier nor the orchestrator asked for a flag.
implementation.follow_ups:
- Direct mode has three ping drivers: the 5 s arm, plus ForceKeepalive from the 2.5 s setInterval and from the 2 s keepalive worker. Together they send about 1 PingRequest per second. They could be merged into one cadence (out of scope).
- Retail requests a ping when the Link Status panel opens and every 120 s after. holtburger has no Link Status panel, so only the tooltip got the numbers.
- In direct mode the RTT includes main-thread dispatch delay, because the response is timed when the recv loop handles it. Worker mode times it at the wire.
- If a readable real percentage is wanted, x100 would have to be a deliberate departure from retail.

finding.title: InventoryServerSaveFailed (0x00A0) prints 'You can't wield that!' / '[Wield failed] X' / 'WeenieError 0x0000' for every failed item request instead of retail's pending-request line
finding.description:
Retail looks at its single pending inventory request (ACCWeenieObject::prevRequest / prevRequestObjectID). It prints ONE spew-box line, "The <name> can't be merged / split / moved / picked up / put in the container / dropped / wielded / given", plus a per-code suffix such as " - action cancelled", " - you are too encumbered" or " - the container is closed". If no request is pending and the code has no suffix, the line is empty, so nothing shows. It then prints the code's own HandleFailureEvent text, except for 7 codes.

Holtburger ignores what was requested:
- code 0 → the chat line "You can't wield that!" and the toast "WeenieError 0x0000";
- any other code → "[Wield failed] <RustDebugLabel>".

ACE uses this event for nearly every inventory refusal. GameEventInventoryServerSaveFailed defaults errorType to None, with the comment "client doesn't show this error mostly, and defaults to specific error messages, depending on the item name + action". About 111 of roughly 170 senders pass no code, and about 30 pass ActionCancelled. Examples are a busy or encumbered pickup and a move-to chain cancelled while walking to loot.

So a failed pickup, drop, merge, split or give currently tells the player they couldn't WIELD something, and shows a raw hex toast. This happens routinely while looting, and the bot loot loop does it constantly.

Duplicate check: round 5 (FINDINGS-round5.md:66) noted this under "not reported, lower value", and round 1 (FINDINGS-round1.md:159) noted the missing one-at-a-time gate the same way. WebAC ships a ready, decomp-addressed port: the 8 verb templates with .rdata addresses, the NAME_PLURAL vs NAME_APPROPRIATE choice, the 9-code suffix table, the RecordResponse clear sites and the 7-code HandleFailureEvent exclusion. The ACE census shows code-0 item sends are the common case, not an edge.

finding.title: UpdateObject (0xF7DB) on a pack item does not move it to the container's first slot and does not refresh the inventory snapshot
finding.description:
Retail runs UpdateObject as destroy-and-recreate. The re-created weenie is no longer in its container's list, so ACCObjectMaint::SetWeenieDesc falls back to place 0 and ServerSaysMoveItem inserts it at the FRONT of the container.

ACE copies this server-side so the saved order stays in sync. RecipeManager.UpdateObj calls MoveItemToFirstContainerSlot after every UpdateObject for an un-wielded item in the player's inventory, and sends nothing to the client. UpdateObject senders are every recipe that modifies its source or target (tinkering, dyes, imbues, quest combines), Tailoring (2 sites) and Aetheria.

Holtburger's UpdateObject arm only re-applies the description:
- The item keeps its old slot, so the visible order differs from ACE's PlacementPosition until relog, and later drag placements computed from the local order can land one slot off.
- The arm also never sets `inventory_changed`, so the cached playerInventory() snapshot is rebuilt only if some other message happens to dirty it.

This is not covered by createobj-3 (deferred, render-only: house hooks / Setup swap) or by any ledger entry.

The snapshot is rebuilt only when dirty (src/lib.rs:37839-37850). src/lib.rs:34137-34147 routes only ObjectCreate/Delete/InventoryRemove/Parent/Pickup/ObjDesc to the world crate, so crates/holtburger-world/src/handlers/inventory.rs has no UpdateObject arm. finding.title: Waves load lazily on the slow download lane and play late; retail loads every wave when its sound table loads
finding.description: Retail never loads a wave at play time. SoundTableData::UnPack, SoundHook::UnPack and SoundTweakedHook::UnPack each call SoundManager::CreateSound, which builds the SoundBuf, and GetSound only looks the wave up in sound_hash_. A retail sound therefore starts on the frame of its event. Holtburger warms only the SoundTable at entity spawn, never its waves. The first play of each wave calls the wasm fetch_wave, which uses ensure_walk_prefetched, the non-urgent lane. That lane waits on the global fetch semaphore in FIFO order with FetchPriority::Low, the same queue as the speculative ring-baker downloads. Holtburger's own comment says this queue has starved player-blocking fetches for minutes. The first play of the UI table and of each creature table pays the same cost. _startVoice awaits _loadBuffer and then calls source.start(0) with no lateness check. So the first hit, footstep, spell or UI chime of a session (or after a teleport, during heavy streaming) arrives seconds later and plays out of sync with its event. The boot pack holds no waves and no sound tables. WebAC fixes this the retail way: it asks for a table's waves at background priority as soon as the table is read, and fetches a missing wave about one round trip late instead of not at all. The mechanism is confirmed in code; the size of the delay has not been measured.

SoundHook::UnPack 343069-343075 and SoundTweakedHook::UnPack (CreateSound at 343140) do the same. CreateSound 383707 builds SoundBufRef → SoundBuf. GetSound 383433-383458 only `find`s in sound_hash_, so nothing is loaded at play time.

These are single small records with a deadline, the same reasoning as the interior urgent lane. (2) Retail CreateSound analogue in Rust: in fetch_sound_table, after `SoundTable::unpack`, collect every SoundData variant's wave id and `spawn_local` a fire-and-forget low-lane `source.prefetch(&wave_keys)`. Prefetch bytes only, with no decode, so the 64 MB decoded-buffer LRU is not touched. Dedupe with a per-instance HashSet. Optionally hold it until boot settles (__bootState ready) so slow links stream terrain first. Optionally do the same for Sound/SoundTweaked hook wave ids when animations are decoded. (3) Optional: in AudioManager._startVoice, drop a non-loop voice whose buffer resolved more than about 400 ms after the play request, since retail never plays late. Use a default-on `?audioMaxLateMs` with an `=off` escape and count drops in stats. SoundHook::UnPack (343068, CreateSound at 343075) and SoundTweakedHook::UnPack (343123, CreateSound at 343140) do the same. CreateSound (383707) builds a SoundBufRef, whose constructor (383127) constructs a SoundBuf(gid), so the wave is loaded at that point. GetSound (383433) only looks the wave up in sound_hash_. Retail therefore never loads a wave at play time; that part is confirmed.

Holtburger, checked by symbol. The cited lib.rs line numbers are stale: lib.rs is being edited concurrently and moved about 25 lines between my reads. `fetch_wave` calls `prefetch::ensure_walk_prefetched(&source, &[key], |_| {})`, which is the non-urgent lane, and so does `fetch_sound_table`. prefetch.rs `run_walk_loop` sends non-urgent rounds to `source.prefetch`. manifest_source.rs `prefetch_impl` takes `fetch_sem.acquire()` for non-urgent fetches and uses `FetchPriority::Low` (lines ~944/956). Its own doc comment for `prefetch_urgent` (402-423) says the FIFO queue starved player-blocking fetches for minutes. audio_manager.js:710 `await this._loadBuffer(did)` → :761 `source.start(0)`, with no lateness check. entities.js:5642-5643 prewarms only `soundTableCache.get(stbDid)`. dat_shard.rs BOOT_ESSENTIAL_PORTAL_IDS (71-89) contains no Wave and no SoundTable. No wave prewarm exists anywhere in scene3d/plugins/app/src, and the ledgers and git log have no duplicate.

What does not hold as proposed:
(a) Part (2) uses the low lane, so on a cold boot it competes for the same fetch_sem permits and 6 HTTP/1.1 connections as ring streaming.
(b) The shard cache is unbounded by default (manifest_source.rs:314-317: budget usize::MAX), so every prefetched wave stays in wasm linear memory. All 786 waves come to roughly 41 MB raw: audio_manager.js says they decode to ~360 MB, at ~8.7x the DAT bytes.
(c) Part (3), dropping late voices, is an invented rule, not retail. Retail never needs it because it never loads late.

The scene3d wiring passes `fetchWave(did, true)` to the AudioManager, which only fetches a wave when it is about to play it. SoundTableCache now uses `fetchSoundTable(did, true)` when a `resolveSound` (play path) misses. If a play finds the table still queued by the entity-spawn prewarm, it races one urgent fetch against that fetch. The first table to land is installed and the other handle is freed. Waves are fetched on the normal lane, freed at once and never decoded. implementation.deviations:
1) The lane is chosen by an optional `urgent: Option<bool>` argument; Rust `fetch_wave` does not switch to urgent unconditionally. Absent means the old lane, the same convention as fetch_physics_script / fetch_particle_emitter. The default-on decision sits in the scene3d/index.js AudioManager wrapper, with an `?audioUrgentFetch=off` escape. This lets the prefetch queue keep using `fetchWave(did)` on the normal lane, and a stale pkg degrades silently (it ignores the extra argument).
2) Instead of a separate `fetchSoundTableUrgent` export, fetchSoundTable takes the same bool argument, so index.html's import list and init3D opts need no new plumbing. SoundTableCache also escalates: a play that finds the normal-lane spawn prewarm still in flight races one urgent fetch against it, and the first table to land wins. Without this, creature tables warmed at spawn would still play late.
3) Per the orchestrator, wavePrefetch is opt-in `=on`, not the verifier's default-on with an `=off` escape.
4) The boot gate reads `__sceneReadyEverFired` (or `__bootState==='ready'`), not only the `__bootState==='ready'` scalar. index.html documents that 'in-world' can overwrite 'ready' in that scalar.
5) There is no new bytes-only free-function export. The prefetch calls the existing `fetchWave(did)` and frees the WaveJs at once. The cost is a short-lived parse and RIFF copy in wasm memory; there is no decodeAudioData, and no index.html plumbing is needed. The byte budget counts `riffByteLength`, which is about the record size.
6) The Rust helper lives in wave.rs (a lane file) as a free function `holtburger_dat::file_type::wave::sound_table_wave_ids`, not as a SoundTable method in sound_table.rs. It is not re-exported from file_type/mod.rs.
7) scene3d/index.js was edited even though it is not on the listed lane files. These are three small additive hunks: the import, the AudioManager fetchWave wrapper, and the SoundTableCache opts plus `window.__wavePrefetch`. Without them nothing is wired up.
8) Part 3, the late-voice drop, was not implemented, per the verifier.

finding.title: ?audioRetailPan=on: the equal-power StereoPannerNode plays positional sounds up to 3 dB quieter than retail's DirectSound SetPan
finding.description: Retail SoundBuf::Play clamps the integer pan to ±15. When pan is non-zero it calls IDirectSoundBuffer::SetPan(100*pan): only the far channel is turned down by |pan| dB, the near channel stays at full level, and pan 0 leaves both channels at full level. In holtburger's opt-in retail mix every positional voice goes through a StereoPannerNode, including pan 0. stereoPositionFromPan only matches the left/right ratio. For a mono input, Web Audio's equal-power law gives each channel cos/sin(π/4) = 0.707 at centre, which is -3.01 dB. At full pan the loud side is 0.985 against retail's 1.0. Centred sounds (playFromCenter: UI, constant ambients) bypass the panner and play at full level. So the mix this mode exists to reproduce has positional sounds up to 3 dB low compared with centred ones: 3 dB for anything within 5 m or straight ahead or behind, less as the pan grows. WebAC builds the exact DirectSound law from a channel splitter/merger with per-channel gains, and skips panning when pan is 0. The default HRTF path is the owner's choice and is not affected.

SoundPlayer.ts:312 `if (pan) SoundPlayer.connectPanned(...) else source.connect(gainNode);`, :325-344 connectPanned (explicit stereo up-mix → ChannelSplitter → two GainNodes → ChannelMerger).
finding.holtburger_evidence: scene3d/audio/audio_manager.js:620-626 passes `pan: m.pan` (0 included) to _startVoice. :721-724 `if (!panner && pan != null && typeof this._ctx.createStereoPanner === "function") { panner = this._ctx.createStereoPanner(); panner.pan.value = stereoPositionFromPan(pan); }`. scene3d/audio/retail_mixer.js:112-121 stereoPositionFromPan: "an equal-power panner at position p gives right/left = tan((p+1)*pi/4)", which matches the ratio only. tests/audio_retail_mixer.test.mjs:133-149 checks only the position value, not the channel levels.

Volume is SetVolume(100*vol).

For pan ≠ 0 either (a) keep the StereoPannerNode and multiply `gain.gain.value` by 1/max(cos θ, sin θ) with θ = (p+1)π/4 when buf.numberOfChannels === 1, or (b) port WebAC's connectPanned graph (AGPL, attribute WebAC) for exact SetPan gains on mono and stereo buffers. Extend tests/audio_retail_mixer.test.mjs: pan 0 → no panner node; pan 15 → effective L/R = 0.178/1.0 within 1e-3. The HRTF default path is unchanged.

A non-zero pan builds this graph: voice gain (2 channels, 'explicit', 'speakers', so a mono wave up-mixes to both channels at 1.0) → ChannelSplitter(2) → per-channel GainNodes (far side 10^(-|pan|/20), near side 1.0) → ChannelMerger(2) → bus. This is exact for mono and stereo waves. The SetPan nodes are disconnected in onended and when the voice pool drops the voice. The pure gains live in a new `retailPanGains(pan)` export in retail_mixer.js, along with a `PAN_MAX = 15` constant. The play() handle gains an additive `setPan` field (null when unused). In retail mode `panner` is null; it is a StereoPannerNode only on a context with no splitter/merger, where the old equal-power fallback is kept. The HRTF default path is untouched: it passes `pan: null` and never reaches the new code, and a new test checks its node graph is unchanged.

finding.title: The MP3 wave 0x0A000393 is wrapped in a RIFF/WAVE container with format tag 0x55; browsers that only accept PCM WAV cannot decode it
finding.description: One end-of-retail wave, 0x0A000393, is stored as a bare MPEG-1 Layer III stream with a 30-byte header (WAVEFORMATEX format tag 0x0055). ACE treats Header[0] == 0x55 as mp3 and names this id in a comment. Holtburger's Wave docs assume every retail wave is PCM. to_riff_wav always writes a RIFF/WAVE/fmt chunk that claims tag 0x55 around the MP3 frames. Chrome's FFmpeg-based decoder may accept this. Firefox's WAV demuxer accepts only PCM, float, A-law and µ-law, so decodeAudioData fails there, the failure is cached as null, and that sound is silent for the session. Every engine decodes a raw MP3 stream, which is what WebAC passes. Only one wave is affected, so impact is low, and which sound uses it is unverified (no DAT loads in this phase).

(wave.data.buffer as ArrayBuffer) : wave.toWavBuffer();`. tests/verify-wave-mp3-decode.ts:4-19 (real-DAT scan: of 786 waves exactly one is MP3-flagged, 0x0A000393, 30-byte header, 5120 bytes of MP3 data).

finding.decomp_evidence: n/a. ACE /home/wbterminal/ace-server/Source/ACE.DatLoader/FileTypes/Wave.cs:33 `if (Header[0] == 0x55) ext = ".mp3";` and :61-63 comment "usually 18 bytes, with some exceptions notably objectID A000393 which is 30 bytes".
finding.proposed_change: In lib.rs fetch_wave, or in a new `Wave::to_browser_bytes()` in wave.rs, return the raw `data` bytes when `pcm_format().format_tag == 0x55`, otherwise to_riff_wav. Correct the wave.rs doc comment. Add a cargo unit test with a synthetic 0x55 header asserting the raw stream comes back. A JS-only alternative needs no wasm rebuild: in AudioManager._loadBuffer, if the RIFF fmt tag (bytes 20-21) is 0x55, pass the data-chunk payload to decodeAudioData.

verification.reasoning:
Mechanism confirmed. crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/wave.rs:47-51 assumes every wave is PCM, and `to_riff_wav` (139-156) always writes a RIFF/WAVE/fmt chunk carrying the record's own header. For a 0x55 wave that means a 30-byte MPEGLAYER3WAVEFORMAT fmt chunk around raw MP3 frames. lib.rs `fetch_wave` calls `wave.pcm_format()` and then `wave.to_riff_wav()` (checked by symbol; line numbers are stale). audio_manager.js:488-499 caches a decode failure as null; only FETCH failures retry after 30 s.

ACE Wave.cs:33 (`if (Header[0] == 0x55) ext = ".mp3"`) and its :61-63 comment name 0x0A000393 as the 30-byte exception. Even ACE's own export RIFF-wraps it, truncating the header to 16 bytes. WebAC Wave.ts:28-29 isMP3 and SoundPlayer.ts:257-260 pass the raw stream.

What does not stand: the impact. RIFF with tag 0x55 (MP3-in-WAV) is a legal container, and Chromium's FFmpeg wav demuxer plus mp3 decoder very likely decode it. Only PCM-only WAV demuxers (Firefox) fail, and the owner's test targets are Chromium. Which sound uses 0x0A000393 is unknown: no reference in holtburger docs or data, and no DAT loads were allowed in this phase. Value is low; the fix is cheap and safe.

implementation.summary:
I fixed six row-level bugs in the examine panel. It is a pure JS HUD text change, ships default-on with no flag, and needs no wasm rebuild. Each fix was checked against acclient.c.

(a) Workmanship now uses retail's adjective table (`rgWorkmanshipStrings` 0x8215FC from the 2013 bndb, via `InqWorkmanshipAdjective`). A plain item reads e.g. 'Utterly flawless (8)'. A salvage bag divides ItemWorkmanship by NumItemsInMaterial: 72/10 reads 'Flawless (7.20)' with a 'Salvaged from 10 items.' line under it (`Appraisal_ShowTinkeringInfo`).

(b, c) `bondedText` maps -2 to 'Destroyed on Death', -1 to 'Dropped on Death' and 1 to 'Bonded'. `attunedText` accepts 1 and 2. Both are emitted in retail's `Appraisal_ShowSpecialProperties` order, Attuned before Bonded.

(d) The Nether armor row now passes highlight bit 0x100 (`InqFloatEnchantmentMod` 0xA5). Vanilla ACE never sets that bit, so nothing changes against our server.

(e) `DAMAGE_TYPE_BITS` now says 'Electrical' and adds 0x10000000 'Prismatic' (`DamageTypeToString`).

(f) `protectionText` takes an optional `damageBit`. With a negative modifier and a bit given, it returns retail's per-type sentence plus '  (%.0f)', e.g. 'Your armor is flammable.  (-50)'. Without a bit it still returns 'Vulnerable (-50)', so the existing pin in test_examine_format.mjs:37 stays green. The armor-row label 'Electric' is left alone because `DamageResistanceToString` uses 'Electric: '.

(g) I removed the dead `hp.hook_type` debug row and the `hp`/`showHook` locals that only it used. HookProfile has only flags, valid_locations and ammo_type.

Start with ShowWeaponAndArmorData, ShowDefenseModData, ShowArmorMods, ShowCasterData and ShowActivationRequirements. In examine-target.js renderAppraisal, render these lines inside the existing 'Weapon'/'Armor'/'Magic' sections with the current kit kv/prose styling, so the look is unchanged and only the content grows. Default-on with a `?examineRetailText=off` escape. Tests: new test_appraisal_text.mjs with fixture snapshots (melee weapon with offense 1.15 and defense 1.2, caster with ManaConversionMod 0.08 and ElementalDamageMod 1.1, bow with maxVelocity, shield).

verification.reasoning:
Re-read examine-target.js:878-888. The weapon block shows Skill (tinted with weaponTone(0x0001)), Damage, Speed, and a 'Damage bonus' from damage_mod for ANY weapon. Line :931 shows 'Arcane Lore to activate'.

rg over plugins/app/ui finds no reads of weapon_offense, max_velocity, WeaponDefense, WeaponMissileDefense, WeaponMagicDefense, ManaConversionMod, ElementalDamageMod, ElementalDamageBonus, WeaponType or ItemSkillLevelLimit. WeaponProfile does carry weapon_offense and max_velocity (holtburger-protocol types.rs:209-220), and build_appraisal_snapshot (src/lib.rs:32838-32868) passes properties, weaponProfile and resistHighlight/resistColor to JS. ACE marks every one of these floats and ints [AssessmentProperty].

Decomp strings verified:
- Appraisal_ShowWeaponAndArmorData (acclient.c:231171): Base/Effective Shield Level, 'Skill: ' + ' (Sword)' etc., 'Damage Bonus: ', 'Elemental Damage Bonus: %d, %s.', 'Damage Modifier: %s.', 'Range: %d yds.%s', 'Bonus to Attack Skill: %s%d%%.', and the ammo lines.
- Appraisal_ShowCasterData (:231613): Mana Conversion, the 'Damage bonus for %s spells:' and ' vs. Monsters/Players' lines.
- Appraisal_ShowDefenseModData (:231730): Melee/Missile/Magic Defense.
- Appraisal_ShowActivationRequirements (:232724).
InqFloatEnchantmentMod maps 0x3E (WeaponOffense) to weapon bit 1 and 0x1D (WeaponDefense) to bit 2 (acclient.c:477525-477532). So holtburger's tint of the Skill row with bit 0x1 belongs on the Attack Skill line.

Additional retail detail the comparer did not state:
- 'Bonus to Attack Skill' is suppressed for missile launchers that use ammo: raised = (lm & 0x400000) && ammoType (acclient.c:231328-231330), test at :231563.
- 'Damage Modifier' prints only for launchers (`if (v9 && v39)`, ~:231467). holtburger's current 'Damage bonus' row on melee weapons is therefore non-retail; it is usually hidden only because damage_mod is 1.

The proposed `?examineRetailText=off` flag contradicts the project's HUD-fixes-skip-url-flag-gating rule and would need url-flags.md and lint registration. Drop it. No ledger entry covers this. WebAC ItemAppraisalText.ts:626-706 is correctly cited.

implementation.summary:
I added plugins/appraisal_text.js, a new DOM-free module with four line builders taken from acclient.c: weaponAndArmorLines (ItemExamineUI::Appraisal_ShowWeaponAndArmorData :231171), defenseModLines (:231730), casterLines (:231613) and activationRequirementLines (:232724), plus the retail formatters (ModifierToString, SmallModifierToString, %g, missile range, ClothingPriorityToString).

- The weapon builder prints "Skill: X (Sword)" with the WeaponType suffix and no tint. It prints "Damage:" (or "Damage Bonus:" with no damage types for a launcher that takes ammo), Elemental Damage Bonus, and Damage Modifier for ammo launchers only. Speed and Range (pow(v,2)*0.10204*1.094, capped at 85) only show when lm & 0x2500000. "Bonus to Attack Skill" uses weapon bit 0x1 and is skipped for ammo launchers.
- It also prints the ammunition lines, Base/Effective Shield Level (from the viewer's Shield skill, halved below specialized) and "Covers …" for armor and clothing.
- Tints use the decomp's InqFloatEnchantmentMod/InqIntEnchantmentMod bit map, including the resist bits 0x1000/0x2000 for the caster lines. They only apply when the IdentifyResponse carries the matching enchantment flag.

In examine-target.js, renderAppraisal now draws these lines inside the existing sections. Weapon/Armor gets the weapon, shield, ammo and covers lines, then the defense and caster lines. Magic gets "Activation requires …" in place of the old "Arcane Lore to activate" row. Value lines use the existing kv rows with tints; sentences use the existing prose rows. The bit-0x1 tint moved from the Skill row to the Attack Skill row, and the non-retail "Damage bonus" row for every weapon is gone.

All of this runs for items only, never for creatures or players. It ships on by default with no URL flag, since it is a HUD text fix.

implementation.eye_test:
On the 1070, off-screen, with ?nosw=1. Examine each of these and check the examine panel:
- A melee weapon with an attack/defense bonus. Weapon section reads "Skill: Heavy Weapons (Sword)" (untinted), "Damage 13.5 - 27, Slashing", "Speed …", "Bonus to Attack Skill +N%" (green under a Blood Drinker-type buff), "Bonus to Melee Defense +N.N%", and no "Damage bonus" row.
- A bow. "Damage Bonus", "Damage Modifier +N%", "Range NN yds." and "Uses arrows as ammunition." show; there is no Attack Skill line.
- A wand or orb. "Bonus to Mana Conversion", "Damage bonus for <type> spells:" and the vs. Monsters / vs. Players rows show under Weapon.
- A shield. Base and Effective Shield Level show above Armor Level.
- A piece of armor. A "Covers Chest, …" line shows.
- A high-level loot item. The Magic section shows "Activation requires Arcane Lore: N, …".
Pass criteria: no layout change apart from the extra rows, and no console errors.
implementation.deviations:
- The test plan pins "Bonus to Melee Defense: +20%." Retail Appraisal_ShowDefenseModData uses SmallModifierToString ("%c%.1lf%%", acclient.c:226492), so the line is "+20.0%." The test and code follow the decomp.
- The verifier says the activation skill comes from "ItemUseable skill". The decomp reads AppraisalItemSkill (int 0xB0 = 176), which ACE fills from ItemSkillLimit (AppraiseInfo.AddPropertyEnchantments), so I used that.
- Beyond the verifier's list (all taken from the same decomp function):
  - "Covers …" (ClothingPriorityToString :479868) for non-wieldable armor and clothing.
  - "This item can only be activated by <CraftsmanName | the original owner>." (end of ShowActivationRequirements).
  - Speed is gated on lm & 0x2500000, as retail does, so arrows and casters no longer show a Speed row.
- Holtburger-only fallback: an object with a weapon profile but no ValidLocations at all reads as a melee weapon, so its weapon lines still show. A known ValidLocations of 0 prints nothing, as in retail.
- Placement: caster lines go in the Weapon section after the defense mods, and activation lines go in the Magic section. Retail prints caster data after the requirements, but our panel groups by section.
- No escape flag, per the verifier and the HUD-fixes-skip-url-flag-gating rule.
- No code was copied from WebAC (cross-check only, noted in the module header).
implementation.follow_ups:
1. ORCHESTRATOR (needed before the gate passes): run `node scripts/gen-modulepreload.mjs` once after merging. index.html is stale for ./plugins/appraisal_text.js, which examine-target.js now imports statically, and for other lanes' ./scene3d/audio/wave_prefetch.js, fade_alpha_state.js, luminous_hook.js, surface_anim_flag.js and ./ui/hud_focus.js. Then bump the pinned non-app modulepreload count in harness/test_build_shell.mjs.
2. hookProfile.valid_locations is a bitflags-2 EquipMask, which serde_json writes as a name string ("MELEE_WEAPON | …"). JS cannot read a hooked item's ValidLocations, so the module only uses it when it is a number (GetHookedItemValidLocations parity is partial). Fix: serialize EquipMask in the snapshot as u32.
3. Possible bugs in the Rust assessment model (crates/holtburger-world/src/assessment.rs), noted and not fixed:
   - get_bonuses reads "Attack Bonus" from PropertyFloat::WeaponOffense before the WeaponProfile (retail reads only wap.weapon_offense) and does not suppress it for ammo launchers (acclient.c:231563).
   - ItemDifficulty is folded in as a wield "Skill: Arcane Lore" requirement (~:502). Retail prints it in "Activation requires …" (Appraisal_ShowActivationRequirements), and the model ignores ItemAllegianceRankLimit, HeritageGroup, ItemSkillLevelLimit+AppraisalItemSkill and the attribute/vital limits.
   - Elemental damage has no PvP line ((m−1)×0.25+1).
   - "Mana Conv" is hidden when the value is 0, but retail prints any value it receives.
4. examine-target.js still carries now-unused names: the imports skillName, damageTypeLabel, weaponSpeedText and damageRangeText, plus the consts wp, wh, wc and weaponTone. I left them to avoid touching the shared examine_format import block while other lanes edit it; they can be pruned after merging.
5. Other SetAppraiseInfo sections are still unported: ShowBoostValue, ShowHealKitValues, ShowCapacity, ShowLockAppraiseInfo, ShowManaStoneInfo, ShowRemainingUses, ShowUsageLimitInfo, ShowRatings and ShowSet.

finding.title: EoR item property lines missing: Set, Ratings + Vitality, the Properties line (slayer, imbues/rending, crushing/biting, armor/resistance cleaving, cast on strike, unenchantable, ivoryable/dyeable), Cleave, Cooldown, Item Level/XP, and the utility sections
finding.description:
Holtburger's 'Properties' section knows only Bonded/Attuned/IsSellable/Retained. Retail SetAppraiseInfo also prints the following, from properties ACE already sends:
- 'Set: <name>' (EquipmentSetId 265, a fixed name switch incl. the Sigil/Weave/Shrouded Soul families).
- 'Ratings: Dam N, Dam Resist N, Crit N, Crit Dam N, …, Life Resist N.' and 'This item adds N Vitality.' (GearDamage 370 … GearMaxHealth 379).
- 'You can only carry N of these items.' (Unique).
- 'Cooldown When Used: 1m 30s' / 'Cooldown Remaining:'.
- 'Cleave: N enemies in front arc.'
- 'Properties: <Creature> slayer, Multi-Strike, Critical Strike, Crippling Blow, Armor Rending, Slash/Pierce/…/Nether Rending, +1 Melee/Missile/Magic Defense, Phantasmal, Magic Absorbing, Unenchantable, Attuned, Bonded, Retained, Crushing Blow, Biting Strike, Armor Cleaving, Resistance Cleaving: <type>, Cast on Strike, Ivoryable, Dyeable', then 'This item cannot be further imbued.' and 'This item is tethered to the left side.'
- 'Item Level: L / Max' + 'Item XP: a / b' for Aetheria/cloaks (ItemTotalXpToLevel styles 1-3); holtburger shows only 'Item level cap'.
- 'This cloak has a chance to reduce an incoming attack by 200 damage.'
- 'Use requires level N.' / 'Use requires <Skill> of at least N.'
- Lock ('The lock looks <difficulty> to pick (Resistance N).'), mana stones ('Stored Mana', 'Efficiency', 'Chance of Destruction').
- 'Number of uses remaining: N', healing kits ('Bonus to Healing Skill', 'Restoration Bonus'), food ('Restores N Stamina when consumed.'), capacity, 'N of M pages full.', 'Rare #N' + rare-timer text, 'Created by X.', 'Destination: X'.
- Lifespan ('This item expires in …'), portal restriction lines, augmentation-gem XP cost.
- The LongDesc decoration ('<workmanship> <material> … , set with N <gems>').
Without these, the examine panel cannot tell a player what makes an EoR item valuable.

implementation.summary: Phase 1 of examine-text-6 is in. plugins/appraisal_text.js has four new pure line builders, each re-derived from acclient.c and cross-checked against WebAC ItemAppraisalText.ts. equipmentSetLines covers Appraisal_ShowSet: the full 119-entry InqInt(0x109) switch, including the folded retired Weave ids. ratingLines covers Appraisal_ShowRatings in retail order, with Crit Dam before Crit Resist, followed by "This item adds N Vitality.". specialPropertyLines covers Appraisal_ShowSpecialProperties: Unique with commas, "Cooldown When Used" through a ClientUISystem::DeltaTimeToString port, an optional "Cooldown Remaining" hook, "Cleave" when the count is above 1, the comma-joined "Properties: ..." line in AppendHelper order, "This item cannot be further imbued." and "This item is tethered to the left side.". The Properties line covers slayer and Bael'Zharon's Hate, Multi-Strike (AttackType & 0x79E0), the 15 imbue bits (Nether between Acid and Cold, 0x80000000 = Phantasmal), Magic Absorbing, Unenchantable (>= 9999), Attuned/Bonded, Retained, Crushing Blow, Biting Strike, Armor Cleaving, "Resistance Cleaving: <type>", Cast on Strike (DID 55), Ivoryable and Dyeable. itemLevelLines covers Appraisal_ShowItemLevelInfo: it ports ExperienceSystem::ItemTotalXPToLevel/ItemLevelToTotalXP for styles 1-3 using Number math, prints "Item Level: L / Max" and "Item XP: a / b", and adds the CloakWeaveProc 2 sentence. In plugins/examine-target.js these render default-on with no URL flag, following the HUD-fixes-skip-url-flag-gating rule: a "Set & Ratings" block above the Weapon/Armor section, and a Properties section moved ahead of Requirements to follow SetAppraiseInfo order. The Properties section uses retail's lines in place of the old " · " list, and its "Cannot be sold" word is now retail's sentence "This item cannot be sold.". The Item Level / Item XP rows sit in Requirements. All of this applies to items only, never to creatures or players.
implementation.eye_test: There is no flag; this is the default path. Use the 1070 off-screen with ?nosw=1. 1) Examine an EoR loot weapon from your inventory (spawn one with an imbue, a slayer, a set and gear ratings if you can). A "Set & Ratings" section should sit above the Weapon section, showing a "Set" row with a set name and a "Ratings" row such as "Dam 3, Crit 2". 2) The Properties section should come before Requirements. It should show "Cooldown When Used" and "Cleave" rows where they apply, then one prose line "Properties: Olthoi slayer, Slash Rending, ..." with no " · " separators, then "This item cannot be further imbued.". 3) Examine an Aetheria or a cloak. Requirements should show "Item Level 2 / 5" and "Item XP 3,500,000,000 / 7,000,000,000"-style rows and no "Item level cap". A cloak with the damage-reduction proc should also show the 200-damage sentence. 4) Examine a quest item that cannot be sold. Its Properties section should end with "This item cannot be sold.". Pass: rows use the kit kv/prose styling, long Properties lines wrap inside the panel without horizontal overflow, the console shows no errors, and creature and player examines are unchanged.
implementation.deviations: 1) The Item Level lines go into the existing Requirements section, not a block of their own. The old "Item level cap" row stays as a fallback, but only for an item that has ItemMaxLevel and no XP curve. tests/examine_wield_requirements.test.mjs pins `row("Item level cap", itemLevelCap)` in that block and I may not edit existing tests. Retail would print nothing in that case. 2) The "Set & Ratings" block sits above the combined Weapon/Armor/Craftsmanship section, because the tinkering rows live inside that section. As a result, Set and Ratings show before the tinkering rows, whereas retail prints tinkering first. 3) examine-target.js passes `attuned: attunedText(ints.Attuned), bonded: bondedText(ints.Bonded)` into specialPropertyLines through opts. tests/examine_text_rows.test.mjs pins those exact calls, in that order, in examine-target.js. Without opts, the builder computes the same words from the property bag. 4) The lockbox and mana-stone fixtures in the test plan belong to Phase 2 (ShowLockAppraiseInfo / ShowManaStoneInfo), which the orchestrator deferred, so I did not write them. 5) Material names (MaterialType) were not needed: they are used only by the ShowDescription LongDesc decoration, which is Phase 3. 6) specialPropertyLines supports "Cooldown Remaining" through opts.cooldownRemaining(sharedCooldownId), but the panel does not wire it yet; see follow_ups. 7) "This item cannot be sold." closes the Properties block. Retail prints it later in SetAppraiseInfo, after Craftsman. 8) The Properties section is now gated to items, as in retail ItemExamineUI. It used to render for creatures too.
implementation.follow_ups:
- Phase 2 (deferred): ShowUsageLimitInfo, plus Boost, HealKit, Capacity, Lock, ManaStone, RemainingUses, Craftsman and Rare info, with the lockbox and mana-stone fixture tests from the verifier's test_plan.
- Phase 3 (deferred): the ShowDescription extras, namely lifespan, the portal restriction bitmask, and the LongDesc workmanship/material/gem decoration (needs MaterialType names).
- "Cooldown Remaining": wire opts.cooldownRemaining in examine-target.js. Enchantment startTime is relative at receipt, so it needs the hotbar's receipt-time bookkeeping (hotbar.js cdReceivedAt + inventory_helpers matchCooldownEnchantment) moved into a shared helper. Otherwise the remaining time would be stale.
- Drop the non-retail "Item level cap" fallback once the pin in tests/examine_wield_requirements.test.mjs is updated.
- Drop the attuned/bonded opts pass-through once the pin in tests/examine_text_rows.test.mjs moves.
- Usage ("Use" section) still renders after Requirements. Retail Appraisal_ShowUsage comes between SpecialProperties and LevelLimit.
- examine-text-7 plans its own DeltaTimeToString port (Time in Dereth); dedupe it with appraisal_text.js deltaTimeToString.
- Bugs in crates/holtburger-world/src/assessment.rs (CLI model, not fixed here):
  - Effect::from_object maps IgnoreArmor (float 155) to "Armor Rending". Retail prints "Armor Cleaving" for it; "Armor Rending" is imbue bit 0x4.
  - The ResistanceModifier cleaving element is taken from the weapon's damage type. Retail uses ResistanceModifierType (int 263): "Resistance Cleaving: <type>".
  - Slayer requires SlayerDamageBonus > 0. Retail needs only SlayerCreatureType, and type 31 reads "Bael'Zharon's Hate".
  - Multistrike tests DoubleStrike|TripleStrike. Retail tests AttackType & 0x79E0.
  - Cleaving uses > 0. Retail uses > 1.
  - The label "Magic Absorption" should be retail's "Magic Absorbing".
  - Biting Strike and Crushing Blow require the value to be > 0. Retail checks presence only.
- ACE ExperienceSystem's FixedPlusBase (style 3) curve differs from retail's scheme 3 (acclient.c:499244). Both Aetheria and cloaks use style 2 in LSD, so there is no visible effect today.

finding.description:
For a player or templated NPC, retail CharExamineUI fills a misc-info list under the stat rows. ACE builds every field (AppraiseInfo.cs:352-389 and AddRatings :586-610).
- 'Society: Radiant Blood ~ Knight', coloured green for the viewer's own society and red for a rival.
- 'Alleg. Monarch: N Followers', or 'Monarch:' / 'Patron:' / 'Monarch/Patron:'; the allegiance name line; the window title prefixed with the allegiance rank title.
- The armor block 'Head/Chest/Groin  AL: a/b/c' with '*' marking unenchantable (≥ 9999).
- 'Dmg/CritDmg Rating: d/cd', 'Dmg/CritDmg Resist: …', 'DoT/Life: Resist: …'.
- 'Fellowship:', 'Arrived in Dereth:' (DateOfBirth), 'Time in Dereth:' (Age as 'Nmo Nd Nh Nm Ns'), 'Chess Rank:', 'Fishing Skill:', 'Deaths:' / 'Has never died', 'Titles Earned:', and the '* = Unenchantable' legend.
A plain creature appraisal also gets the ratings block. Retail picks the character page whenever the appraisal has PropertyString 5 (Template) or PropertyInt 0x105 (CharacterTitleId), so templated NPCs get heritage/title lines. Holtburger decides only by the ODF PLAYER bit, shows heritage/gender/title/PK/level plus the attribute block, and drops all the misc lines.

implementation.summary: The examine panel now shows retail's misc-info list under the attribute block, re-derived from acclient.c CharExamineUI::SetAppraiseInfo (:233437), CreatureExamineUI::SetAppraiseInfo (:233213) and ClientUISystem::DeltaTimeToString (:403033); WebAC CreatureAppraisalText.ts was used only as a cross-check. New pure helpers in examine_format.js: examineSubPage, deltaTimeToString, armorCell, societyRankSuffix, societyRow, allegianceRows, allegianceNameText, characterArmorRows, creatureRatingRows and characterMiscRows. The row builders return {key,label,value,tone}, plus blank separator rows and a note row for the '* = Unenchantable' legend. Character pages get a 'Character' section in retail order. It has Society (green for the viewer's own society, red for a rival; the viewer's Faction1Bits comes from objectIntProperty(localGuid, 281)), the Alleg. Monarch / Monarch / Patron / Monarch/Patron rows, the Head/Chest/Groin 'AL: a/b/c' rows with '*N', the Dmg/CritDmg and DoT/Life ratings, Fellowship, Arrived and Time in Dereth, Chess Rank, Fishing Skill, Deaths / Has never died, Titles Earned and the legend. Plain creatures get a 'Ratings' section. Dispatch now follows gmExaminationUI::SetAppraiseInfo (:228878): a creature appraisal that carries Template (string 5) or CharacterTitleId (int 0x105) goes to the character page even without the PLAYER description bit, and also gets the CharExamineUI PK line. The header now adds the allegiance name (m_displayText_AllegianceName) under the PK line and uses Template as the Profession fallback. This is a HUD-only text and layout change with no world-rendering impact, shipped default-on without a flag (HUD-fixes-skip-url-flag-gating; the verifier proposed no flag).

implementation.eye_test:
No flag is needed (default-on HUD change); use ?nosw=1. Examine four targets.
(1) Another player in an allegiance and a society. Expect a 'Character' section after Attributes: 'Society: Radiant Blood ~ Knight' (green if you are in the same society, red if you are in a rival one); the monarch/patron rows; then after a small gap 'Head/Chest/Groin  AL: a/b/c' (×3, with '*N' for all-unenchantable locations). Next come the Dmg/CritDmg rating lines (only when that player has ratings), then Fellowship / Arrived in Dereth / Time in Dereth ('1mo 2d 3h 4m 5s'), Deaths ('Has never died' when 0), Titles Earned, and '* = Unenchantable' last. The header should show the allegiance name under the PK line, and there should be no 'Armor by Location' grid for players.
(2) A templated town NPC (e.g. Holtburg Town Crier or a shopkeeper). Expect a 'Character Level' box, the template text as the title line, 'Non-Player Killer', the paperdoll leading, and a Character section (at least the legend).
(3) A monster with ratings. Expect a 'Ratings' section with 'Dmg/CritDmg  Rating: d/cd' and/or 'DoT/Life:  Resist: a/b', and no Character section.
(4) Pass criteria: no raw ids or hex, no console errors, and nothing in the 3D world changes.
implementation.deviations:
1. armorCell(10000) returns '*1', not the verifier's '*10000'. The decomp prints sprintf("*%d", v - 9999) (acclient.c:233938), and ACE ArmorLevel.cs adds 9999 to an all-unenchantable location. Tests pin '*1', '*0' and '*100'.
2. NumDeaths 0 or below gives 'Has never died', but an ABSENT NumDeaths gives no Deaths row. Retail prints the line only when InqInt(0x2B) succeeds, and ACE drops NumDeaths when AllowOthersToSeeYourNumberOfDeaths is off, so 'Has never died' would be false there. The verifier's test plan said 'or absent'.
3. The test cases are in a new file, tests/examine_character_misc.test.mjs, instead of test_examine_format.mjs, because existing tests must not be edited. They cover every test_plan case and add fake-DOM panel tests.
4. On the character page the body-location armor appears as retail's three 'AL: a/b/c' rows inside the Character section, and the 'Armor by Location' grid is skipped. For other creatures (ACE also sends ArmorLevels for non-attackable NPCs) the grid stays, with armorCell '*N' values (plain %d now, no thousands comma) and a '* = Unenchantable' note when any cell is starred.
5. The allegiance name goes in the header (CharExamineUI m_displayText_AllegianceName), not as a misc row.
6. The window-title allegiance rank prefix is not done; the verifier marked it optional because the title table is missing.
7. The header Profession line got a Template fallback (retail: CharacterTitleTable name, else Template). The CharacterTitleId-to-name lookup is not wired.
8. A templated NPC routed to the character page also gets the CharExamineUI PK line (pkStatusText of its description bits, stored as model.pkOdf).
9. The creature-only rating block uses the section title 'Ratings'. kvRow gained tones 'ok' and 'warn' (classes is-ok / is-warn, which colour the label and value, as retail's AddLineToMiscInfo does).
implementation.follow_ups:
1. identify.rs:51 merges appraisal properties into the entity instead of replacing them, and ACE sends rating ints only when they are non-zero. A rating that drops to 0 between appraisals therefore leaves a stale 'Dmg/CritDmg Rating' line, and the same goes for Fellowship or AllegianceName after leaving. The new rows read the merged bag, so this area_missed_notes #6 issue is now user-visible.
2. Retail AppraisalSystem::InqGenderHeritageDisplay (acclient.c:480424) prints gender then heritage ('Female Aluvian') and falls back to the creature-type name when HeritageGroup is 0. examineHeaderModel prints 'Aluvian Female' (pinned by test_examine_format.mjs:122) and has no creature-type fallback.
3. The window title should be AllegianceData::GetFullName (rank title + name). That needs the AllegianceSystem::GetTitle heritage x gender x rank table, which nothing in JS or Rust has.
4. CharacterTitleId to name: character-info.js has a partial, unexported TITLE_NAMES (ids 1-30), and the CharacterTitle StringTable 0x2300000E is not wired. The examine header falls back to Template, which is retail's behaviour when the lookup fails.
5. Retail CreatureExamineUI never shows ArmorLevels, but we still show the 'Armor by Location' grid for non-character NPCs.
6. On a failed assess retail still runs CharExamineUI (so the legend at least is printed). We skip the misc list because the failed snapshot has empty properties.
7. crates/holtburger-world/src/assessment.rs has no character or creature misc-info model, so there was nothing to cross-check and no bug to note there.

finding.title: No retail 'Character Information' report (gmCharacterInfoUI): Born/Played/Deaths, Natural/Drain resistances + Regeneration tiers, innate attributes, masteries, luminance auras, gem augmentations, burden penalty
finding.description:
Retail's Character Information panel (gmCharacterInfoUI, one scrolling text element) is how a player sees their augmentations, masteries, luminance auras and creation stats. Holtburger's character view has only Attributes/Skills/Titles tabs, and nothing else in the web client shows these.
- 'Born on …', 'Played …', deaths.
- 'Natural Resistances / Drain Resistances / Regeneration Bonus' tiers from base Str+End and Str+2·End (None/Poor/Mediocre/Hardy/Resilient/Indomitable at 200/260/320/380/440 and 200/346/470/580/690).
- Innate attributes (the creation values).
- Chess rank / fishing skill.
- Melee/Ranged/Summoning mastery names.
- The Luminance Augmentations block (base/spec damage, reduction, crit, surge, mana use/gain ×5, healing, skilled craft/spec, all skills).
- Every gem augmentation the character owns (attribute +N×, resistances, spec tinkering, extra pack slot, carrying capacity, death-item loss, spells past death, crit defense, bonus XP/salvage/imbue, faster regen, spell duration, Infused schools, Skilled melee/missile/magic, damage bonus/resist, crit expertise/power, Jack of All Trades).
- The load line (unburdened, or 'N burden over, −P% …').
All strings are StringTable 0x23000001 ID_CharacterInfo_* tokens. Holtburger already loads string tables (ui/ac_strings.js) and exposes PropertyInt reads (objectIntProperty).

Build it from a new pure plugins/character_info_report.js: `buildCharacterInfoReport({prop, rawAttr, innateAttr, strength, str})`, re-derived from the decomp Update* order. implementation.summary: The character pane now has a fourth "Info" tab. It shows the text of retail's Character Information panel (gmCharacterInfoUI) in place of the stat template, under the title "Character Information". The text comes from a new pure module, plugins/character_info_report.js, which follows the decomp's gmCharacterInfoUI::Update order: born / played / deaths, then resistance and regeneration tiers from raw Str+End and Str+2·End, innate attributes, chess rank (default 1400) and fishing skill (default 0), melee / ranged / summoning mastery, the luminance header and auras (values above 5 split into base 5 plus a Seer remainder; mana use and gain ×5, skilled spec ×2), every gem augmentation in the decomp's order, and the burden line (buffed strength through EncumbranceCapacity / Load / LoadMod, plus the Seventh Mule line). ui/ac_strings cannot fill these templates because the wasm fetch_string_table export keeps only each template's first fragment. So all StringTable 0x23000001 templates are embedded verbatim, read straight from client_local_English.dat with a small Python DAT reader. A script confirmed 74 of 74 match the DAT exactly. Only Resist_Nether is not in the DAT; it has hand-written fallback wording. The panel reads the local player's ints through the existing objectIntProperty(playerGuid, id) and attributes from the stats stride: raw = base, buffed = current, innate = attributeXp start, or base − ranks on an older pkg. The builder is loaded with a dynamic import on first use, so the existing spliced tests need no new stub and the modulepreload block does not change. The text refreshes on playerStatsUpdated and once a second while the tab is open, and the DOM is written only when the text changes. No Rust, wasm, flag or rynth changes.

implementation.eye_test:
No URL flag; this is default-on HUD (main panel only, no world-render change). In-world, press F1 and click the new "Info" tab (4th, narrow). Check:
(1) The strip fits at 300px: "ATTRIBUTES" is not clipped, and Info sits at its natural width.
(2) The panel title reads "Character Information". The header, XP meter, list and raise footer are hidden, and one scrolling text block shows.
(3) Text order: born date as M/d/yyyy h:mm:ss AM/PM (when the server sent CreationTimestamp), "You have played for …", the deaths line; blank line; Natural/Drain Resistances + Regeneration Bonus; Innate Strength…Self; Chess Rank (1400 default) / Fishing Skill; "Luminance Augmentations:" plus any auras/augs; the burden line.
(4) Pick up items past capacity: within about 1 s the last line changes to "overburdened by N burden units … by P%".

implementation.deviations:
Verifier test plan, corrected against the decomp:
- "Str 100/End 100 → regen Mediocre" is wrong. Str+2·End = 300 is not above 0x15A (346), so retail prints "Poor"; the test pins Poor.
- "Str 200/End 245 → Indomitable/Indomitable" contradicts the >690 edge the verifier also cites: 200+2·245 = 690 → "Resilient". The test pins 200/245 → Indomitable/Resilient and 201/245 → Indomitable/Indomitable.

Strings:
- ac_strings could not resolve the templates (fetch_string_table returns fragment 0 only), so per the orchestrator note the English templates are embedded. They are DAT-verbatim, not invented.
- The one exception is ID_CharacterInfo_Augmentation_Resist_Nether. Retail requests it but the EoR DAT has no entry, so its wording copies the sibling lines.
- No compute_str_hash port was added at runtime. An optional src.str(token, values) hook is there for a future DAT-backed resolver.

Ways this differs from WebAC (decomp wins):
- Chess and fishing always show, with defaults 1400 / 0.
- The Load_Augmentations (Seventh Mule) line is emitted.
- The burden penalty uses retail truncation: 10·(10 − trunc(LoadMod·10)).
- The played duration follows ID_DurationFormat: years / months (30 d) / weeks / days / hours / minutes / seconds, space-separated. I trimmed the leading space the retail template leaves when years = 0.

Info button tag:
- The Info button carries data-pane="info", not data-tab. The existing tests/character_info_tab_labels.test.mjs pins exactly three data-tab buttons, and editing existing tests was not allowed.
- The builder module is loaded with a dynamic import, so the existing spliceModule tests need no new stub.
implementation.follow_ups:
1. The wasm fetch_string_table export (src/lib.rs ~15245) serializes only `v.strings.first()`. That loses every later StringInfo fragment and the variable list. A new additive export returning [[key, [fragments], [varHashes]]] would let this report, and any other StringInfo user, read the DAT instead of embedded English. finding.title: Retail icon composite missing in vendor/trade/salvage/tinker/house windows and the buffs HUD; composeLayers is not Blit_3Alpha/Blit_4Alpha
finding.description: Bug 12 (2026-10-07) added retail IconData::RenderIcons, but only inventory, container, corpse, hotbar and drag use it. Every commerce_window slot goes through fillSlotIcon, which draws the RAW DAT icon: no item-type backdrop, no underlay or overlay, and the exact-white key outline is not replaced. These are the "white boxes" that bug 12 fixed elsewhere, still showing in the vendor list, trade wells, salvage list, tinker slots and house payment wells. The buffs HUD (and spell-research-panel) draw raw spell icons too. Retail's effects list (EffectInfoRegion) uses ClientMagicSystem::GetSpellIcon, which runs CompositeSpellIcon: power-component backing, white → Reversed/NonReversed tile, self/fellow overlay. Separately, composeLayers uses a single float alpha-over for every layer. Retail draws the overlay with FourChannelAlpha, which copies src when the destination alpha is 0 and is a non-premultiplied "over" otherwise. Holtburger's version gives `out.rgb = src*sa + dst.rgb*(1-sa)`, which darkens anti-aliased overlay pixels that lie over transparent icon pixels. That colour is then attenuated again when the drag icon is blended over the backdrop, which leaves a dark fringe on IconOverlay edges.

Blend: ui/ac_icon_compose.js:155-179 composeLayers does `out.rgb = src*sa + dst*(1-sa)`. Retail FourChannelAlpha (BlitLoopNoScale__BlitOp_FourChannelAlpha_ARGB_ARGB_1, acclient.c:642714-642840) writes src unchanged when the dst alpha byte is 0 (`if (*(_DWORD*)v7 >> 24)` guards the blend) and when the src alpha is 255. It lerps rgb when dst alpha is 255, and otherwise does a non-premultiplied over: out = dst - (dst-src)*sa'/outA', outA' = sa'+da'-sa'*da'/256. So the darkening is real, but it is limited: it hits only anti-aliased IconOverlay pixels over transparent icon pixels. Background, underlay and drag-over-opaque produce the same results as today, give or take ±1 rounding.

finding.title: House data is never queried at login, so the map 'Your house' marker and the house panel stay empty
finding.description: Retail CPlayerSystem::InitializePlayer ends with CM_House::Event_QueryHouse. ACE answers with HouseData (0x225, the owner's house position, types and payments) or HouseStatus (0x226 BadParam, no house). That is how gmMapUI shows the 8x8 "Your House" icon from the moment of login, and why the House page is filled before anyone opens it. Holtburger sends HouseQuery only when the player presses "Query House" in the house panel. Until then the house panel says "Not looked up yet — press Query House.", and map-panel.js, which reads playerHouseData() for the house icon, never draws the owner's marker. ACE never pushes HouseData on its own (HandleActionQueryHouse is called only after buy, rent or abandon), so most sessions never get the data. HouseStatus is a silent snapshot in holtburger (lib.rs:32395-32397), so an automatic query adds no chat line for players without a house.

implementation.summary: The client now sends HouseQuery (0x021E) once at login, as retail does: CPlayerSystem::InitializePlayer (acclient.c:400740) ends with CM_House::Event_QueryHouse (:400811) right after LoginComplete. Before this, the only houseQuery() caller was the House panel's button, and ACE never pushes HouseData by itself. A new module, app/house_query_login.js, holds houseQueryAtLoginEnabled(search) (default ON; `?houseQueryAtLogin=off/0/false` turns it off) and maybeQueryHouseAtLogin(handle). That function keeps a WeakSet of handles that already asked, so it sends once per SessionHandle: death respawns, teleports and repeat kind=7 events send nothing, while a relog or session takeover (a new handle) asks again. It is a no-op for a stale pkg/ without houseQuery and never throws; a closed command channel is caught and warned once. app/client_events.js calls it from the kind=7 ENTERED_WORLD arm, after the evtGuard movement-gate flip and the login portal-space request, with `window.__sessionHandle ?? handle` (the same choice as the rynth auto-boot), inside its own try/catch. The wasm queues kind=7 on PlayerCreate after it has sent LoginComplete, so the order matches retail. The wasm HouseStatus arm only stores a snapshot, so a character without a house gets no chat line. No Rust or wasm change.

finding.title: Secure trade: a dropped pack is offered whole (retail offers its contents), and equipped items are wrongly refused
finding.description: Retail gmSecureTradeUI::AddItem lists an object only when it has no contained items and no contained containers. For a pack with contents it shows the 0x1a notice "Trading contents of <name>" and adds each contained item. Nested non-empty packs are skipped, and the pack itself is never offered unless it is empty. Holtburger sends addToTrade(packGuid, 0) for whatever is dropped. ACE accepts it (Player_Trade.HandleActionAddToTrade has no container check), so the player gives away the bag along with its contents, and the partner sees one opaque pack instead of the items. Separately, offerItem refuses equipped items with an invented "Unequip X before trading it". Retail DragItemAcceptable only requires IsOwnedByPlayer, which covers wielded items, and ACE explicitly falls back to GetEquippedItem. Salvage already walks packs (salvage-panel.js addFromDrop), so trade is the inconsistent panel.

finding.title: Spell bar has no endowment icon: wielded casters with a built-in spell can't be selected/cast from the bar
finding.description: Retail gmSpellcastingUI::UpdateEndowmentIcon checks the item at the Held location (0x1000000). If its ItemType has the Caster bit (0x8000) and its PublicWeenieDesc _spellID is set, a 32x32 endowment icon appears at the left of the spell bar: the spell icon as underlay, the item's drag icon as overlay, a selected overlay, and the tooltip "%s (%hs)\nDouble-click to cast this spell". It becomes the default selection when no spell is selected, and the Next/Prev/First/Last walks include it. With it selected, Cast runs ItemHolder::UseObject(endowmentItem, 1, 1), which sends UseWithTarget on the selected target. ACE implements this server side: Player_Use.cs:60-89 casts `sourceItem.SpellDID` on the target. Holtburger's spell bar has no such slot, so built-in caster spells can only be reached through generic inventory use. Holtburger already has everything the slot needs: PropertyDataId::Spell is hydrated from the PWD (crates/holtburger-world/src/hydration.rs:149-151) and readable via objectDataIdProperty(guid, 28), and the item composite (drag) and spell composite icons exist.

implementation.summary: I added retail's spell-bar endowment cell (gmSpellcastingUI m_endowmentIcon, acclient.c:247815). It is a cell placed ahead of slot 1 on the magic-stance spell strip, and it appears when the Held item (0x1000000) is a Caster (ItemType 0x8000) with a PWD spell id (PropertyDataId 28). It shows the spell composite under the item's drag icon (two background layers) with retail's tooltip "%s (%hs)\nDouble-click to cast this spell". The rules live in a new module, ui/ac_spell_endowment.js: findEndowment, the selection walk, the UseObject cast decision, texts and the flag. Small glue functions in the same module read the inventory and DIDs, build the icons, and cast. That cast goes through the shared 0.2 s use throttle, then sends useWithTarget, useObject or showTransientLine. plugins/combat-bar.js uses it as follows. The endowment auto-selects when no bar spell is selected (UpdateEndowmentIcon). It joins the Del/PgDn/Ctrl walks as [endowment, 0..N-1] with wrap (RecvNotice_*SpellSelection). With it selected, Cast/End/double-click runs ItemHolder::UseObject(item,1,1): it sends UseWithTarget(item, selected target) and ACE casts the SpellDID. With no target it shows the 0x1A line "Select your target before using the X", and right-click examines the item. The current-spell well shows the endowment while it is selected. combat-bar.js loads the module with a dynamic import. A new static import would break tests/combat_bar_skill_stride.test.mjs, which splices the module with explicit per-import stubs and which I may not edit. The cell ships default-ON under the HUD rule, with the `?spellbarEndowment=off` escape. With the flag off, or with no held caster, the cell stays display:none and every selection and Cast path is unchanged.

implementation.deviations:
1. findEndowment follows retail exactly: it takes THE object at the Held location, then rejects it if it is not a caster or has no spell. The verifier's version took the first row matching all three tests. Only one item can be Held, so the two agree in practice; the decomp wins.
2. "Targeted" comes from the item's ItemUseable (ItemUses::IsUseable_Targeted, `& 0xFFFF0000`), as UseObject does, not from the spell. I also ported UseObject's USEABLE_NO branch ("The %s cannot be used") and its 0.2 s m_timeLastUsed gate, using the shared consumeUseThrottle from scene3d/target_cycle.js.
3. combat-bar.js loads the helper with a dynamic import, not a static one. tests/combat_bar_skill_stride.test.mjs splices combat-bar.js with an explicit stub for every static import and fails on a new one, and existing tests may not be edited. sneak-hud.js already uses this pattern.
4. Two additions beyond the verifier's change, both from retail ListenToElementMessage :249263: double-click casts (message 10) and right-click examines the item via `window.__showExamineFor` (message 8). The existing current-spell well (BuiltInSpell position) also shows the endowment while it is selected.

finding.title: Failure codes retail never prints still reach chat: 'I teleported.' after every portal and 'Turbine chat is enabled.' at every login
finding.description:
Retail HandleFailureEvent's switch default prints nothing, and both Handle_Communication__WeenieError and ...WithString call it directly. holtburger runs its silence check (0x3B/0x3C only) on the UseDone path alone. The WeenieError arm has no silence check, so every unknown code goes to the PascalCase-to-sentence fallback as a System chat line. On vanilla ACE this happens all the time:
(a) Portal.cs:289 sends SendWeenieError(ITeleported 0x3C) after every portal use, so 'I teleported.' is printed.
(b) Player_Networking.cs:88 sends TurbineChatIsEnabled 0x51D at every login (use_turbine_chat defaults to true, PropertyManager.cs:608), so 'Turbine chat is enabled.' is printed.
(c) About 34 ACE-emitted codes have no retail case at all (checked against WebAC's 344-code table), for example TradeNonCombatMode 0x455 (Player_Trade.cs:65) -> 'Trade non combat mode.', and TradeItemBeingTraded 0x453 via UseDone (Player_Use.cs:126) -> 'Trade item being traded.'. Others include NoPhysicsObject, GeneralMovementFailure, SkillTooLow, TradeClosed, TradeAlreadyTrading, FellowshipIgnoringRequests, LevelTooLow and ContractError.
This re-raises the round-2 use-3 correction (5), 'keep the sentence-case fallback for unknown codes so non-retail ACE codes stay visible'. New evidence: that decision assumed the fallback only fires for rare unknown codes. In fact it fires on every portal use and every login, and 0x51D appears nowhere in acclient.c. WebAC's generated table also matches the decomp's case count, so 'retail has no case for this code' can be decided exactly. Owner call on how far to go.

Only the UseDone arm checks silence (:920 `None if holtburger_core::errors::is_silent_failure(`). crates/holtburger-core/src/errors.rs:45-47 `matches!(error, WeenieError::ILeftTheWorld | WeenieError::ITeleported)`; :376-389 is the fallback ('Convert the enum name "PascalCase" to "Sentence case"'). verification.reasoning:
I re-read the cited code and it holds. In holtburger's game_event.rs, the WeenieError arm (now about :1002-1070) pushes format_weenie_error(...) as a kind=2 line for every code outside spellcast_error_text. The WeenieErrorWithString arm (:1071-1091) does the same. Neither calls is_silent_failure; only the UseDone arm does (:920). errors.rs:45-47 silences only ILeftTheWorld and ITeleported. Neither ITeleported nor TurbineChatIsEnabled has a template (they appear only in is_actually_weenie_error, :412-424), so the PascalCase fallback (:376-389) prints 'I teleported.' and 'Turbine chat is enabled.'. app/client_events.js:121-160 appends every kind=2 line, filtered only by the chat hook, and I found no JS filter on 0x3C or 0x51D.

Player_Networking.cs:85-88 sends TurbineChatIsEnabled when use_turbine_chat is on. finding.description:

finding.title: HearRangedSpeech ignores the wire range: NPC ranged Say emotes are shown out to ACE's 96 m broadcast instead of the emote's Extent
finding.description: ACE broadcasts an NPC's ranged Say emote to everyone within LocalBroadcastRange (96 m) but writes the emote's much smaller Extent into the message's range field. The retail client enforces that range itself: HandleRangedTalkEvent shows the line only when ObjectsInRange(player, sender, range) passes. That is a 3D centre distance <= range, and it fails when the sender object is unknown. holtburger parses the range but never uses it, so town and quest NPC chatter from far beyond the intended radius fills the chat log and the speech bubbles. This was deferred under chat-6 ('its range gate is not ported'). WebAC adds the ACE evidence (96 m broadcast vs Extent) and a working implementation. The same chat-6 deferral also covers CanHear's radar gate, which drops HearSpeech and emotes from known senders beyond 75 m outdoors or 25 m indoors (2D) and could go in the same patch. That part is optional and is mentioned only because it is the same code site; WebAC has no new evidence for it.

Usable helper: crates/holtburger-common/src/position.rs:238 `Position::distance_to`, already used for range checks at src/lib.rs:38895-38913.

ACCWeenieObject::ObjectsInRange :436730-436750 returns 0 when either object is not in CObjectMaint, otherwise checks `CPhysicsObj::get_distance_to_object(v5, v6, _use_radii) <= _range` (use_radii=0, centre distance). For the optional radar gate: CanHear :434317-434367 and GetRadarRadius returns 75.0 outdoors and 25.0 indoors. ACE: EmoteManager.cs:1125-1126 `if (emote.Extent > 0) WorldObject.EnqueueBroadcast(new GameMessageHearRangedSpeech(message, name, ..., emote.Extent, ChatMessageType.Emote), WorldObject.LocalBroadcastRange);` and WorldObject.cs:1018 `LocalBroadcastRange = 96.0f`.

Otherwise look up the sender's and the player's `entities.get(guid).position`. If either is missing, drop the line (retail behaviour); otherwise require `player.distance_to(&sender) <= data.range`. Skip both the chat line and the bubble when the check fails. Put the decision in a pure helper in chat_format.rs and unit-test it there. Escape flag: ?rangedSpeechGate=off. Optionally, in the same patch, the CanHear radar gate for HearSpeech, EmoteText and SoulEmote (known sender only, 2D distance < 75 m outdoors or 25 m indoors).

finding.title: Spew-box (0x1A) lines are also copied into the chat log, and the on-screen notice holds only one line
finding.description: In retail, text type 0x1A goes to the spew box over the 3D view: the newest line on top, an identical top line replaced rather than stacked, and a fixed maximum number of lines. Every chat window starts with the 0x1A bit cleared from its filter, so these lines appear in chat only when the player ticks the 'Errors' chat option. holtburger tags them TRANSIENT, which shows in the HUD chat under 'All' and in the System tab. It also raises a single toast that each new line replaces, lasting 2.4 s. The result: every server transient string (ACE has 138 CommunicationTransientString call sites) and every 0x1A failure line clutters the chat log, and two quick notices overwrite each other. ACE's own enum notes say type 0x1A is 'Client doesn't display it' in chat, and the 2026-10-09 charselect handoff records the same rule ('retail text type 0x1A is never a chat line'). The 4-line cap and 5 s lifetime come from WebAC's DAT reading (layout 0x21000011) and were not re-verified here.

finding.title: Retail /age and /birth client commands are missing, and the QueryAgeResponse line reads '? 2d 3h' instead of 'You have played for 2d 3h.'
finding.description: In retail, /age sends CM_Character::Event_QueryAge (0x1C2) and /birth sends Event_QueryBirth (0x1C4). Both are ordinary player commands. holtburger has neither GameAction (they are commented out in opcodes.rs), and the verbs are not in RETAIL_CLIENT_VERBS, so '/age' goes to ACE as the text command '@age', which ACE does not have. Separately, the existing QueryAgeResponse path formats the reply as `${name || "?"} ${age}`. ACE always sends an empty name, so the line would read '? 1d 2h 3m'. Retail prints 'You have played for %s.' when the name is empty and '%s has played for %s.' otherwise, as a type-0 line. ACE answers QueryBirth itself with a Broadcast line ('You were born on M/d/yyyy h:mm:ss tt.'). Optional, not required: /loc, /day, /framerate and /version are also retail client-side verbs.

finding.title: Death purge wipes item-spell (duration -1) enchantments and cooldowns from the local mirror, so buffed stats drop after every death
finding.description:
On death ACE sends MagicPurgeEnchantments, or MagicPurgeBadEnchantments when the player has the augmentation. Holtburger's PlayerState::purge_enchantments keeps only VITAE entries (plus BENEFICIAL ones on the bad purge). It therefore deletes two kinds of entry the server and retail both keep:
(a) item-cast enchantments. Cantrips from worn gear sit in the player's registry with Duration = -1.0 (ACE BuildEntry, equip branch).
(b) shared-cooldown entries (StatModType COOLDOWN, spell id > 0x7FFF).
ACE never sends them again, so until relog or re-equip:
- attribute, skill and vital 'current' values computed in stats_calc.rs lose every cantrip bonus (lower Strength and skills, wrong max Health/Stamina/Mana, so the vitals HUD percentages are wrong);
- buffs-hud loses the item-spell icons;
- cooldown timers vanish.
This is a silent, recurring stat-display bug on the most common death path. WebAC brought the lead (it keeps cooldowns across the purge). The decomp adds the duration -1 rule, which WebAC itself misses.

WebAC does not keep duration -1 entries, so take that rule from the decomp, not from WebAC.

Called from crates/holtburger-world/src/handlers/player.rs:555-563 for both purge events. Tests crates/holtburger-world/src/player/tests.rs:562 and :1222 cover only buff, debuff and vitae; no duration -1 or COOLDOWN case. The stat consumers are crates/holtburger-world/src/player/stats_calc.rs:11-27 (multiplier/additive over self.enchantments) and :116-140 (vital current).
