finding.title: Auto-repeat attack lifecycle is incomplete: a new selection keeps ACE swinging at the old target; slider changes, jump charges and presses while a reply is pending are lost
finding.description:
Retail ClientCombatSystem tracks repeatAttacking, attackServerResponsePending and attackWhenResponseReceived. Holtburger defaults Repeat Attacks on, but tracks only a lockout bool (`attackInProgress`) that every AttackDone clears.

(a) Target switch. picking.js sends CancelAttack only when the selection is CLEARED. Retail RecvNotice_SelectionChanged sends CancelAttack on ANY selection change while a repeat attack is live. ACE does not let a new TargetedMelee/MissileAttack pre-empt a running loop: it only enqueues the power, and HandleActionTargetedMeleeAttack also stores the new height. So in holtburger, Tab or clicking a second monster and pressing attack keeps hitting the FIRST monster until it dies, unless the player moves.

(b) Slider drift. On AttackDone(0) while repeating, retail re-sends at the slider's power when |requested − slider| > 0.01, and ACE's AttackQueue.Fetch then uses the newest value. Holtburger sends nothing, so every repeat keeps the first swing's power.

(c) Jump. With Repeat Attacks on, retail CommenceJump sends CancelAttack and ends the repeat. Holtburger's jump paths don't, and ACE's loop keeps running through and after the jump.

(d) Pending reply. A press or release while a reply is pending is dropped ('gated'). Retail queues it (attackWhenResponseReceived) and replays it after AttackDone.

(e) End of chain. ACE's end-of-chain AttackDone(ActionCancelled) is treated like AttackDone(None), so the meter paints 'ready' at 100% instead of ending the repeat and resetting.

On the 2026-10-11 regression (picking.js:1955-1959 comment): it came from cancelling on EVERY selection event in a combat stance, because ev.guid was undefined. Gating on a real repeat-state flag, a different non-zero guid and !lodRespawn avoids it.

finding.proposed_change:
Add a pure retail repeat-state module, e.g. ui/attack_repeat_state.js, unit-testable like attack_power_bar.js. State: repeatAttacking (set when a non-followUp attack is sent while __combatBarState.autoRepeat), responsePending (set on send, cleared on attackDone), queuedRelease {height, power}.
Hooks:
(1) picking.js selectionChanged: keep the clear arm, and add one more case. When the repeat state is live, the new guid is non-zero and differs from the last attack target, and !d.lodRespawn, call cancelAttack() on the existing 500 ms throttle and end the repeat.
(2) attackDone listener reads detail.error:
- error != 'None' → end the repeat and reset the meter (not 'ready');
- error == 'None' && repeating && no key held && |lastPower − slider| > 0.01 → re-send through the existing opts.followUp path (no turn, prediction or lockout);
- then replay queuedRelease.
(3) Space keydown (both arms) → cancelAttack() when autoRepeat && the repeat is live.
(4) The picking.js:1538 gate stores queuedRelease instead of dropping.

implementation.summary:
I added a pure module, ui/attack_repeat_state.js, that tracks retail ClientCombatSystem's repeat-attack state: repeatAttacking, the pending server reply (attackServerResponsePending), and a queued press (attackWhenResponseReceived). scene3d/picking.js is wired to it:
- Only the user fire path (fireOnce) calls noteSend. The bot's wasm attacks never set repeatAttacking.
- A press while the old lockout is set or a reply is pending is queued instead of dropped. The server's kind=19 combatCommenceAttack also raises the pending flag. After AttackDone the queued press is replayed in a microtask, together with retail's second request at the selector.
- A queued release holds back its own follow-up.
- On AttackDone(None) while repeating with no key held, the attack is re-sent once through the followUp path if the slider drifted by more than 0.01. A non-zero AttackDone ends the repeat.
- Selecting a different non-zero object (not the same guid, not the wielded-weapon redirect target, not a lodRespawn) sends a throttled CancelAttack and ends the repeat.
- Space, when canJumpNow is true and a repeat is live, sends CancelAttack. This is caught in picking.js's raw keydown watcher, which sees all three index.html Space paths.
- The existing deselect and movement CancelAttack paths also end the local repeat.
To keep the target switch working between swings, the module expects the ActionCancelled that answers our own CancelAttack: if a new attack was sent after the cancel, that reply no longer ends the new repeat (the same idea as rynth's _expectStaleEnd). plugins/combat-bar.js now empties its meter to 0% on a chain-ending AttackDone (ActionCancelled) instead of painting 100% 'ready'. The change is JS only, ships on by default, and `?attackRepeatState=off` restores the old lockout-only behaviour exactly. No rynth files were touched.

implementation.deviations:
1. I added handling for the reply to our own CancelAttack, which the verifier did not ask for. If the player switches target between swings (nothing pending), the press on B goes out at once. ACE's ActionCancelled for the old chain then arrives after B's send. Without this handling it would end the B repeat locally, and the next switch (B to C) would hit the original bug again. The module records the cancel and ignores a chain-end that arrives after a newer send, within 3.5 s. It does this only when the cancel was really sent while a chain was live.
2. The jump hook lives in picking.js's raw keydown watcher (onKeyDownAbortCharge, Space checked first, gated on canJumpNow). I did not edit the index.html Space arms: index.html is not in this lane's file list, and the watcher already receives every gated keydown through the input funnel or the document listener, so it covers the legacy, jumpParity and cmdInterp arms.
3. A non-zero AttackDone ends the repeat locally only. Retail's AbortAutomaticAttack would also send CancelAttack there. I follow the verifier and WebAC's stopRepeating instead: ACE's OnAttackDone has already ended the chain, and a CancelAttack at that point would only call cancel_moveto.
4. combat-bar.js inlines the error test and the flag reader instead of importing ui/attack_repeat_state.js. With the import, existing spliced tests (combat_bar_skill_stride and others) refuse the unstubbed import, and I may not edit those tests. The new test runs the inlined copies against the module's helpers so the two stay in sync.
5. A queued press replays immediately at its queued power. Retail instead rebuilds the bar to that power first; here ACE enforces NextRefillTime itself. The replay runs in a microtask so it comes after every AttackDone listener (the combat-bar lockout clear and the meter paint).
6. I added a 4 s ack-loss safety on the pending flag, which retail does not have. Without it, a lost reply would leave presses queued forever.
7. combat-hud.js's meter is unchanged. At rest it paints the selector power, not 'ready'.

finding.title: In-world Escape does nothing; retail Escape cancels a jump charge, deselects (willingly, so no auto-target), or stops and aborts the repeat attack
finding.description:
RE-RAISE of the deferred 'selection-2: Escape-deselect not wired' (HANDOFF-openac-comparison-2026-10-08.md:200). Two things are new.
First, WebAC brings a ready implementation, ordered exactly as the decomp, with 12 targeted tests.
Second, the combat half was never part of the deferral. In retail, Escape is the standard way to stop an auto-repeat swing loop: StopCompletely, the 'Action interrupted' line when moving, and AbortAutomaticAttack (CancelAttack).
Retail OnAction 0x27 runs in this order:
1. A jump charge is cancelled, and nothing else happens.
2. A focused UI element releases focus.
3. When standing still with no repeat attack: a pending vendor open is cleared, else the selection is dropped with targetWillinglyLost=1 (so no auto-target), else the options page toggles.
4. Otherwise: stop completely, print 'Action interrupted' (0x1a) if the player was moving, and AbortAutomaticAttack if a repeat attack is in progress.
Holtburger already has most of the pieces:
- EntityManager.deselectTarget() sets _targetWillinglyLost and clears, but nothing calls it;
- sessionHandle.cancelAttack;
- the stop path;
- jumpChargeAbort.

No in-world Escape handler deselects, stops or cancels the attack loop.

IsStandingStill && !RepeatAttackInProgress → attemptOpenVendorID ? SetTargetMode(0) : selectedID ? (targetWillinglyLost=1; SetSelectedObject(0)) : DoVisibilityToggleAction(0x1000001B). Else StopCompletely; `if ( v10 )` 'Action interrupted' (0x1A); `if (RepeatAttackInProgress) AbortAutomaticAttack`. Helpers: RepeatAttackInProgress :407523; AbortAutomaticAttack :407958 (CancelAttack only when pending/request/inProgress/repeating).

The decomp order is verified at acclient.c:402170-402224:

2. m_focusElement → release focus.
3. When standing (the cmdinterp vfptr[15] query) && !RepeatAttackInProgress: attemptOpenVendorID → SetTargetMode(0); else selectedID → targetWillinglyLost=1 + SetSelectedObject(0); else DoVisibilityToggleAction(0x1000001B).
4. Otherwise StopCompletely, 'Action interrupted' (0x1A) when not standing, and AbortAutomaticAttack when a repeat is in progress.

- keymap.js:57 binds Escape to 'Close Panel / Popover';

But the deferral reason is stated explicitly in docs/url-flags.md:1526: '…no key calls it, because ~25 panels already own Escape'. The proposal's 'bind at a LOWER priority than the panel handlers' does not solve this. The funnel's priority (ui/input-funnel.js:233-290) orders only funnel subscribers. implementation.summary:
I added the retail in-world Escape (ClientUISystem::OnAction case 0x27, acclient.c:402170-402224) as a new module, ui/escape_action.js, wired from scene3d/picking.js. Default ON; `?escapeAction=off` turns it off.

It follows the decomp order:
1. A held jump charge is cancelled and nothing else happens.
2. When standing still with no repeat attack, a pending use-on-target is cleared. Otherwise the selection is dropped through `em.deselectTarget()`, which sets the willingly-lost mark so no auto-target follows. With nothing selected, nothing happens (the options toggle is not ported).
3. Otherwise the client move and autorun stop, "Action interrupted" goes to the spew box (0x1A) when the player was moving, and a running repeat attack is aborted. Abort means a throttled CancelAttack through the combat-magic-2 repeat state, plus cancelling a power bar that is still building.

Decomp correction: the field the decomp calls `attemptOpenVendorID` in step 2 is really `targetMode`, because OnAction's `this` sits 8 bytes into ClientUISystem. So that step is the use-on-target cursor.

The central Escape-consumed signal needs no panel edits. The action is the input funnel's last raw subscriber (priority -1000). For each Escape it opens a short session: a MutationObserver over the document plus a one-shot listener on window, which is the last stop of the event path. The Escape counts as used by a panel when it was preventDefault()ed, its propagation was stopped (the window stop never comes and a 0 ms timer settles it), it carries `markEscapeConsumed`, or the DOM changed during dispatch (a panel hid or closed itself). Changes made before the session opens, such as the hover tooltip hiding, don't count.

The existing picking.js Escape use-target cancel now steps aside when the action is installed. Tests: 41 node tests, all passing; the related suites also pass.

implementation.deviations:
- **Consumed signal without panel edits:** the verifier wanted panels to mark the event or register in an open-panels registry. Most of those panels are in other lanes, so the signal is detected centrally instead (preventDefault, stopped propagation, a DOM change during dispatch, or the optional `markEscapeConsumed` mark). The in-world handler still runs after every panel handler, at the window bubble stop.
- **Stop path is JS-only:** it is cancelClientMove (stopStick + cancelPursuit) plus autorun off (SetAutoRun(0, 0)). There is no JS-callable StopCompletely export: the wasm MaybeStopCompletely runs only before attack and cast sends, and `cancelPursuit` deliberately leaves a server-commanded MoveTo alone. So held movement keys and a server MoveTo keep going after the "Action interrupted" line.
- **Standing-still check:** built from what the page can see — the pose's isOnGround, held W/A/S/D/Q/E in the funnel's held-key ledger (read-only `funnel._held`), `window.__autoRunOn`, and `localAutonomousMotion()`.
- **Step 3c:** the options-page toggle is a no-op, as the verifier said.
- **Use-target cancel moved:** picking.js's old Escape use-target cancel now runs inside the action (retail step 3a, standing only), not on every Escape. With `?escapeAction=off` it is unchanged.
implementation.follow_ups:
1. Add a wasm `stopCompletely()` export, then call it from the `stopCompletely` dep in ui/escape_action.js. The chain is SessionCommand → InterpOp/QueuedDriveCommand::StopCompletely → `CommandInterpreter::stop_completely`, called unconditionally. Retail's Escape calls StopCompletely directly (acclient.c:402212), not MaybeStopCompletely, which is suppressed under server control. The legacy lane would use PlayerDriveIntent::Stop. This lets Escape clear held keys and cancel a server MoveTo. The JS cannot run it today.
2. picking.js never unbinds its funnel raws (picking.abortCharge, picking.cancelUseTarget) in destroy(). This leak was already there before this change. The new escape subscriber does unbind; destroy() keeps the `escapeAction` reference set so the leaked use-target arm stays quiet.
3. ui/input-funnel.js could expose a public held-codes accessor so escape_action.js does not read `_held`.
4. Panels whose Escape close is caught only by the DOM-change signal could call `markEscapeConsumed(ev)` or preventDefault() to make it explicit: allegiance, social, fellowship, vitae, the spellbook detail popover, the bar.js settings and the inventory armed item.
5. Retail step 3c (DoVisibilityToggleAction 0x1000001B, the options gameplay page, when nothing is selected) is not ported.
6. A JS-synthesized Escape must use `bubbles: true` to reach the window stop. Otherwise it settles as "propagation" and nothing happens in-world.

finding.title: spellcast-5 re-raise: the personalized-formula port is now decomp-verified, the hash already exists in holtburger, and a three-way agreement can supply the missing golden vectors
finding.description:
RE-RAISE with new evidence. Holtburger still renders base-formula tapers in the spellbook, and its opt-in precheck matches item NAMES against the base formula. rg finds no RandomizeVersion or customized-formula code anywhere. The item was deferred because there were no exact golden vectors.
New evidence:
(1) Decomp check. I checked ACE SpellTable.cs:32-172 line by line against the decomp: SpellFormula::RandomizeVersion1/2/3, the RandomizeForName dispatch and CSpellBase::InqCustomizedSpellFormula. Every expression, modulus (0x13D573, 0x4AEFD, 0x96A7F, 0x100A03, 0xEB2EF, 0x121E7D, 0x65039), slot index and the +GetLowestTaperID (63) matches.
The only retail-only details:
- V1 counts NON-ZERO slots; this is equivalent, because holtburger's decrypt_components drops zero slots;
- V1 has unreachable divide-by-zero guards;
- V2/V3 read a missing slot 7 as 0 from the fixed 8-slot array, where ACE's List would throw.
(2) The account hash is AC1Legacy::PStringBase<char>::compute_hash. Holtburger already has it byte-identical as spellbase_string_hash, and real DAT data validates it every time a formula is decrypted (a wrong hash gives out-of-range component ids). Only about 40 lines of u32 arithmetic are actually new.
(3) WebAC ships an independent port: getPlayerFormula (ACE-derived) and decomp-derived scarabOnlyFormula/appropriateSpellFormula/spellComponentsSatisfied. Its scarab-only keep-set, including 0x6F, and the FindMostPowerfulPowerComponent taper counts match the decomp. It also pins real-DAT values: Lead Scarab → WCID 691 via DualDidMapper 0x27000002, and foci DidMapper 0x27000003 = [15271, 15270, 15269, 15268, 43173] for War/Life/Item/Creature/Void.
WebAC has NO exact vectors either; its tests pin only determinism and the 63..74 taper range. Golden vectors can therefore come from three-way agreement: the Rust port transcribed from the decomp, WebAC getPlayerFormula and ACE GetSpellFormula, over 3-4 formulas (versions 1/2/3) and 2 account names.
Warning: WebAC's SpellComponentCheck.ts header says AreSpellComponentsRequired defaults to false when bool 68 is absent. The decomp sets `required = 1` first, so keep holtburger's round-1 reading (default true).

finding.title: Spell bars (8 tabs) are browser-wide localStorage, never saved to ACE; the per-character SpellLists8 holtburger already parses is ignored
finding.description: All 8 spell-bar tabs live under one browser-wide localStorage key, "holtburger_combat_bar_v1". The key has no account or character in it, and nothing is ever sent to the server. Two consequences. (1) Switching characters in the same browser, which is now a first-class flow since /logout reloads into character select (2026-10-09), shows the previous character's spells. Pressing a spell-bar key then casts a spell this character does not know, and ACE refuses it. (2) Logging in from another browser or device shows empty bars. In retail the bars are per-character PlayerModule state. Every edit goes to the server (Event_AddSpellFavorite / Event_RemoveSpellFavorite). Login rebuilds the bars from PlayerDescription and drops spells the character no longer knows. ACE implements both ends. Holtburger already decodes SPELL_LISTS8 into world.player.hotbar_spells, but no wasm getter exposes it and the two opcodes are commented out. The spellbook filter word has the same problem: spellbook.js says it is 'persisted per browser here (retail kept it in the character's PlayerModule)'. ACE accepts SpellbookFilter 0x0286, and PlayerDescription already hydrates world.player.spellbook_filters.

finding.title: canEquipInSlot inverts retail's held-caster combat rule, misses shield-with-wand, and invents refusal text (retail CPlayerSystem::AutoWieldIsLegal)
finding.description: Both the double-click wield and the paperdoll drop go through canEquipInSlot, which approximates ACE's server checks rather than retail's client check, and diverges in four ways. (a) It refuses a CASTER in a Held slot while in combat with a melee weapon. Retail does the opposite: casters are allowed, and a held NON-caster is refused outside NonCombat ("Cannot hold %s while in combat"). ACE agrees with retail (Ball-of-Gunk rule). (b) buildPlayerEquipState files a Held item (a wand) under `offhand`, so the shield check, which reads mainWeapon, never sees a wielded caster. Retail checks weaponReadySlot, which includes Held, against BlocksUseOfShield. (c) Casters are detected through DefaultCombatStyle, a PropertyInt that is only known after appraisal. Retail uses ITEM_TYPE 0x8000 from the PublicWeenieDesc, which is always present and already on the inventory row as itemType. (d) The texts are not retail: holtburger says 'This ammunition does not fit your X' where retail says 'Cannot be used with %s', and 'This item cannot be worn in that slot.' where retail's drop on a non-matching slot is silent. Net effect: a hybrid in melee combat cannot double-click an appraised wand to swap to it, which retail and ACE both allow, and equipping a shield while holding a wand is not refused client-side.

verification.reasoning:
I re-read inventory_helpers.js. The rule at :310-315 refuses a caster (DefaultCombatStyle caster bit) in a Held slot when inCombatMode and a MeleeWeapon is equipped. buildPlayerEquipState (:238-260) sets mainWeapon only for Melee, Missile and TwoHanded, and files Shield or Held under offhand, so the shield cascade at :299-308 never sees a wielded wand. Refusal texts are at :291 and :323. Retail CPlayerSystem::AutoWieldIsLegal (acclient.c:397227-397330) runs three checks:
- Ammo item against the weaponReadySlot launcher's ammoType gives "Cannot be used with %s" (NAME_APPROPRIATE).
- An item with the Shield bit 0x200000 against BlocksUseOfShield(weaponReadySlot) gives "A shield may not be worn with the %s". BlocksUseOfShield (:395589) is true for combatUse 2 with ammoType, combatUse 5, or the InqType bit 0x8000 (Caster).
- A Held 0x1000000 item with combatMode != 1 whose InqType lacks 0x8000 gives "Cannot hold %s while in combat". This applies to non-casters only, so holtburger's caster rule is inverted.

ACE agrees: Player_Inventory.cs CheckWeaponCollision case Held refuses only DefaultCombatStyle == null outside NonCombat (the Ball-of-Gunk rule). The comparer's "cannot swap" consequence also holds. activateItem (inventory.js:617-640) calls canEquipInSlot before executeItemAction to setWielded/wieldFromPack. The wasm WieldFromPack (session/commands/inventory.rs:531+) unequips conflicting weapons first through holtburger_world::equip::wield_unequip_conflicts, so retail and ACE would let a hybrid in melee mode swap to a wand, and holtburger refuses client-side. For a shield while holding a wand, retail refuses, but holtburger passes the check and wield_unequip_conflicts (shield_vs_weapon, equip.rs:93-96) silently strips the wand. On the paperdoll, retail gmPaperDollUI::AcceptDragObject (:219987) returns 0 silently on a slot/ValidLocations mismatch, and HandleDropRelease (:220960) only clears the waiting state. DefaultCombatStyle is a PropertyInt read in lib.rs (~:46704) that a PublicWeenieDesc does not carry, whereas row.itemType is always present. combatUse is on the row only with a newer wasm (copyInventoryRow :476). This finding is not in any ledger.

Add retailAutoWieldIllegal(item, rows, inCombat) to plugins/inventory_helpers.js as a straight port of AutoWieldIsLegal:
- weapon = the row with equipMask & 0x3500000.
- If item.validLocations & 0x800000 and weapon.ammoType is non-zero and differs from item.ammoType, return `Cannot be used with ${appropriateName(weapon)}`.
- If item.validLocations & 0x200000 and blocksUseOfShield(weapon), return `A shield may not be worn with the ${weapon.name}`. blocksUseOfShield = (combatUse===2 && ammoType) || combatUse===5 || (itemType & 0x8000). When combatUse is absent, fall back to equipMask & TwoHanded.
- If item.validLocations & 0x1000000 and inCombat and !(item.itemType & 0x8000), return `Cannot hold ${appropriateName(item)} while in combat`.

Wiring:
- Route activateItem (inventory.js:631-639) and dropCtx.canEquip (:1565) through it behind ?retailWieldLegal (default on).
- In decideItemDrop DOLL_SLOT, make (vl & mask)===0 a silent NOOP instead of 'This item cannot be worn in that slot.'.
- Keep the 'Item attributes pending' guard.
- Leave canEquipInSlot as it is for =off, so tests/inventory_paperdoll_helpers.test.cjs stays unedited.

Re-derive from the decomp.

implementation.summary: I ported retail CPlayerSystem::AutoWieldIsLegal (acclient.c:397227) into plugins/inventory_helpers.js after re-reading it, ACCWeenieObject::BlocksUseOfShield (:395589) and the 0x3500000 weaponReadySlot setup (:396022, :221868). It adds `retailAutoWieldIllegal`, `blocksUseOfShield` and `retailAppropriateName`, plus a private `retailWieldVerdict`. The checks run against the weapon-ready slot, which includes a wielded wand. Ammo whose AmmoType differs from the launcher's gives "Cannot be used with X". A shield next to a launcher, two-hander or caster (ITEM_TYPE 0x8000) gives "A shield may not be worn with the X". A held NON-caster outside NonCombat gives "Cannot hold X while in combat", which fixes the old rule that refused casters instead. Both the double-click wield (activateItem) and the paperdoll drop (dropCtx.canEquip) now use it behind `?retailWieldLegal` (default ON, read with defaultOnUrlFlag). "In combat" comes from the wasm `combatMode() != 1`, guarded with typeof. The old source, `__combatBarState.inCombatMode`, is a field nothing ever sets, so the held rule could never have fired. Dropping an item on a paperdoll slot outside its ValidLocations is now a quiet refusal (gmPaperDollUI::AcceptDragObject / HandleDropRelease): the slot still turns red on hover, and the release shows no message and makes no error sound. `=off` keeps the old canEquipInSlot cascade and texts unchanged, and the existing paperdoll helpers test passes as is.

implementation.deviations: 1) Wiring: inventory.js does not import `retailAutoWieldIllegal` directly. tests/inventory_dnd_dom.test.mjs loads inventory.js with an explicit stub list and fails hard on any new imported name, and existing tests may not be edited. Instead, `buildPlayerEquipState(rows, {retailWieldLegal: true})` marks the state and carries the rows, and `canEquipInSlot` hands such a state to the retail verdict right after the shared 'Item attributes pending' guard. The legacy body below that point is untouched and still runs for `=off` and for every existing test. Both call sites now share a local `wieldEquipState(rows)` helper. 2) "In combat" on the retail path comes from the wasm `h.combatMode() != 1` (retail ClientCombatSystem::combatMode), guarded with typeof. `window.__combatBarState.inCombatMode` is never set anywhere, so with it the held rule would never fire; `=off` still reads it. 3) The BlocksUseOfShield fallback is used when combatUse is 0 as well as when it is absent. The fallback is the TwoHanded slot, or the MissileWeapon slot with an AmmoType. combatUse 0 means unknown on a fresh wasm, and the fallback stops the wasm wield_unequip_conflicts from quietly removing a two-hander. 4) The quiet refusal is `{op:"noop", refused:true}`, still op "noop". inventory.js hitFor keeps the red reject highlight (retail OnItemListDragOver reject state 0x10000041). The release is silent because of a one-line item_drag.js onDrop change: `if (!hit.silent) uiError()`. Returning a plain NOOP would have turned a slot that refuses the item green. 5) The activateItem path also honours `verdict.silent`: no toast, nothing sent. In practice it is unreachable there, because its slotMask comes from ValidLocations. 6) NAME_APPROPRIATE is `retailAppropriateName`: the plural name for a stack above 1, else the name. The material prefix retail adds via name_with_material is not reproduced, and rows carry no pluralName, so plurals fall back to name + s/es.

finding.title: Hotbar bindings use one browser-wide localStorage cache, so another character's shortcuts leak onto the bar; retail flushes the bar on PlayerDescription
finding.description: The hotbar loads 'holtburger_hotbar_v1' once at mount and merges it with the server's shortcuts. Three problems. (1) The key is the same for every account and character. (2) The wasm playerShortcuts() returns [] both before PlayerDescription and for a character with no saved shortcuts, so such a character can never reconcile. (3) The merge keeps any locally cached spell binding wherever the server slot is empty. Retail gmToolbarUI::UpdateFromPlayerDesc flushes all 18 slots and rebuilds them from the new character's PlayerModule. With /logout returning to character select in the same tab (2026-10-09), switching characters now hits this path. ACE stores only ObjectId per shortcut, so holtburger's spell-on-hotbar bindings exist only in this cache. They then follow the browser rather than the character, and they are overwritten by whichever character played last.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/network/itemShortcutRestore.ts:313-330 restoreFromDescription: 'flush every slot first (a re-sent description replaces the whole bar — also clears the previous character's icons after a switch)', then binds each record, deferring unknown items through a pending map (no browser storage). main.ts:5510 `itemShortcutRestorer.clear();` in teardownWorldState. main.ts:9634 PlayerDescription hook.
finding.holtburger_evidence: plugins/hotbar.js:95 `const LS_KEY = "holtburger_hotbar_v1";`, and :667 `const state = loadState();` (mount-time, browser-wide). reconcileWithServer :1403-1447: :1408 `if (!flat || flat.length === 0) return false;` and :1442 `merged[idx] = l; // preserve local spell binding (server is item-only)`. The 1 Hz timer :1648-1651 gives up after 30 tries. The prune keeps never-seen items for NEVER_SEEN_GRACE_MS (:1474, 30 s) and then sends RemoveShortCut. src/lib.rs:42281-42293 playerShortcuts() returns an empty Vec until stats exist, and also when the character has no shortcuts.
finding.decomp_evidence: gmToolbarUI::UpdateFromPlayerDesc (acclient.c:241958) calls gmToolbarUI::FlushShortcuts and then AddShortcut for each of the 18 PlayerModule slots (loop `while (v6 < 18)`). The bar is exactly the new character's, with nothing kept from before. ACE Player_Character.cs:252-258 HandleActionAddShortcut persists (Index, ObjectId) per character, with no spell field.
finding.failure_scenario: In one tab, character A binds items to 1-9 plus a spell, runs /logout, and enters with character B, who has no saved shortcuts. implementation.summary: Hotbar bindings were cached under one browser-wide localStorage key (holtburger_hotbar_v1). That key was loaded at mount, which is page load, and merged with the server list only once that list was non-empty. After /logout and a different character, the last character's items came back on the bar and its spell bindings stayed for good. plugins/hotbar.js now keeps the cache per server, account and character, under `holtburger_hotbar_v1|${lastLocationKey({...__hbLoginKey, charId})}`, with the guid taken from getLocalPlayerGuid() or handle.playerGuid(). Nothing is loaded until the character is known. On PlayerDescription the bar is rebuilt as retail gmToolbarUI::UpdateFromPlayerDesc does (acclient.c:241958): server item bindings win, this character's cached spells fill the slots the server left empty, and every other cached item is flushed. An empty playerShortcuts() now counts as authoritative once PlayerDescription has landed. The signal is playerStats().attributes being non-empty, which needs no wasm change, because the wasm publishes shortcuts and attributes in the same snapshot. The bar mounts at page load, so the 1 Hz poll can give up before login. A playerStatsUpdated subscription, late-bound through __pluginClientReady, retries until one merge lands, then unsubscribes. The old browser-wide cache is handed once to the first character loaded, copied to that character's key and marked with a flag; it stays in place for `?hotbarPerChar=off`. That flag restores the old path: browser-wide key read at mount, merge only on a non-empty list, no bus listener. The mount, the DOM, the 'hb-hotbar-mounted' event and the window.__hotbar API (including addonSlot) are unchanged, and the new test checks them.

finding.title: 3D drop onto a vendor gives the item away instead of retail AttemptSellToVendor; no merge into a ground stack; no mid-air refusal
finding.description: decideItemDrop's WORLD case covers 3D drops and is missing three retail ItemHolder::AttemptPlaceIn3D branches. (1) Retail first tries AttemptMerge onto the found object, so a stack dropped on a same-wcid ground stack merges. Holtburger drops a second pile. (2) Retail handles a found object with BF_VENDOR (0x200) through ClientUISystem::AttemptSellToVendor. If that vendor's window is open, the item is added to the sell list. Otherwise the vendor is Used, and the item is staged when its VendorInfo opens the shop in sell mode; a partial split is refused with 'You must split the stack before selling it.'. Holtburger treats vendors as creatures and sends GiveObjectRequest. ACE then walks the character to the vendor and answers with a refusal (doesn't want that / not accepting gifts). (3) Retail refuses a ground drop when the player is not on the ground ('You cannot do that in mid air'). Holtburger sends DropItem while airborne. ACE supports landblock merges (LocationsICanMove includes Landblock), so (1) needs no server change.

I re-read decideItemDrop DROP_TARGET.WORLD (inventory_helpers.js:615-642). In order it handles the owned check, self, open container, the charopt-4 trade, isCreature (give), and the extcontainer-3 container refusal, then falls through to drop. There is no merge, no vendor branch and no on-ground check. describeWorldEntity (item_drag.js:494-538) reads odf but exposes no vendor bit, and handleWorldDrop (:541-548) adds nothing.

Retail ItemHolder::AttemptPlaceIn3D (acclient.c:433163-433340, called with _dropIfGiveFails=1 from :275714) runs in this order:
1. Not owned gives "You must first pick up the %s".
2. Trading gives "You are trading the %s, it cannot be dropped" (:433226).
3. ItemHolder::AttemptMerge(obj, target, 0). IsMergeAttemptLegal (:432033) is quiet unless both objects are stackable. When both are, it prints "The destination stack is already full." or "You cannot merge different types of items." and the flow continues.
4. pwd._bitfield & 0x200 (BF_VENDOR): a full split goes to ClientUISystem::AttemptSellToVendor (:433250), otherwise "You must split the stack before selling it." (:433256).
5. DragItemOnPlayerOpensSecureTrade, then creature (UIAttemptGive), then container checks.
6. If not on_ground, "You cannot do that in mid air" (:433320).
7. Split or put in 3D.

AttemptSellToVendor (:401304) sends AddItemToSell when that vendor is open, and otherwise UseObject(vendor) while remembering attemptOpenVendorID/attemptSaleObjectID. ACE confirms the server side. HandleActionStackableMerge searches LocationsICanMove, which includes Landblock (Player_Inventory.cs:499 / :2861-2862), and it builds a MoveTo chain toward a world target, so a ground merge works on vanilla ACE. GiveObjectToNPC sends a vendor without a give emote the not-accepting or doesn't-want refusal.

The pieces needed already exist. vendor-ui.js has an internal stageSell(guid) (:435) and a sellQueue. executeItemAction 'merge' calls mergeStacks. The on-ground state is available through handle.getLocalPlayerPose().isOnGround (index.html:4215-4217). Note that __readLocalPose is a closure-local in index.html, not a window global. This finding is not in any ledger.

finding.title: ACE's AccountBoot reason (wrong password, client version, world closed, forced log-off) is parsed and then dropped; retail shows 'You have been booted from Asheron's Call%s.'
finding.description: ACE terminates a session with a GameMessageBootAccount that carries a reason in several common cases: a wrong password, a client-version mismatch, a forced log-off of a duplicate, the world closing, and DAT mismatches. holtburger-protocol decodes AccountBoot{reason}, but the wasm GameMessage dispatch has no arm for it and no ClientEvent is raised. The player only sees the transport-level 'Disconnected: … Reload the page to retry.' line. The most common case, a wrong password, therefore gets no explanation. auto_login.js also cannot tell a password boot from a network drop, so it may keep retrying.

implementation.summary: ACE's AccountBoot (0xF7DC) used to be decoded and then dropped by the wasm dispatcher's misc catch-all. It now ends the session the way retail CPlayerSystem::Handle_AccountBooted (acclient.c:400213) does. A new pure function, account_boot_text (src/account_boot.rs), builds "You have been booted from Asheron's Call%s.", using " for Code of Conduct Violations" when the reason is missing or empty, which matches retail's m_len != 1 check. A new login.rs arm, routed from messages/mod.rs, pushes one kind=4 Disconnected event: stringPayload is that line and u32Payload is the 0xF7DC boot marker, which no other Disconnected event carries. The arm then exits the recv loop, because ACE sends the boot only from Session.Terminate and then drops the session silently. Before CharacterList (wrong password, client version) no handle exists to drain that event, so start_session now finds the marked event in queued_events and rejects with the retail line instead of "recv loop exited before CharacterList arrived". On the JS side, new app/account_boot.js has isAccountBootDisconnect and accountBootSince. client_events.js shows the escaped line in loginStatus and in the banner, sets __lastDisconnect.booted, and skips the bot/agent auto-reload on a boot. auto_login.js treats a boot as terminal after both the connect wait and the spawn wait, whatever maxRetries is. Ordinary disconnects behave exactly as before, and a stale pkg/ simply never sends the marker.

implementation.deviations:
1. I took the verifier's second option and attached the text to the Disconnected event, with no new ClientEvent kind. The boot is marked by u32Payload = 0xF7DC (GameOpcode::AccountBoot) on kind=4, so the generated kind table and kind numbers are unchanged and there is no collision risk with parallel lanes. The recv loop emits that Disconnected itself and exits on the boot (the existing send_or_disconnect pattern). Without that, no transport Disconnected would come promptly: ACE drops the session silently over UDP, so the client would only notice after the 60 s / 140 s silence detector.
2. I edited src/lib.rs, which is not in the lane file list. A pre-CharacterList boot (the wrong-password case) happens before start_session returns a handle, so no ClientEvent can be drained. start_session's map_err now rejects with the boot line taken from the marked event. lib.rs also needed the mod account_boot registration and a kind=4 doc line.
3. account_boot_text takes Option<&str> rather than Option<String>; callers pass data.reason.as_deref().
4. The verifier's JS test, "booted event followed by DISCONNECTED", became "a marker-carrying DISCONNECTED", plus a negative control and auto_login source pins.
5. I added a terminal treatment the verifier did not mention: the bot/agent auto-reload in the DISCONNECTED arm is skipped on a boot. A reload cannot fix a bad password, a wrong client or a closed world, and it would undo an admin boot. Retail stays on the disconnected screen.
6. auto_login also stops on a boot when maxRetries=0. That only changes the final boot-state message.
7. I did not implement AccountBanned, which the verifier marked optional (see follow_ups).
8. There is no escape flag; the verifier proposed none and this is a behaviour fix.

finding.description: Retail answers @corpse (and /corpse) on the client from the PlayerDesc LastOutsideDeath position (PositionType 14). ACE's PlayerDescription position table carries only LastOutsideDeath, but holtburger's parser keeps only position 1. The in-session PrivateUpdatePosition after a death does land in world.player.local_position_overlays, but JS cannot read it.

verification.reasoning:
The gap is real. app/slash_commands.js has no corpse verb: it is not in RETAIL_CLIENT_VERBS (:163-169), so `@corpse` is forwarded verbatim (:620-621), and vanilla ACE has no corpse command handler. Retail ClientCommunicationSystem::DoCorpse (acclient.c:418186) reads CBaseQualities::InqPosition(PlayerDesc, 0xE) (:418240). It prints "The last time you died outside, your corpse was located at (%s).\n" using LandDefs::CellidToCoordinateString(objcell_id), or "We're sorry, but we have no record of your last outside corpse location.\n". It is registered as both "corpse" and "cor" (:428426-428462). ACE GameEventPlayerDescription.cs:202-211 writes only PositionType.LastOutsideDeath, and Creature_Death.cs:558-559 sends PrivateUpdatePosition(LastOutsideDeath).

Two of the comparer's holtburger claims are wrong:
(a) The protocol parser does not keep only position 1. PlayerDescriptionEventData keeps the full `positions: BTreeMap<u32, WorldPosition>` (events.rs:113, filled :237-364, returned :634), and `pos` is just positions[1] (:625). What actually ignores the map is the holtburger-world PlayerDescription hydrate (player/mutations.rs has no `positions` use).
(b) On wasm the in-session PrivateUpdatePosition never reaches world.player.local_position_overlays. should_route_message_to_world (src/lib.rs:34968-35027) explicitly leaves PrivateUpdatePosition un-routed, and session/messages/mod.rs (~:1416-1421) captures only the Sanctuary type into latest_sanctuary. So the overlay path exists only on the native runtime.

The formatting proposal also needs a fix. CellidToCoordinateString (:467472) is cell-granular. It takes lcoord from the cell id only, computes (lcoord - 1024) * 0.1 + 0.5, prints "%.1f%s, %.1f%s" with N/S first, and uses an empty direction at exactly 0. map-panel formatCoords on a fractional origin would give different numbers.

The wasm crate now keeps a per-session LastOutsideDeath slot, following the latest_sanctuary pattern, and exports it as SessionHandle.playerLastOutsideDeath() → LastOutsideDeathJs {cellId,x,y,z} or undefined. One `last_outside_death::observe` call in session/messages/mod.rs fills the slot. It is placed next to the PlayerDescription cache and runs whether or not the world exists yet. finding.title: .met reader fails on LF-only copies: `ba` lengths are CRLF char counts but are consumed as raw bytes
finding.description:
VTank and metaf write the `ba` length of EmbedNav and CreateView as the sum of (line length + 2), so CRLF counts as 2. That count stays the same when git converts a file to LF; WebAC found LF-only copies throughout the community repos it validated (70+ files). holtburger explicitly supports bare-LF .met files (it detects eol "
" and writes LF back), but its `ba` case consumes exactly N bytes. In an LF copy it over-reads by one byte per line break inside the embed and swallows the following State `s` row and later rules. parseMet then returns ok:false ('unexpected end of file', 'unknown value type' or 'runs past the end of the file') and the meta cannot be imported. Example: a rule Always -> EmbedNav 'loop' with 3 points has a 55-char CRLF body; the LF copy is 45 bytes. holtburger reads 55 bytes (body plus 's
Default
'), and the State read hits end of file. The writer has the mirror problem: with eol "
" it writes the LF byte length, which is wrong for VTank once the file is CRLF again. metaf reads .met line by line and uses the count only as `> 5`; WebAC normalises to CRLF first. Both load such files.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/shared/src/routines/vtank.ts:32 `const crlf = (text: string): string => text.replace(/^﻿/, '').replace(/\r?\n/g, '\r\n');`; :81 `case 'ba': { const n = r.int(); return { t: 'ba', v: r.chars(n) }; }`; :100 `const r = new Reader(crlf(text));`; docs/vtank-formats.md:20 "Any length/char counts embedded in the files (.met `ba`, .utl requirement length codes, .utl block lengths) are always computed with CRLF = 2 chars, even in LF-only copies… All 70+ LF-only files validated only under that assumption".
finding.holtburger_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/rynth/vt/formats/met.js:121-127 `case "ba": { const n = this.int("byte count"); … v = { k: "ba", bytes: this.b.subarray(this.p, this.p + n) }; this.p += n;`. :684 `const eol = r.lf > 0 && r.crlf === 0 ? "\n" : "\r\n";` (bare-LF is a supported mode). :454-459 writer `line(chunks, String(b.length), eol)`. tests/rynth_vt_formats_meta.test.mjs:414-417 covers only an LF file with no `ba`. All 18 corpus .met files in /mnt/wbterminal2/met-corpus are CRLF, so the fixtures never exercise this.
finding.decomp_evidence: Authority for this format is metaf, not acclient.c. In /mnt/wbterminal2/met-corpus/format-spec-source/metaf-project/Operations/Actions/AEmbedNav.cs, :41 parses the count, :56 uses it only as `_exactCharCountToAfterMetNAV_InclCrLf > 5`, and :88-89 compute it as `+= f.line[i].Length + 2;` (CRLF convention, line-based reader).
finding.proposed_change: In met.js, give Reader an `lfOnly` flag. parseMet sets it when the header lines end in a bare LF and the body has no CRLF pair. In the `ba` case, when lfOnly, advance byte by byte counting each LF as 2 until the count n is reached (error if the file ends first), then keep the bytes subarray as today. In encScalar('ba'), when eol==='\n', write `b.length + (number of 0x0A bytes in b)`. CRLF files never take the new branch, so they stay byte-identical. LF copies then parse and round-trip byte-stable, because the hint check compares the canonical encoding with the original bytes. New test, with existing tests unedited: take rynth/testdata/vt/meta/BGAugGem-e4623d0c5858aa80.met (17 `ba`) and replace CRLF with LF. Assert parseMet is ok with 65 rules, the same nav tags and point counts as the CRLF parse, and writeMet(parsed) equal to the LF bytes. The Default profile loads no meta, so tests/rynth_vt_parity.test.mjs is unaffected.

verification.reasoning:
Re-read holtburger rynth/vt/formats/met.js. Reader.value case "ba" (:121-127) does `this.int("byte count")`, then `this.b.subarray(this.p, this.p + n); this.p += n`, so it consumes raw bytes. parseMet detects bare-LF files (:684 `const eol = r.lf > 0 && r.crlf === 0 ? "
" : "
"`) and keeps them LF (:704 source.eol), so LF is a supported mode. The writer encScalar('ba') (:454-459) writes `String(b.length)`, which is the LF byte length when eol is "
". The only LF test (tests/rynth_vt_formats_meta.test.mjs:414-417) has no `ba`. metaf AEmbedNav.cs (format-spec-source/metaf-project/Operations/Actions/AEmbedNav.cs) reads line by line and uses the count only as `> 5` (:56). Its writer sums `f.line[i].Length + 2` (:88-89), so the count is CRLF-based. WebAC vtank.ts:33 normalises to CRLF and :81 reads `r.chars(n)`; docs/vtank-formats.md:20 gives the CRLF=2 rule. I checked this directly with a read-only Python port of the reader's byte logic on rynth/testdata/vt/meta/BGAugGem-e4623d0c5858aa80.met (17 `ba`, 6511 CRLF). The CRLF file parses to 65 rows. The LF copy fails with "unknown value type 'ault'" (the swallowed 'Default' state). Counting each LF as 2 in the ba read gives all 65 rows back. The comparer's illustrative arithmetic (55-char body vs 45 bytes for 3 points) is off: 3 points span about 20 lines, not 10. The mechanism and the failure are real. No duplicate in the openac ledgers, HANDOFF §5, PARITY-STATUS or git log -400.
verification.corrected_change: In met.js: (1) parseMet scans the body once and sets `lfOnly = !hasCRLF(body) && body.includes(0x0A)` before building the Reader, passing it as a Reader option. (2) In Reader.value case "ba", when lfOnly, walk from this.p, adding 2 for each 0x0A byte and 1 for any other byte, until the count reaches n. Error with MetError if the end is reached first. If the walk overshoots (the count lands inside a CRLF pair, which an LF file cannot have), treat that as an error too. Keep `bytes = subarray(start, p)`. (3) Compatibility fallback: if the lfOnly parse throws, retry once with raw byte counts (today's behaviour) and keep whichever succeeds. An LF .met that holtburger itself once wrote with byte counts (only possible after adding an EmbedNav to an LF meta that had none) still loads that way. (4) In encScalar 'ba', when eol === "\n", write `b.length + countOf(b, 0x0A)`, the CRLF char count VTank and metaf expect. CRLF files never take the new branches, so their output stays byte-identical. hintIfNonCanonical then still compares the canonical encoding with the original bytes, and LF copies round-trip.
verification.rynth_risk: Touches rynth/vt/formats/met.js only. CRLF files (every corpus file and every fixture) never enter the new branch, so the four MET_FIXTURES round-trip tests and the bare-LF test at :414-417 (no ba) are unchanged. The Default profile loads no meta, so tests/rynth_vt_parity.test.mjs is unaffected. Guard: leave existing tests unedited and add a new test file.
verification.test_plan: New tests/rynth_vt_formats_met_lf.test.mjs (node, no DATs): (a) load BGAugGem-e4623d0c5858aa80.met, replace CRLF with LF, and assert parseMet ok with 65 rules, the same nav tags and the same navTextInfo point counts as the CRLF parse, writeMet(meta) byte-equal to the LF input, and meta.source.eol === "\n"; (b) a synthetic LF meta with one EmbedNav written by writeMet: assert the ba count line equals bytes + LF count and that the meta re-parses; (c) an LF file whose ba count is the raw byte length (the legacy holtburger LF export) still parses through the fallback; (d) the CRLF fixtures stay byte-identical (already covered by the existing suite, run unchanged).

implementation.summary: I fixed rynth/vt/formats/met.js so it loads and round-trips bare-LF .met copies. VTank and metaf write each `ba` length as a CRLF character count (metaf AEmbedNav.ExportToMet sums `line.Length + 2`; ACreateView counts "2 chars for a newline"), and a git LF copy keeps that count. The old reader took the count as raw bytes, over-read by one byte per line break and swallowed the next State. I reproduced this on an LF copy of BGAugGem: `unknown value type "ault"`. The fix: (1) Reader.baEnd walks the bytes and counts each bare LF as 2 when the file is LF (`crlfCounts`), and reports an error if the count ends inside a line break or past the end of the file. (2) parseMet now calls a new parseBody helper. LF files are read with CRLF counts first, then retried once with raw byte counts, which covers LF files holtburger wrote before this change; that retry adds a warning. (3) For LF metas, encScalar('ba') writes crlfLength(b), which is the byte length plus one for each bare LF. (4) hinted() reads `_met` hint bytes with CRLF counts when the meta's eol is "\n". The eol is passed through condTypeOf, actTypeOf, encodeCond, encodeAct and writeMet. Old raw-count hints are therefore re-encoded with VTank's counts, so a saved file never mixes the two conventions. CRLF files never reach any of the new code, and every CRLF fixture and all 17 corpus .met files are still byte-identical. In an ad-hoc check, LF copies of all 17 corpus .met files parse with the same rule counts. All 15 that have no stray CR in string values also round-trip byte-for-byte; this includes FacilityHub_Expanded with 69 `ba` and 4Hives.

tests_run.result: all 8 checks passed. Mutation-checked on a scratch copy: removing the LF detection, the writer count, the retry or the hint-mode change each fails 1 to 7 checks
all 34 checks passed (unchanged; same before and after)

implementation.deviations: 1) How an LF file is detected. The verifier said to use LF counting when the body has no CRLF pair anywhere. I use LF counting when the first header line ("1") ends in a bare LF, and the walk adds 2 only for a bare LF: an LF that follows a CR inside the `ba` adds 1, so a CRLF pair still counts 2. For pure-LF files (git copies) this is exactly the verifier's rule. The difference is that reader and writer stay consistent when an LF meta's CreateView XML contains a CRLF. With the verifier's rule, the written file would hold a CRLF pair, be read with raw counts and fail to load (covered by a new test). CRLF-headed files never enter the new branch, same as the verifier's rule. 2) Writer count. The verifier specified `b.length + countOf(b, 0x0A)`; I count bare LFs only (crlfLength). This is the same for EmbedNav and for any content without CR, and it matches the reader in the mixed-content case. 3) Hint handling, beyond the verifier's text. hinted() now takes the eol and reads `_met` hint bytes with CRLF counts for LF metas, without falling back to raw counts. Otherwise the raw-count retry would let old raw-count hints be written back unchanged next to newly encoded nodes, and the saved file would mix both conventions and load in neither mode. Because of this, an older LF export is saved with VTank's CRLF counts instead of round-tripping byte-for-byte; a test asserts the output equals the VTank-count LF copy. 4) Added a warning on the raw-count retry: `"ba" lengths are LF byte counts, not VTank's CRLF character counts (an older LF export); saving writes VTank's counts`.
implementation.follow_ups:
- `ba` counts are still read as UTF-8 byte counts. metaf and WebAC count C# or JS characters (UTF-16 units), so the two disagree for non-ASCII EmbedNav names or CreateView XML. This is a separate issue that already existed; the header comment claims byte counts are correct.
- The LF copies of FellowSpells and abmain have a CR at the end of a string value. After CRLF to LF conversion that CR plus the line's LF forms a new CRLF pair, so eol is detected as "\r\n" and the LF copy does not round-trip byte-for-byte. This already happened before the change and does not involve `ba`.
- If an unknown CType or AType in an older raw-count LF export carries `ba` data, those bytes are still written back unchanged. This is theoretical, since VTank has no such types.
- I created a scratch mutation copy at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-wbterminal/5f7926ef-9e64-4580-8465-f313ab864389/scratchpad/metlf-mut. `rm` was denied, so it is still there, outside the repo.

finding.title: Comma-decimal VTank/metaf files are misread: .nav coordinates silently truncated, .utl double thresholds inflated, .met `d` rejects the whole meta
finding.description: metaf, and VTank which is also .NET, parse and write doubles with the Windows locale; metaf-project never uses InvariantCulture. A player on a comma-decimal locale (de, fr, nl…) therefore produces `33,579` in .nav files and in .met `d` lines, and VTClassic's own .utl reader turns ',' into '.' (HaxConvertDouble). holtburger has three failure modes. (1) nav_file.js uses parseFloat, so '33,579' becomes 33. The error is silent, up to 0.999 map units (about 240 m) per axis, so the route walks to the wrong place; the .af NAV path behaves the same. (2) utl_eval.js dbl() deletes commas, so '0,95' becomes 95: a DoubleValKeyGE rule never matches and a LE rule always does. This silent loot misclassification comes from RynthAi's NumberStyles.AllowThousands. (3) met.js `d` does Number('25,5'), gets NaN and throws 'bad double', so the whole meta import fails; af.js `d` arguments become 0 with a warning. WebAC accepts ',' as the decimal point in all of these readers.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/shared/src/routines/vtank.ts:58-63 `num(): number { const l = this.line().trim().replace(',', '.'); …`, used for .met `d` at :80 (`case 'd': return { t: 'd', v: r.num() };`) and for nav coordinates at :141 (`const ew = r.num(); const ns = r.num(); const z = r.num();`). :747 utl DoubleValKey `value: Number(String(a).replace(',', '.'))`. vtankUsd.ts:64 the same for `d`. docs/vtank-formats.md:22 "VTC's `HaxConvertDouble` (Constants.cs:416) does `s.Replace(',', '.')`… Accept `,` as a decimal point".
finding.holtburger_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/rynth/nav_file.js:235-237 `p.ew = parseFloat(take()); p.ns = parseFloat(take()); p.z = parseFloat(take());`, also :261-263 (exit coordinates), :266-268 (jump heading and delay), and :498 for .af NAV `const num = (s) => parseFloat(s);`. rynth/vt/formats/utl_eval.js:88-91 `function dbl(d, i) { const t = String((d && d[i]) ?? "").trim().replace(/,/g, "");`. rynth/vt/formats/met.js:110-114 `const n = Number(raw.trim()); if (!raw.trim() || !Number.isFinite(n)) throw new MetError(`bad double …`)`. rynth/vt/formats/af.js:202-204 `case "d": { const n = Number(v.trim());`. Origin: /mnt/wbterminal1/ac-refs/rynthsuite/Plugins/RynthCore.Plugin.RynthAi/Loot/VTankLootEvaluator.cs:325 `double.Parse(d[idx], NumberStyles.Float | NumberStyles.AllowThousands, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`.
finding.decomp_evidence: metaf (the format authority) in /mnt/wbterminal2/met-corpus/format-spec-source/metaf-project: Navigation/NavNodes/NPoint.cs:20-24 `_x = Double.Parse(f.line[f.L++]);` and :32-34 `f.line.Add(c.ToString());`; NPortal_NPC.cs:72-79 does the same. Both are culture-sensitive, and there is no CultureInfo or InvariantCulture anywhere in metaf-project. The local corpus (CRLF, all '.') contains no comma file, so this is robustness for European players' files rather than an observed failure.
finding.proposed_change: Add a tiny local helper in each module, because Wave-1 packages may not import each other and nav_file.js sits outside vt/: `const vtNum = (s) => Number(String(s ?? '').trim().replace(',', '.'))`, a single comma, since VTank never writes group separators. Use it at the nav_file.js parse sites (ew/ns/z, exit*, heading/delay, .af `num`), in utl_eval.js dbl (replace the comma instead of deleting it), in the met.js `d` case and the numOf string path, and in af.js `d`. Raw text is already preserved (nav `raw` lines, met `_met` hints, utl data strings), so writers stay byte-stable. New tests: a .nav with 33,579/42,07/0,39 gives ew 33.579 and ns 42.07. A .utl rule `0;1;5` with data ['0,95','5'] keeps an item with floats{5:0.96} and returns null for 0.5. A .met MobsInDist_Name with `d\r\n25,5` gives dist 25.5 and rewrites byte-identically. No existing test asserts comma behaviour.

WebAC vtank.ts:58-63 and :747 accept ','. The comparer's main justification is refuted, though. metafREADME.af:266-269 (repeated in metaf-project/Core/FileOutputStrings.cs:341-344) says: "I have now forced .NET to remain culture-invariant for metaf, wherever it runs ... but it does require periods, not commas", and ".met always uses periods (I think)". The absence of the string 'InvariantCulture' in the local metaf-project files does not mean metaf writes locale commas; the forcing lives outside these sources. The local corpus has no comma-decimal line in any of the 48 .utl or 22 .nav/.met files under /mnt/wbterminal2/ac-discord-archive/export/media, and WebAC's own doc (vtank-formats.md:22) says "Doubles are written with `.` in every sample". That leaves one supported part: VTClassic's HaxConvertDouble (Constants.cs:416, cited by WebAC at a pinned commit; the source is not local) turns ',' into '.' when reading .utl. VTank's "G" formatting never emits group separators, so a comma in a .utl double can only be a decimal comma, and holtburger's RynthAi-inherited strip (VTankLootEvaluator.cs:325 AllowThousands) misreads it by a factor of 10^k. The .nav/.met/.af parts are optional hardening with no evidence that such files exist. The .met error is at least loud.

Keep parseFloat (not Number) so today's leniency on trailing junk is unchanged and '.'-files parse identically. In met.js `d` and af.js `d`, accept a single comma the same way. The raw text is already preserved (nav raw lines, met _met hints, utl data strings), so writers stay byte-stable.

The existing nav tests (rynth/test_*.mjs, tests/rynth_vt_nav_model.test.mjs) must stay green unedited.

implementation.summary: Only the .utl part is done, following the verifier's corrected_change and the orchestrator note. In rynth/vt/formats/utl_eval.js, dbl() used to delete every ',' (`.replace(/,/g, "")`), which it inherited from RynthAi's ReadDouble with NumberStyles.AllowThousands. A comma-decimal threshold like "0,95" therefore read as 95: a DoubleValKeyGE rule could never match and a LE rule always did. dbl() now replaces the first ',' with '.', which matches VTClassic's HaxConvertDouble. VTank writes doubles with "G", which never emits group separators, so a ',' can only be a decimal comma. finding.title: .utl SalvageCombine: the line holtburger calls 'version' is the block's char length, so an edited or new block is written with a stale length and value-mode pairs are dropped
finding.description:
VTClassic writes extra blocks as `<blockTypeId>`, `<length in chars, CRLF=2>`, then the body. The SalvageCombine body is: format version, default bands, n, n×(material, bands), and in newer blocks nValueModes plus that many (material, value) pairs. holtburger ported RynthSuite's misreading: it reads the length line as `version`, the format version as `enabled`, and the trailing `0` (nValueModes) as a terminator. Unedited files round-trip because the trailer is echoed verbatim. Whenever writeUtl takes its canonical branch (salvageCombine edited, built in code, or a JSON profile without `_fmt`), it writes `sc.version`, the old length. In holtburger's own test, default bands '1-6, 7-8' plus one material produce a 29-char body written with length 11. VTClassic then reads 11 chars and tries to parse the rest as another block, which corrupts the profile. The writer also always emits `0` value modes, and parseSalvage stops before them, so newer blocks lose them on rewrite. Proof from holtburger's own corpus: in RynDQLLootProfile, '277' equals exactly the CRLF char length of the rest of the block; in the Aun profile, '11' equals len('1

0
0
'). Both were computed here.

finding.proposed_change: In writeUtl's canonical branch, compute the length line as the sum of (utf8Len(line) + 2) over the body lines (the same convention as utlLengthCode) instead of echoing sc.version. In parseSalvage, read nValueModes and its pairs into `valueModes`, adding the field only when the count is above 0 so the existing corpus deepEquals hold, and write them back instead of the hard-coded '0'. Keep the field names `version` and `enabled` (existing tests deepEqual them) but document that they hold the block length (informational) and the block format version. New test: parse the RynDQL fixture, edit materials[0].bands, write it, and assert the line after SalvageCombine equals the CRLF char length of the block that follows; then parse back. Caveat: the existing assertions at tests/rynth_vt_formats_utl.test.mjs:355 and :366 encode the bug (length 11 for a 29-char body) and must be amended, which needs owner sign-off under the 'existing tests unedited' rule. :186 stays valid, since 11 is correct there. Nothing at runtime consumes salvageCombine (CombineSalvage is inert), so bot behaviour and Default parity are unchanged.

finding.title: metaf .af EmbedNav point transform {a b c d e f g} is ignored, so duplicated-dungeon metas run the untransformed route
finding.description: metaf documents this feature: "for duplicate dungeons, you can create one nav, then simply transform it… Seven numbers = entirely new nav". When it builds the .met, metaf applies x'=a·x+b·y+e, y'=c·x+d·y+f, z'=z+g to every node and to the ptl/tlk target position. holtburger parses the seven numbers, warns 'point transform … is not supported (ignored)' and embeds the untransformed nav. In a meta written this way, the bot walks the source dungeon's coordinates while standing in another landblock, so legs are unreachable and it falls into unwedge loops. WebAC implements the transform. The gap is loud (a warning), and no file in the local .af corpus uses the feature, so the value is medium-low. This is an additive fix with a ready reference.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/shared/src/routines/vtankAf.ts:167-177 (EmbedNav parses `{a b c d e f g}` and throws unless there are 7 finite numbers). :275 `const moved = e.transform ? transformNav(nav, e.transform) : nav;`. :281-295 transformNav maps node ew/ns/z and, for types 6/7, the target x/y/z.
finding.holtburger_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/rynth/vt/formats/af.js:174 `EmbedNav: [["tag", "word"], ["displayName", "s"], ["_xf", "s?"]]`; :288-290 `if (field === "_xf") { warn(`${where}: EmbedNav point transform {${tok.value}} is not supported (ignored)`); continue; }`.

finding.proposed_change: In af.js, when an EmbedNav carries `_xf`, accept exactly 7 finite numbers (otherwise keep today's warning and ignore it). Build a derived nav: clone the cited NAV's points, apply the affine map to ew/ns/z (and exitEW/exitNS/exitZ for types 6/7), rebuild navText with nav_file.writeNav, and register it under a derived tag (navTagFor(`${tag}~xf`)) so untransformed citations of the same NAV keep the original. writeAf then emits the derived NAV as a plain section, just as metaf bakes transforms into the .met. This is additive: only files that contain a transform change behaviour. New test: a 2-point NAV plus a ptl point, cited with `{1 0 0 1 0.8 -0.8 0}`; assert the shifted coordinates and target, and that the plain citation is unchanged.

verification.reasoning: rynth/vt/formats/af.js:174 declares `EmbedNav: [["tag","word"],["displayName","s"],["_xf","s?"]]`. :288-290 warns 'EmbedNav point transform {...} is not supported (ignored)' and drops it. metaf-project/Navigation/Nav.cs:18-33 defines _xf and ApplyXF (x'=a·x+b·y+e, y'=c·x+d·y+f, z'=z+g). AEmbedNav.cs ExportToMet sets `tmp.transform = _xf` per EmbedNav before exporting, and ImportFromMetAF parses the 7 doubles. ApplyXF is applied in EVERY node type's ExportToMet: NPoint, NPause, NChat, NOpenVendor, NRecall, NCheckpoint, NJump, NPortal, NPortal_NPC (both my and obj xyz) and NNPCTalk. A jump's heading is NOT rotated. metafREADME.af:102-104 documents the feature. WebAC vtankAf.ts:167-177, :275 and :281-295 implement it. The gap is real but loud (warning), and 0 of the 3 corpus .af files use a transform (the 18 EmbedNav lines in BGAugGem0 have none), so the value is low.
verification.corrected_change: In af.js, when an EmbedNav carries `_xf`, accept exactly 7 finite numbers (else keep today's warning). Build a derived nav: parse the cited NAV's navText with nav_file.parseNav. For every point apply the affine map to ew/ns/z, and also to exitEW/exitNS/exitZ for types 6 and 7. Leave the jump headingDeg unchanged, as metaf does. Regenerate navText with writeNav, and register the result under a derived tag (navTagFor(`${tag}~xf`) via the existing usedTags), so plain citations of the same NAV keep the original. The EmbedNav node then cites the derived tag. writeAf emits the derived NAV as a plain section, the same baked form metaf writes into the .met.

No corpus or fixture file has one, so the existing af/meta tests are unaffected. The Default profile loads no meta. Do not edit nav_file.js; use its exported parseNav/writeNav only.
verification.test_plan: New tests/rynth_vt_formats_af_xf.test.mjs: a 2-point NAV plus a ptl (type 6) point, cited once plainly and once with `{1 0 0 1 0.8 -0.8 0}`; assert the derived nav's ew/ns are shifted by +0.8/-0.8, the ptl exit coordinates shifted the same way, z unchanged, the plain citation's navText byte-identical to the original, no warning for the valid transform, and a warning (and ignore) for a 6-number transform. Also check writeMet(parseAf(...)) re-parses with the transformed points.

implementation.summary: rynth/vt/formats/af.js now applies the metaf EmbedNav point transform `{a b c d e f g}`. Before this, it warned "not supported (ignored)" and embedded the untransformed nav. parseOp accepts a braced string of exactly 7 finite numbers and stashes it as a temporary `_xf`; anything else still warns and is ignored, with the message reworded to "is not seven numbers {a b c d e f g} (ignored)". In the EmbedNav link stage of parseAfText, a transformed citation produces a derived nav via the new applyXf. applyXf runs nav_file.parseNav on the cited navText and maps every point with x'=a·x+b·y+e, y'=c·x+d·y+f, z'=z+g (metaf Nav.cs ApplyXF). For ptl/tlk (types 6/7) it maps exitEW/exitNS/exitZ the same way and leaves the jmp heading alone. It deletes p.raw on each transformed point so writeNav cannot echo the original lines, then regenerates navText with writeNav. The derived nav is registered under navTagFor(`${tag}~xf`, usedTags), where usedTags is built from the file's nav keys, and the EmbedNav cites it. Plain citations keep the original nav byte-identical, and an identical transform of the same nav reuses one derived nav. Follow and empty routes are left as they are, since they have no positions to move. A route that cannot be parsed warns and falls back to the untransformed route. writeAf writes the derived nav as a plain NAV section and writeMet embeds the moved route, the same baked form metaf produces. Only .af files that contain a transform behave differently. The Default profile, corpus and fixtures are unaffected.

tests_run.result: all 4 checks passed (unchanged, run before and after the final rename)
342 corpus checks passed (17 .met, 3 .af, 48 .utl, 1 view); .af files still parse with 0 warnings and writeAf/parseAf stays stable

implementation.deviations: (1) An invalid transform still warns and is ignored, but the text now says what is wrong: "EmbedNav point transform {…} is not seven numbers {a b c d e f g} (ignored)". No existing test asserted the old "not supported" text. (2) An unbraced token in the transform slot is rejected (metaf requires the {…} form). (3) af.js had no `usedTags`, so a Set of the file's lower-cased NAV keys is built before linking and passed to navTagFor. The derived navs are merged into meta.navs only after the walk, so a later citation cannot accidentally resolve to a derived tag. (4) Additions the verifier did not specify: an identical (nav, transform) pair reuses one derived nav; a transform on a Follow or empty route is a silent no-op that cites the original, as metaf's NFollow has no position; and a route that cannot be parsed, or has a non-numeric position, warns and keeps the untransformed route. (5) A source NAV cited only through a transform still counts as cited (no "never used" warning) and still takes its displayName from the first citation, as before. The derived nav takes the transformed citation's display name. nav_file.js was not edited; only its exported parseNav/writeNav are used.
implementation.follow_ups: The orchestrator asked for p.raw to be deleted, so writeNav writes transformed points fresh. Its fresh path writes PortalLegacy (type 1) and OpenVendor (type 5) guids unsigned (`>>> 0`), while af.js's own raw lines and VTank use signed Int32. In a transformed nav, a prt/vnd guid at or above 0x80000000 would therefore be written as an unsigned decimal in an exported .met, which VTank's Int32.Parse may reject. ACE static guids (0x7xxxxxxx) are unaffected, and a vendor guid in a duplicated dungeon is unlikely to make sense anyway. A proper fix is a signed fresh-write option in nav_file.writeNav, which was out of scope here (nav_file.js is not editable in this lane). Separately, nav_file.parseAfNavs (the route-import path, rynth/nav_import.js) reads NAV sections only and never sees EmbedNav transforms; that matches its scope but is worth knowing.

finding.title: No import for VTank .usd settings profiles (Settings, MyMonsters, Items, Consumables and buff tables)
finding.description: A VTank user's real configuration lives in .usd profile files. holtburger's own research confirms VTank profiles are .usd files, per character with 'By Char'. Those files include the monster list, with priorities and the per-monster debuff and spell switches that holtburger's MonsterList models one-to-one. holtburger imports .met, .af, .nav and .utl but not .usd, so moving a VTank setup over means re-entering every option and monster row by hand. WebAC has a reader and writer it validated byte-for-byte on five VTank-written files, plus a precise spec. A .usd is the .met typed-value grammar plus a `b` (True/False) tag, a `<tableCount>`, then per table: name, ncols, column names, `y`/`n` index flags, nrows and row-major values. RechargeHandlerSet is a nested `TABLE` value. Settings rows carry a SettingType (1 bool, 2 double in map units ÷240, 3 int, 5 string, 6 enum, 7 table). The MyMonsters switch columns map onto holtburger's column letters.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/shared/src/routines/vtankUsd.ts:65 `case 'b': … return { t: 'b', v: /^true$/i.test(l) };`; :75 `const index = Array.from({ length: ncols }, () => r.line().trim() === 'y');`; :82 parseUsd; :132-136 `MONSTER_SWITCHES = [['Imperil','I'],['Vuln','V'],['Yield','Y'],['GravityW','G'],['Attack','A'],['Ring','R'],['Broadside','B'],['Fester','F'], …]` and USD_MONSTER_COLUMNS; :161 SettingType; :311 importUsd. docs/vtank-formats.md:386-419 (layout and the tables Settings, MyMonsters, BuffedItems, AssistItems with kinds 0-11, GemFoodItems, ExtraBuffSpells/AntiExtraBuffSpells, ItemUseSpecifiers). Fixture: tests/fixtures/vtank/hunter.usd.

In rynth/vt/settings/schema.js, the VTank-name rows with vtUnit "lbf" already convert ×240. /mnt/wbterminal1/rynth-vtank-2026-10-12/understand/U7a-cs-support.md:72 and :517 record that VTank profiles are .usd files.
finding.decomp_evidence: n/a: VTank is closed source, and WebAC's facts come from VTank-written files (MossTank fixtures, kept out of their repo).
finding.proposed_change: Add a new rynth/vt/formats/usd.js that reuses met.js's Reader grammar, adding the `b` tag and the multi-table header with y/n flags. `parseUsd(text)` returns { settings: [{vtName, value, type}], monsters, items, consumables, extraBuffs, blacklistedBuffs, warnings }. Add `library.importUsd(name, text)`, which always creates a NEW user profile, never Default. It applies Settings through VtOptions' VTank-name accessor (unknown names become warnings, as with /rs opt), maps MyMonsters to MonsterList entries (WeaponToUse -1 means auto), and keeps object ids with a 'server-specific' warning. Ship import only first and add export later. Port the format facts from WebAC's spec (AGPL; attribute vtankUsd.ts and docs/vtank-formats.md §6), and validate against a real VTank .usd before calling it done. Default and the parity oracle are untouched.

implementation.summary: Added rynth/vt/formats/usd.js, a VirindiTank `.usd` settings-profile reader and importer (import only). The format facts are attributed to WebAC vtankUsd.ts and docs/vtank-formats.md §6 (AGPL-3.0). parseUsd(text|bytes) uses met.js's typed-value grammar, plus the `b` True/False tag (any case), the table-count header and y/n index flags, nested TABLE values, the same CRLF-count `ba` rule with a raw-count retry for bare-LF copies, and a decimal comma. It returns { tables, settings:[{vtName,t,value,type}], monsters (already in MonsterList entry shape), items, consumables, gemFood, extraBuffs, blacklistedBuffs, itemUses, warnings } and never throws. It is bounded against nesting bombs, huge row counts and truncation. importUsdProfile(options, name, data, {mineOnly, normalizeMonster}) only ever creates a NEW user profile. It refuses Default, [By char], an existing name, an invalid name or a bad file before anything changes. It then calls VtOptions.saveAs, sets each Settings row through options.set by VTank name (lbf ×240, clamps and unknown names reported as warnings), and stores MyMonsters through the MonsterList validator. That mapping is <DEFAULT>→DEFAULT, 14 switch columns→F/B/G/I/Y/V/A/R/S/WC/FC/Cp/DC/Cs, VT damage ints→elements, WeaponToUse -1 and SecondaryEquip 0→Auto, and other object ids kept with a server-specific warning. The Items, Consumables and Buffs tables are parsed and reported but not applied. The layer exposes it as bot.vt.library.importUsd(name, data, {mineOnly}), with normalizeEntry injected. The Default profile and the parity oracle are untouched (parity test passes unchanged).

finding.title: Expression number-to-text follows .NET Core shortest round-trip (RynthAi), not the 15-digit G of VTank and UtilityBelt (.NET Framework)
finding.description: VTank and UtilityBelt are Decal plugins on .NET Framework, where Double.ToString() prints at most 15 significant digits. holtburger's formatNumber deliberately reproduces .NET Core 3.0+ shortest round-trip, because the reference it ported (RynthAi) targets net10.0. So `echo[1/3]` prints 0.3333333333333333 where VTank prints 0.333333333333333, and 0.1+0.2 prints 0.30000000000000004 where VTank prints 0.3. The difference shows in echo, ChatExpr and `/f` chat lines built by concatenation, and in string comparisons or regexes over concatenated numbers. WebAC's formatNumber is G15 and its test pins `1/3+``` -> '0.333333333333333'. holtburger's exponent layout (E+XX, fixed when -5 < exponent < 15) is already better than WebAC's and should be kept.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/shared/src/routines/vtankExpr.ts:528-533 `/** Number → text the way .NET's double.ToString() ("G15") prints it. */ export function formatNumber(n) { if (Number.isInteger(n) && Math.abs(n) < 1e15) return String(n); … return String(Number(n.toPrecision(15))); }`; tests/verify-vtank-expr.ts:191 `expect(run('1/3+``')).toBe('0.333333333333333');`.
finding.holtburger_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/rynth/vt/expr/values.js:104-121 formatNumber, commented ".NET double.ToString(\"G\", InvariantCulture) (.NET Core 3.0+: shortest round-trip digits …)", with :113 `const exp = n.toExponential(); // shortest round-trip mantissa`. tests/rynth_vt_expr.test.mjs:194 `assert.equal(formatNumber(0.1 + 0.2), "0.30000000000000004");`. /mnt/wbterminal1/rynth-vtank-2026-10-12/understand/U5-cs-meta.md:565 records the .NET Core choice. rynthsuite RynthAi csproj `<TargetFramework>net10.0-windows</TargetFramework>`.
finding.decomp_evidence: n/a. The change in Double.ToString between .NET Framework and .NET Core 3.0 is a documented runtime behaviour, and VTank and UB are .NET Framework Decal plugins.
finding.proposed_change: In formatNumber, take the mantissa from `n.toExponential(14)` (15 significant digits) with trailing zeros stripped, and keep the existing fixed/E±XX layout rules. This is not a pure fix under this round's rules: tests/rynth_vt_expr.test.mjs:194 pins the RynthAi output, so the owner must choose between VTank fidelity and RynthAi parity. The Default profile evaluates no expressions, so parity is unaffected either way.

verification.reasoning: rynth/vt/expr/values.js:104-121 formatNumber is documented as '.NET Core 3.0+: shortest round-trip' and uses n.toExponential() (shortest). tests/rynth_vt_expr.test.mjs:194 pins formatNumber(0.1+0.2) === '0.30000000000000004'. U5-cs-meta.md:565 records that the .NET Core choice was deliberate, made to match RynthAi (net10). WebAC vtankExpr.ts:529-532 uses `String(Number(n.toPrecision(15)))`, and tests/verify-vtank-expr.ts:191 pins '0.333333333333333'. That .NET Framework's Double.ToString() gives at most 15 significant digits ('G15'-like) while .NET Core 3.0+ gives shortest round-trip is a documented runtime change, and VTank/UB are .NET Framework Decal plugins. However, VTank's expression engine is closed source, so it is unverified that it stringifies numbers through Double.ToString() (rather than a format string or 'R'). WebAC's test is its own inference, and the only Discord hit with a 17-digit float (utilitybelt 2024-04-21 '113.99999999999999') is a JavaScript discussion, so it settles nothing. The change also requires editing a pinned existing test, so it is an owner decision between VTank fidelity and RynthAi parity, not a fix. WebAC's version is worse for |n| ≥ 1e21 (lower-case 'e+21'), so only the 15-digit mantissa idea should be taken.
verification.corrected_change: If the owner picks VTank fidelity: in formatNumber, take `n.toExponential(14)`, strip trailing zeros from the mantissa, and derive the exponent from THIS rounded string, because rounding to 15 digits can carry, e.g. 999999999999999.9 → 1E+15. Then apply the existing layout: fixed when -5 < e < 15 (print the 15-digit-rounded value in fixed notation, e.g. via String(Number(n.toPrecision(15))) for that range), otherwise mantissa + 'E±XX'. Keep -0 → '0', NaN and Infinity as today. Otherwise leave it as is and document the choice in the README.
verification.rynth_risk: The Default profile evaluates no expressions, so parity is unaffected. It changes the text of echo/ChatExpr and string compares built from numbers in user metas, which could change which rules fire for metas that regex-match concatenated numbers. tests/rynth_vt_expr.test.mjs:194 must be edited, which needs owner sign-off under the 'existing tests unedited' rule.
