finding.title: Buff B5 'achieved tier' cap is seeded from any registry read and also caps the cast target, locking a family below its best tier for the life of the bot (and across relogs)
finding.description: buff_loop._recordAchievedTiers records the tier of EVERY registry entry whose spell the character knows, not only tiers our own casts landed at. That includes an older lower-tier buff that is already active at login, or one landed after a B9/fizzle walk-down. The first _refresh runs in the same tick the B1 gate opens, because lastRefreshAt starts at 0. The cap then feeds _buildLadders, which drops every ladder rung above it, so `desired` is re-resolved DOWN to the landed tier. _isActiveReal then sees landed == desired and never upgrades. The cap only rises when a higher tier lands, and the bot never casts above the cap, so the family stays locked for the life of the bot. Across sessions the lower buff never lapses (it is rebuffed at 300 s remaining), so the lock re-seeds on every login. Fizzle walks feed the same trap: three fizzles in a row (≈12% per triple at skill = power under ACE's 0.07 sigmoid) add the tier to `_unresolvable` permanently. A long hunt therefore ratchets families down and never recovers. The RynthAi reference applies the cap only inside IsBuffActive. Its target resolver FindBestSpellId → GetDynamicSelfBuffId never reads _familyAchievedTier, so in C# a low cap only delays an upgrade until the next expiry window. Test F3 in rynth_bufffix_test.cjs passes only because it hand-seeds the cap to 7 after mkLoop's own _refresh has already re-resolved the ladder down to tier 5.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/agent/macro/buffPlan.ts:372 recomputes the best rung on every plan with no learned cap: `if (skill === null || s.power + threshold > skill) continue;`. In buffPlan.ts:399-410 remainingFor treats a weaker same-category enchantment as missing (`if (power !== undefined && power < planned.power) continue;`), so a lower tier is always replaced by the better level.
finding.holtburger_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/rynth/buff_loop.js:584-597 `_recordAchievedTiers(reg)` reads any registry row: `if (tier > prev) { this._familyAchievedTier.set(family, tier); changed = true; }`, then `_buildLadders()`. :562-568 `const cap = this._familyAchievedTier.get(fam) ?? 8; ... .filter((e) => e.tier <= cap)` caps the CAST target. :301 `this.lastRefreshAt = 0;` with :1270 `if (now - this.lastRefreshAt > PERIODIC_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS) { this._refresh(); ...}` means the cap is seeded on the first ready tick. :746-747 the upgrade test uses `Math.min(desiredTier, cap)`. :950 `this._unresolvable.add(spellId)` is never removed after a walk. rynth_bufffix_test.cjs:158 `loop._familyAchievedTier.set(101, 7); // seen landing at 7` (manual seed after mkLoop :81-88 already ran _refresh).
finding.decomp_evidence: n/a (bot logic). Reference bot: /mnt/wbterminal1/ac-refs/rynthsuite/Plugins/RynthCore.Plugin.RynthAi/Combat/BuffManager.cs:1207-1209 (cap only in IsBuffActive), :1251-1256 RecordAchievedTier, :945-946 FindBestSpellId → SpellManager.GetDynamicSelfBuffId (never reads the cap). ACE fizzle odds: ACE.Server/WorldObjects/Player_Magic.cs:528-540 + SkillCheck.cs:19-21 (factor 0.07).
finding.proposed_change: rynth/buff_loop.js: (a) in _buildLadders, remove `.filter((e) => e.tier <= cap)`. This matches C#: the cap stays only in _isActiveReal as the Incantation flap guard. (b) Optionally record an achieved tier only from our own B8 confirm, when the landed tier is lower than the cast tier, not from arbitrary registry rows. (c) Give `_unresolvable` entries added by a FIZZLE walk an expiry (10 min, the same as vt/combat/attack_planner.js EXCLUDE_MS); 'unknown-spell' and silent no-show entries stay permanent, so F5 is unchanged. Add a new targeted test file (no existing test edited): reg=[wire(1015,3000)], known 1011..1017, raw [1011]; after _buildLadders + _refresh, expect desired=[1017] and _isActiveReal(1017)===false. verification.reasoning: The bug is real; the proposed fix (a) is not usable. Re-read rynth/buff_loop.js. In _tickJs (~1250-1272) the B1 gate sets registryReady, and in the same tick `now - this.lastRefreshAt(0) > 30_000` calls _refresh() (:673-677). That runs _recordAchievedTiers(reg) (:584-597), which takes the max tier from EVERY family row in the registry and then calls _buildLadders(). _buildLadders filters `.filter((e) => e.tier <= cap)` (:562-566), so a lower-tier buff present at login re-resolves `desired` down to that tier. _isActiveReal (:746-747) then sees landed == min(desired, cap), and the family stays locked: the bot only ever recasts the capped tier, so the cap never rises. The C# reference records from all rows too (BuffManager.cs:1383 in RefreshFromLiveMemory) but applies the cap ONLY in IsBuffActive (:1207-1209). GetDynamicSelfBuffId (SpellManager.cs:170-205) never reads it, so C# just waits for expiry and then casts the best tier. The C# reference also does not blacklist on fizzles (BuffManager.cs:570 'lag/fizzle → retry (NO blacklist)'). The 3-fizzle walk into a permanent `_unresolvable` (:949-955, :1003-1008) is a holtburger addition and is never cleared. F3 (rynth_bufffix_test.cjs:151-170) does hand-seed cap 7 after mkLoop's _refresh, which had re-resolved desired to 1015, and it calls _isActiveReal(1017) directly. The comparer missed two things that change the fix. (1) Removing the filter breaks an EXISTING test: rynth_ladder_smoke.cjs:26-35 (in rynth_test_all.cjs FULL) asserts `_familyAchievedTier.set(1,4); _buildLadders()` → 1330. Tests must stay unedited, so (a) is rejected. (2) The B8 confirm (:1296-1298) is checked BEFORE `p.refusal` (:1320), and `this.pending` (:1421) stores no pre-cast snapshot. So an UPGRADE cast whose family already holds the old lower tier is 'confirmed' at 600 ms even when it fizzles, and its fizzles are never counted. The login lock currently hides this. Remove the lock alone and a character who knows an uncastable tier 7 will recast-fizzle it forever while the old tier-5 buff lasts (up to an hour of mana and kernel time). Citations otherwise verified.

implementation.summary: Fixed the B5 buff tier lock in rynth/buff_loop.js, in three parts. (1) Registry rows, including the login snapshot, no longer set the ladder cap. They now fill a new `_familySeenTier`, which only the `_isActiveReal` upgrade guard reads, as C# IsBuffActive does at BuffManager.cs:1207-1209. `_familyAchievedTier`, the ladder cap that `_buildLadders` still filters by (rynth_ladder_smoke B5 relies on it), is now set only by `_recordOwnLanding`: our own confirmed cast landing below its cast tier, with no refusal on record. Result: a lower tier standing at login no longer pulls `desired` down to itself. The best tier is cast at the old buff's rebuff window, matching C#, instead of the family staying locked for the life of the bot and across relogs. (2) B8 upgrade mis-confirm: when a cast is an upgrade over a lower tier, the pending cast stores `pending.prior` = {spellId, expiresAtMs}. While that same entry still stands (expiry within one 5 s ACE heartbeat), the cast does not count as landed, so fizzles are counted and the tier walk runs. A pending with no `prior` (same-tier recast, empty family, or one built by hand in tests) confirms as before. (3) A tier walked down after 3 fizzles goes back on the ladder after 10 min (FIZZLE_WALK_RETRY_MS = attack_planner EXCLUDE_MS). finding.title: Loot loop never recognises ACE's corpse-permission refusals (transient strings, not UseDone errors): each non-lootable corpse costs an approach plus 3×6 s Use timeouts, every 5 minutes, ahead of buffing
finding.description: ACE refuses a corpse the player may not loot ('You do not yet have the right to loot the …', 'You may not loot the … because …') and a corpse someone else has open ('The … is already in use by …!') with a CommunicationTransientString. TryUseItem then sends a plain UseDone with WeenieError.None. The wasm turns transient strings into kind=2 chat events. loot_loop._onEvent only reacts to kind 13 and 48, so OPEN waits out OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS three times (18 s) before parking the corpse, and the park lasts only LOOTED_TTL_MS (5 min). _findCorpse takes ANY wcid-21 corpse within 30 m. ACE uses one 'corpse' weenie for monsters and players, so this includes other players' kills, fellows' unshared kills, rare and PK corpses (never lootable by others), and player corpses, which last at least an hour. The kernel ranks Loot above Buffing, so in a shared hunting spot the bot repeatedly walks to and pokes corpses it can never open while rebuffs wait. VTank's default (LootAllCorpses off) loots only its own kills; in holtburger that schema cell is inert.

implementation.summary: ACE turns away a corpse we may not loot with a CommunicationTransientString, then sends a plain UseDone with no error code. I checked this in ACE.Server Corpse.Open, Container.InUseMessage via Player.SendTransientError, and Player_Use.TryUseItem. The wasm delivers these lines as kind=2 chat with category 9 (Transient), so loot_loop never saw them: OPEN waited out 3 x 6 s per corpse and tried again every 5 minutes, while the kernel kept Loot ahead of Buffing. loot_loop.js now records a matching kind=2 line (category Transient or System) when the name in it is this corpse's TryGetObjectName, and APPROACH/OPEN act on it on the next tick. "You do not yet have the right to loot the X." parks the corpse right away; the normal 5-minute park already outlasts ACE's 180 s HalfLife, so no separate deferral clock is needed. "You may not loot the X because ..." (rare or PK kill) parks it for as long as the guid stays in NearbyGuids. "The X is already in use by Y!" skips it for 10 s without parking and parks it on the 3rd refusal. The strings come from ACE source; the 10 s / 3-refusal numbers come from WebAC corpseBook.ts, with an attribution line. A corpse ACE opens never triggers any of this, so the default path is unchanged: T-P1 parity and the loop-hooks goldens both pass as they are. The done-set and LootOwnership/LootAllCorpses ideas are left out, as instructed.

implementation.deviations:
1. The refusal is recorded in any loop state, not only APPROACH/OPEN, but it is acted on only in APPROACH/OPEN and only for the same corpse guid. Picking a new corpse or finishing one clears the record. Reason: a host can answer the Use before _issueOpen switches to OPEN (the verifier's own test plan has UseObject emit the line synchronously, while the loop is still in SCAN or APPROACH). Changing the order of UseObject and _setState instead would have risked the parity goldens.
2. The verifier's "retry no sooner than ~180 s in view, or LOOTED_TTL, whichever is later" is just the normal LOOTED_TTL park. LOOTED_TTL is 300 s counted from the park, which always comes after first sight, so it always ends after "180 s from first sight". No first-sight tracking was added; a comment explains this.
3. Two small hardening choices: only chat category Transient (9) or System (0) is accepted (a fake with no u32b reads as 0), and the line is trimEnd()'d. If TryGetObjectName is missing or returns nothing, the anchored ACE pattern alone is trusted.
4. _finishCorpse gained an optional `park = true` parameter so the in-use skip leaves the corpse without parking it. All existing callers behave exactly as before.
implementation.follow_ups:
1. Kept out as ordered, for a later default-OFF / VT-cell item: a done-set of finished corpses (like RynthAi's _completedCorpses, forgotten when the guid leaves view) and a live LootOwnership / LootAllCorpses filter (RequestId, then LongDesc "Killed by <me>." — RynthAi CorpseOpenController.cs:625-787 defaults to My Kills Only; vt/settings/schema.js:155 LootAllCorpses is still inertBool).
2. ACE refusals name a corpse, not a guid, so a refusal for a different corpse with the same name (for example "Corpse of Drudge") that arrives while we are opening ours would park ours by mistake. This needs the player to Use another same-named corpse at that moment; the ownership filter would remove the case entirely.
3. "Not yet" corpses that are player corpses (they last at least an hour) still cost one approach and one Use every 5 minutes, and nothing in the client tells player corpses from monster corpses. LongDesc / ownership would fix this too.
4. The orchestrator should run rynth_loot_smoke.cjs (--full) and rynth_kernel_smoke.cjs. Both launch headless chromium, so I did not run them.
5. rynth/ai/observe.js's corpse count (its comment cites loot_loop) ignores parks and refusal memory. It is informational only, but it could now overstate the corpses the bot can actually loot.

finding.title: Vitals give-up valve mistakes incoming damage for 'spell too weak' and parks healing for 60 s while the character is being hit
finding.description: The valve built for the Heal-Self-I-vs-99,999-HP livelock measures progress as the NET change in the vital fraction between two consecutive casts: `pct <= lastPct + 0.5` counts as no progress. Under sustained incoming damage (a melee tank, several mobs), each heal can land fully and still leave HP flat or falling. After 6 casts (~15-20 s) the HP axis is parked for VITAL_PARK_MS = 60 s, and _decide skips the heal arm. Only the B15 emergency (≤30% HP, stamina >20%, Stamina-to-Health known) remains, so a character without that spell or without stamina gets no healing in the most dangerous minute. `_lastPct` is also never reset when a vital recovers above its threshold, so the first cast of the next fight at a lower HP than the last cast of the previous one already counts as 'no progress'. Fizzles, which are frequent because of finding 4's skill-blind tier, also count. ACE tells the caster exactly how much each boost restored, so the valve can measure the spell itself instead of the net change.

A heal is judged by what it gives, not by how the vital moved under damage.

implementation.summary: The vitals give-up valve in rynth/vitals.js now judges a recovery spell by what ACE says it restored, not by the net change of the vital. Before, a heal that landed in full under sustained incoming damage counted as "no progress", and HP healing was parked for 60 s in the middle of a fight. _onEvent now also reads kind=2 lines through a new exported parseVitalGainLine. When a vital is at or above its current threshold (combat or idle), step() also clears that axis's _lastPct, _noProgress and per-axis cast record. The Heal-Self-I-vs-99,999-HP case still parks after 6 casts (test G3). The output of _fractions() and status is unchanged; the per-axis max is kept in this._max.

finding.title: Self-buff and vitals tier choice ignores the character's magic skill (RynthAi gates it with BuffMinSkillLevelTier), and fizzle demotions never expire
finding.description: Since 2026-10-12 vitals._spell and buff_loop B4 resolve to the HIGHEST KNOWN tier and learn a lower one only from 3 fizzles in a row. Under ACE every cast rolls chance = 1/(1+e^(-0.07·(skill−power))): 50% at skill = power, almost none 50 below. An under-skilled character, or one before its Focus/Willpower/mastery buffs land at login, therefore burns mana and 3-7 s per fizzle on each tier it cannot cast. finding.title: Indoor routing walks cell bounding-box centres and centre-to-centre midpoints instead of real doorway polygons; WebAC's doorway geometry plus a 1.83 m opening-height filter directly fixes holtburger's documented tavern and Town-Network wedges
finding.description: holtburger's indoor graph anchors each EnvCell at its mesh bbox centre (z = bbox min). toLegs emits cell centres, optionally the average of two centres ('midpoints') or 30%/50% points on the centre-to-centre line ('doorwayApproach'). None of these is where the doorway actually is. An offset door makes the straight leg cut a wall corner, and the exit 'just outside' point is guessed by projecting 9 m past the exit cell centre along the approach direction. That guess lands inside a wall whenever the door is on the side of the exit cell. The code documents live wedges from exactly this: the Town-Network wedge that midpoints did not clear, and the Holtburg tavern, where the egress walked to a CellPortal that is the serving window over the bar counter. That edge is now only excluded REACTIVELY, after a stall. WebAC reads each CellPortal's polygon (polygon_id into the Environment CellStruct) and routes doorway centroid to doorway centroid: each straight leg stays inside one cell, and feet height is the opening's bottom. It uses the polygon's Newell normal for the true outside side of an exit. It drops upright openings shorter than a body (1.83 m: windows, service counters, the tavern bar, with sills up to 1 m) and falls back to them only when nothing else connects. holtburger's DAT crate already parses CellPortal.polygon_id; the wasm exports only the neighbour ids. This is new evidence plus a ready algorithm, not a re-raise.

implementation.summary:
Indoor routing can now use the real CellPortal doorway polygons instead of mesh-bbox cell centres. This is behind the DEFAULT-OFF flag ?indoorDoorways=on (opts.indoorDoorways overrides it).

Rust (src/lib.rs, additive): EnvCellPlacement gets a one-shot `takePortalDoorways()` that returns a Float64Array with 9 values per CellPortal: [otherCellId, cx, cy, cz, nx, ny, nz, height, bottomZ], in the world frame. The rows are built by the new helpers `envcell_portal_doorways` / `portal_doorway_row`, which use the same cell-local to world transform as the PView portal-polygon walk. The normal is the Newell normal, flipped by retail's CellPortal.portal_side so it points out of the owning cell.

JS (rynth/indoor_router.js): node.doors is stored whenever the getter exists. Three opt-in options were added. `findPath` / `findExitPath` take {bodySized}: two passes, where pass 1 skips upright openings under 1.83 m (windows, the tavern bar counter) and accepts an exit cell only if it has a walkable outdoor doorway; pass 2 is the plain search. `toLegs` takes {doorways}: each transition is still exactly 2 legs, one step before and one step past the real doorway at its floor, with arriveM 0.75 and steps clamped inside thin door-frame cells. It also takes lastCentre and exitDoor.

goto_compose.js uses these on all five indoor graph walks (egress/exit, indoor goto, dungeon entry, portal transit, wedge re-path) when tune.indoorDoorways is on and the graph has door data. Egress then leaves through the exit doorway to a point 4 m out along its normal, replacing the 9 m projection guess.

With the flag off, or with a stale pkg (no door data), every call and leg is identical to before. The new test proves this by comparing walks with and without door data.

I checked the doorway data against the real base DATs with a read-only Python parse of the Holtburg tavern (landblock 0xA9B4). The bar room 0x0155 opens onto 0x015C/0x015D through 1.8 m openings over a 1 m sill (the counter). The real doors are 2.5–3.1 m. portal_side orientation points away from the cell centroid for every portal I checked. Under the old BFS, the shortest exit from the bar runs over the counter, which matches the documented wedge.

implementation.deviations:
1. **Row layout.** The getter returns a Float64Array (Vec<f64>), not a Float32Array with the cell id stored as f32 bits. Ids such as lb|0xFFFF for landblocks 0x7F80–0x7FFF and 0xFF80+ are NaN bit patterns as f32. JS reads Float32Array elements as numbers, which can canonicalise NaNs and lose the id. An f64 holds every u32 exactly.

2. **Normal orientation.** The normal is oriented with retail's CellPortal.portal_side flag (the interior halfspace), not by comparing against a cell centre. holtburger-dat tests/cell_portal_flags_parity.rs measured these as identical on 1,855,363 of 1,855,363 portals, and my tavern probe agrees. The rows are built by a shared helper, envcell_portal_doorways, called inside the existing CellStruct block of fetchEnvCellsInLandblock. It uses the same transform as the PView portal-polygon walk. It does not read snap.cell_portal_polygons, which is a later render-snapshot drain and doesn't exist when the placement is built.

3. **Leg shape.** toLegs {doorways} emits a step before and a step after each doorway (±0.4 m, clamped to half the gap to the neighbouring doorway), not a centroid leg plus extra points. This keeps exactly 2 legs per edge, which goto_compose's stalledEdgeFromWalk depends on. The doorway legs carry arriveM 0.75; the router's default 3 m arrival radius would otherwise make the doorway points meaningless.

4. **Wider wiring.** The flag covers all five goto_compose indoor graph walks, not just buildExitLegs. All five use the same opt-in and fall back the same way.

5. **Data populated by default.** node.doors and findExitPath().exitDoor are filled whenever the pkg has the getter, flag or not. This is pure data; only the opt-in options read it, and the tests prove the flag-off legs are identical with or without it.

6. **Floor/ceiling portals.** These (|nz| > 0.7) never count as too low and never drive legs; those transitions keep the 30%/50% legs.

7. **Exit point distance.** The outdoor point is 4 m out (EXIT_DOORSTEP_M), not WebAC's 1.5 m doorstep. With the router's 3 m default arrival radius, 4 m guarantees the body has cleared the doorway plane by at least 1 m when the walk arrives.

finding.title: No proactive portal avoidance: indoor and outdoor legs can walk the body into an unrelated portal (ethereal, so neither sweeps nor navmesh stop it); holtburger only recovers after the wrong teleport
finding.description: Portals are ethereal: the sidecar navmesh and the sweep probes walk straight over them, and touching one teleports the player (ACE Player.OnCollideObject → portal.OnCollideObject). holtburger never feeds portal positions into planning. findPath supports `hazards`, but no caller passes it. toLegs' first leg is the CENTRE of the cell the player already stands in, and patrols visit every cell centre, which is risky in dungeon entry rooms whose exit portal stands near the arrival point. The sidecar's v2 `avoid` circles are used only reactively after a blocked stitch leg. A wrong hop is handled afterwards (walk back out, re-plan; transit budget). WebAC hit exactly this live, when a Banderling Ruin walk left the dungeon through the exit portal beside the entry. Its fix keeps every portal within 80 m that is not the walk's own target out of the path, as a disk of reach + clearance.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/agent/portalAvoid.ts:1-51 `avoidDisks(probe, disks)` stops any probe at a portal disk's rim (header: 'A walk in Banderling Ruin (2026-10-10) planned its first leg over the dungeon's exit portal beside the entry and left the dungeon'). AgentApi.ts:2357-2375 collects every portal object within 80 m except `targetGuid`, `r: (objectReach || 1) + PORTAL_CLEARANCE_M`.

The portal ItemType constant already exists at goto_compose.js:102 `ITEM_TYPE_PORTAL = 0x00010000`.
finding.decomp_evidence: ACE: ACE.Server/WorldObjects/Player.cs:368-376 OnCollideObject dispatches `portal.OnCollideObject(this)` (teleport on touch).
finding.proposed_change: Add a pure helper (rynth/nav_frame.js or a new portal_hazards.js): portalHazards(host, {excludeGuid, maxM: 80}) → [{guid, cellId, wx, wy, r}] from NearbyGuids + ItemType Portal + TryGetObjectPosition (r = 1.5 m + clearance), excluding a planned portal leg or transit target. Indoors: pass the portal cells as findPath/findExitPath `hazards` (goal exempt), and drop path[0]'s centre leg when the pose is already in path[0]; with finding 5, test each leg segment against the disks and insert a side-step waypoint. Outdoors: send the disks as `avoid` circles on the FIRST sidecar request (contract v2 already supported and tested, rynthnav-sidecar tests T10/T11). Gate it with a new option / `?botPortalAvoid=off` escape. The T-P1 world has no portals, so parity is unaffected. implementation.summary: I added rynth/portal_hazards.js, a pure, import-free helper. portalHazards(host) finds every portal within 80 m: ItemType.Portal on PropertyInt 1, or the Portal desc flag 0x40000, read through NearbyGuids and TryGetObjectPosition. Held items and the walk's own target portal are skipped. Each portal becomes a disk of r = 1.5 m reach + 0.8 m clearance (2.3 m). avoidPortalDisks(legs, disks, {start}) then routes the leg list around them geometrically, not by cell. A segment that enters a disk gets a rim side-step waypoint, an inner waypoint inside a disk is moved to the rim, and the goal's own disk is exempt (findPath's rule). Following WebAC, disks more than 3 m above or below are on another floor, and a walk that starts inside a disk may head away. When no clear detour exists, the same legs array comes back. goto_compose.js applies this through one helper, avoidPortalsOnLegs, at every indoor graph walk: indoor goto (Case 2), dungeon entry (Phase C), portal-transit approach and retry, the egress ladder, and the wedge re-path. At the two entry/indoor sites it may drop the own-cell-centre first leg when that leg crosses a disk. The whole path is DEFAULT-OFF (?botPortalAvoid=on, or opts.portalAvoid:true through composeGoto's tune and buildTune). With the flag off it returns the same legs array before any host read, so walks are byte-identical. Recorded-route legs (replayRoute's main follow, VT nav) and every sidecar request are untouched. The egress and wedge-repath ladders count side-step legs out of the stalled-edge mapping (originalLegsWalked), so the doorway-edge blame stays right. Evidence correction: holtburger has its own incident, documented in goto_compose.js outdoorWithAssist ("live v15: the Town Network clipped a non-target portal into the academy interior 44km away").

finding.title: SurfaceTexture level lists are retail detail levels (HiFi + normal), not animation frames — the default-on 4 Hz 'animated surface' cycling is non-retail
finding.description: holtburger reads any SurfaceTexture (0x05) with two or more distinct entries as an animation ("the classic AC water/lava/effect cycle"). If every entry resolves in the baked portal data at the same size, it cycles them on the shared material at 4 fps, emissive alias included. In retail a SurfaceTexture (ImgTex, DB_TYPE_SURFACETEXTURE) holds 1 or 2 source levels and draws exactly one. With two levels it draws level[0] (the HiFi level) unless Render::ShouldDropHighDetail() is true, i.e. client_highres.dat ('HiFi' 0x69466948) is not on disk or the user lowered texture detail; then it draws level[1]. Any other count is a data error. No retail code path cycles source levels. Consequences: (a) any pair whose level 0 is in base portal.dat at the same size flickers at 4 Hz between the HiFi art and the normal art, which retail never shows. (b) Every textured surface DID pays an extra async wasm call plus a prefetch walk. When level 0 is present, its full RGBA decode runs before the second level's size is compared, so a pair of different sizes wastes one decode. (c) If frames do get built, their JS-heap and GPU copies cost memory. The comment's own census (about 2,284 distinct pairs plus about 740 [id,id] pairs, i.e. 3,024 two-level lists) matches WebAC's count of 3,024 two-level lists, about 2,500 of which have level 0 in client_highres.dat, a DAT of about 2,294 textures. So most pairs probably resolve to nothing in a base-DAT bake, and how many surfaces actually cycle has never been measured. The naming makes it worse: SurfaceTexture::highest_res() is documented as "Highest-resolution mip-level (last entry)" but returns retail's lower-detail, drop-high-detail level. That choice is retail-correct without the HiFi DAT, but the name misleads callers. New evidence versus the ledgers: WebAC's TextureManager models the ladder explicitly; there is no ledger entry for this.

finding.decomp_evidence: acclient.c:366232 ImgTex::GetSurfaceDID: `if (m_SourceLevels.m_num == 1) -> m_data[0]; if (m_num != 2) ReportDataErrorFrom(..., "Cannot get surface DID, no source levels are listed!"); if (Render::ShouldDropHighDetail()) -> m_data[1] else m_data[0]`. acclient.c:379978 Render::ShouldDropHighDetail = `!AreOnDisk(1766222152 /*'HiFi'*/, 1) || dword_81EF9C`. acclient.c:137195 RenderTexture::DropUnwantedLevels drops the leading N levels per texture-detail setting. acclient.c:294808 `CLOCache(..., ImgTex::Allocator, 0xBu)` with DB_TYPE_SURFACETEXTURE = 11, and acclient.c:304622 ImgTex::Get(did) uses type 0xB, so ImgTex is the 0x05 SurfaceTexture. acclient.c:366565 ImgTex::InitLoad loads the single RenderSurface that GetSurfaceDID returns.
finding.proposed_change: 1) Retire the animated-SurfaceTexture path, or gate it default-off behind a flag such as `?surfaceAnim=on` (scene3d/statics.js:554, scene3d/index.js:1874, materials.js _maybeSetupSurfaceAnimation and tickAnimatedSurfaces, lib.rs collect_surface_anim_frames and fetchSurfaceAnimFrames). Before deleting, run one live census, `window.liveScene3d.materialCache._animatedMaterials.size` at a pinned pose, to record whether anything ever cycled. 2) Rename SurfaceTexture::highest_res() to something like retail_level_without_hifi(), or add a level(prefer_hifi) helper, and fix the doc comment and the lib.rs comments that call it the 'top mip'. Return value unchanged, so no visual change. 3) Optional, needs the user's decision because it conflicts with the bake-base-dats-only rule: the project already holds the retail client_highres.dat (/mnt/wbterminal1/highres-acquisition-backup/eor2013/). An `eor/highres` HBA namespace plus picking level[0] when it resolves would reproduce retail with HiFi mounted, and would give the ESRGAN pipeline a 2x authentic source. WebAC's TextureManager.ts:138-145 is the reference for a portal-then-highres lookup.

ShouldDropHighDetail at :379978 is !AreOnDisk(0x69466948 'HiFi') || dword_81EF9C. ImgTex is DB_TYPE_SURFACETEXTURE=11: CLOCache(ImgTex::Allocator, 0xB) at :294808, ImgTex::Get uses 0xB at :304622. ImgTex::InitLoad (:366565) loads exactly the one RenderSurface that GetSurfaceDID returns. The other m_SourceLevels users (:136387-137432) belong to RenderTexture, a separate class, and only drop leading levels (DropUnwantedLevels :137195). No retail path cycles levels, so the semantic claim stands.

Even with HiFi mounted, the 2x level 0 fails the dimension check. It does so only AFTER a full to_rgba8 of the 4x-pixel level 0, which is the one wasted-decode case in (b). finding.title: SidesType-2 neg_surface is emitted as a reversed back face; retail's mesh build gives the neg copy the SAME winding (CW-culled, never visible from behind). NoPos polys are skipped where retail draws them
finding.description: The parser is fine. The bug is in what holtburger does with Polygon pos/neg surfaces. Retail's D3DPolyRender::ConstructMesh handles them as follows. SidesType 1 gets two windings: the second is reversed (`2 - v63`), uses pos_surface and pos UVs, and has normals multiplied by -1. SidesType 2 gets two SIDES: side 1 uses neg_surface and neg_uv_indices with normals multiplied by -1, but keeps the SAME index order, because the reversal is keyed on the winding loop, which only runs twice for SidesType 1. RenderMeshSubset culls every subset CULLMODE_CW. So the neg copy is back-face culled from behind, and from the front it is coplanar with the pos face under DEPTHTEST_LESS, with batches drawn in surface-index order. Buildings take the BSP poly path (DrawPolyInternal), which draws only the pos side. Result: retail never shows neg_surface from behind. holtburger's model triangulator and its EnvCell triangulator (the 'G16 fix-2' change) both push a SideKind::Negative triangle with reversed winding (A,C,B) whenever neg differs from pos. Under ?perPolyCull=on (FrontSide), that shows the neg texture from behind, which retail never does. Under the default (DoubleSide for entities, statics, buildings and EnvCells), the pos and neg triangles are coplanar and both rasterize from both sides. three.js uses LessEqual depth and sorts opaque items by material.id (painterSortStable), so the later-created material probably wins on BOTH sides. That would mean G16's goal of a distinct texture per side is not what renders, and the front of a wall can show its back texture. Secondary point, needing a census: ConstructMesh has no `stippling & 4` (NoPos) skip. A NoPos polygon is drawn with pos_surface and UV (0,0) unless DrawMesh drops its untextured batch, which only happens for buildings and EnvCells. holtburger skips every NoPos polygon. For EnvCell and building portal faces this matches retail, because those faces are untextured; for ordinary GfxObjs it may drop drawn faces. Not in any ledger. The 3d-render-fidelity audit's T2 cites only the per-poly path at acclient.c:455346, not ConstructMesh.

implementation.summary:
I added an opt-in flag, `?negFace=retail` (default OFF, only the exact value `retail` turns it on), that makes two-sided polygons behave as retail's ConstructMesh does (acclient.c:455780). Retail gives a SidesType-2 polygon's back side the SAME winding, culled CW, so it is never seen from behind. holtburger's reversed `SideKind::Negative` triangle has no retail counterpart.

Under the flag:
- The GfxObj and EnvCell triangulators in lib.rs stop emitting that reversed triangle.
- The baked-geometry (HBG1) env-cell assembly in geom_bundles.rs drops its back-face subsets.
- The model-bundle exports return every model `missing`, so they fall back to the runtime decode, because the baked model data has no back-face marker.

- A GfxObj polygon with the NoPos bit (stippling 0x4, which means "no positive UV indices", acclient.c:359869) on a textured surface is drawn with UV slot 0 instead of skipped.

Opacity and "textured" come from a new Surface-type cache. It is filled only under the flag, by the same callers that already prime the relief height cache, and an unknown type keeps the default decision. The flag is read inside Rust through the existing `flag_search()` + OnceLock pattern, so the bake worker gets it from the query string it is already handed; no JS changed. `url_flag_diag` gains `negFaceRetail` / `negFacePerPolyCull` so the console can confirm the flag on both the main thread and the bake worker. implementation.deviations:
1) Flag plumbing: `perPolyCull` never reaches lib.rs; it is a JS-only flag that adapter.js reads per triangle via sidesTypes. So I followed the Rust-side URL-flag pattern (`flag_search()` + OnceLock, as `?surfaceCache` and `?interiorStabBatch` do). It reaches both wasm instances (the bake worker seeds its query string) with no JS or index.html edits and no new export. Rust also reads `perPolyCull` with the same rule as the JS reader (case-insensitive `on`).

2) Front-copy rule: the verifier proposed emitting the same-winding back copy as well as the front face, drawn first via renderOrder with LessEqual left as is. That does not work: under three.js LessEqual the LATER draw wins equal-depth ties, so drawing the back copy first lets the front face win (the same as dropping it). Per-group renderOrder also does not exist for multi-material meshes, which sort by material.id. Instead I REPLACE the front triangle with the same-winding back copy. That is deterministic, has no z-fighting, and is exactly what retail's LESS test produces when both batches are opaque.

3) "Both opaque" and "textured" need the Surface `type`, which the triangulator cannot see. I added a Surface-type cache filled only under the flag, by the callers that already prime the relief height cache (the same pattern as SURFACE_HEIGHT). If a surface's type is unknown, the front face wins and NoPos stays skipped.

4) NoPos under the flag is drawn only when the front surface is textured (`type & 6`). The triangulator cannot tell buildings from other objects, and textured-only is exact for buildings and EnvCells (DrawPolyInternal, DrawMesh's skipNoTexture). Untextured NoPos polys on non-building GfxObjs, which retail does draw, stay skipped. EnvCell NoPos polys stay skipped under every flag.

5) The front-copy rule also fires when NoNeg (0x8) is set, because retail builds the back side regardless of NoNeg and reads UV slot 0. The verifier's census population excludes NoNeg; the census counts NoNeg separately.

6) Model bundles: the baked model data marks back-face subsets with no flag (only env subsets carry ENV_BACKFACE). So under `negFace=retail`, `assemble_model_geometry` / `_relief` return every model `missing`, which sends it through the counted runtime-decode fallback.

7) geom_bundles.rs is not in this lane's file list, but the verifier required the env-assembly change; I kept the edits there minimal.

8) I added two keys to `url_flag_diag` for readback. Nothing pins its output shape.

9) No JS test: no JS changed.

finding.title: Iteration (0xFFFF0001) parser mis-models the record: retail/ACE format is a CMostlyConsecutiveIntSet (total + runs), not two ints + a 'sorted' byte
finding.description: holtburger-dat's Iteration reads `[i32 ints[0]][i32 ints[1]][u8 sorted][align 4]`. The real record is retail's CMostlyConsecutiveIntSet: a u32 count, then entries where a non-negative value is a single iteration and a negative value -n is a run of n iterations starting at the next u32. ACE reads it as TotalIterations followed by (consecutive, starting) pairs until the running total reaches 0. On a complete EoR DAT ([2072][-2072][1]) holtburger's layout works by accident: `ints[1]` is the negative run length, and `sorted` is the low byte of the starting iteration. A multi-range (incompletely patched) DAT misparses, and the field names mislead anyone who builds on them. There is no runtime consumer today; the only reader is examples/parse_dat_record.rs. It matters if holtburger ever fills DDD_InterrogationResponse lists, which currently go out empty. ACE treats empty lists as 'no update required'. WebAC has the correct parser plus tests. Low priority, zero risk.

Tests: tests/verify-dat-parser-fidelity-2026-09-26.ts:126-170 (2072/[-2072,1] round-trip, split ranges, totalIterations vs per-entry max 538 vs 982).

implementation.summary: I rewrote crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/iteration.rs to retail's CMostlyConsecutiveIntSet unpack form. The source is acclient.c CMostlyConsecutiveIntSet::Serialize, which DiskController::LoadIterationList feeds the record to. The old parser read `[i32][i32][u8 sorted][align 4]`, and that layout was invented. The record is now read as a u32 count (anything over 100000 is an error, as in retail), then entries until the count is filled. An entry v >= 0 is one iteration, and if bit 30 is set, bit 31 is set too (retail's sign-extension quirk). An entry v < 0 is followed by a start word and means -v consecutive iterations. A run that overfills the count is an error, matching retail RaiseError. i32::MIN fills nothing. There is no alignment pad and no `sorted` byte. The struct is now `Iteration { total: u32, runs: Vec<IterationRun { start: i32, len: u32 }> }`, with total_iterations() (ACE GetTotalIterations semantics, i.e. the count), is_complete() (exactly one run) and ints() (the expanded m_Ints). I checked the real base-DAT bytes: portal [2072][-2072][1], cell [982][-982][1], local [994][-994][1]. That confirms the old layout only parsed them by accident. The only consumer, examples/parse_dat_record.rs, now also emits totalIterations and isComplete next to the raw fields. The change has no runtime or visual effect: no client code reads this record, and the DDD response still sends empty lists.

finding.title: Mouse-focused HUD controls (hotbar slots, target bar, radar lock, status indicators) fire again when the player presses Space to jump or Enter to chat
finding.description: Several HUD controls are focusable (tabIndex=0, role=button) and have their own keydown handlers that act on Enter and Space. Clicking one with the mouse leaves it focused. The gameplay funnel is a capture listener on document: it runs the jump on Space and calls preventDefault, but it never stops propagation. The event then reaches the focused element, whose handler does not check defaultPrevented and fires again. Concrete cases: (1) Click a potion on the hotbar, then jump: the slot fires again on every jump and drinks another potion (or re-equips, or casts). (2) Press Enter to chat: the slot handler calls preventDefault and fires the slot, and the chat panel's document listener then sees defaultPrevented and does not open chat. (3) After clicking the target name, every jump also examines. (4) After clicking the radar lock, every jump also toggles the lock. This lasts until the player clicks something that cannot take focus. Retail never had this problem because its panels never take keyboard focus and every key goes to the action map. WebAC states the same rule in BrowserDefaults.ts. A further, unconfirmed risk: Space autorepeat is not preventDefault'd (the jump branch requires !ev.repeat). A native <button> left focused by a click may therefore activate when a held Space is released.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/input/BrowserDefaults.ts:4-8 "Retail panels never take keyboard focus: every key goes to the game's action map, so outside a text field these keys must never scroll a panel"; :12-17 isKeyboardField (only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT/contentEditable keep their own key behaviour). WebAC's HUD is drawn as layout elements rather than tabIndex=0 DOM buttons, so the double dispatch cannot happen there.
finding.holtburger_evidence: plugins/hotbar.js:1040 `el.tabIndex = 0;` and :1064-1066 `el.addEventListener("keydown", (ev) => { if (ev.key === "Enter" || ev.key === " ") { ev.preventDefault(); if (!ev.repeat) fireSlot(i); } });`. plugins/target-bar.js:414 `target.tabIndex = 0;` and :439-441 (Enter/Space → examineSelected()). plugins/radar.js:654 `lockBtn.tabIndex = 0;` and :729-732 (Enter/Space → lockBtn.click()). plugins/status-indicators.js:499 and :520-525. ui/input-funnel.js:483 `d.addEventListener("keydown", this._onDown, true);` and handleKeyDown never calls stopPropagation. index.html:5736-5751: Space → jump plus preventDefault, then return, with no stopPropagation. Prior art inside holtburger: plugins/chat-panel.js:1034-1038 already guards against a 'button merely left focused by a mouse click (no :focus-visible)' for Enter, but the slot handlers do not.
finding.decomp_evidence: n/a. This is a browser focus issue. Retail sends every key through CInputManager → action maps (ACCmdInterp::OnAction acclient.c:435951), and UI panels never hold keyboard focus.
finding.proposed_change: HUD fix, can ship directly without a flag. In each of the four handlers, act only when the element was reached by keyboard: `if (!el.matches(':focus-visible')) return;`. This is the same test chat-panel.js:1034-1038 uses, and it keeps Tab-keyboard accessibility. Also, or instead, blur these role=button divs on pointerup when pointerType is mouse, or call preventDefault on their mousedown so a mouse click does not focus them. As a belt-and-braces step, also preventDefault Space autorepeat in the gameplay keydown (index.html:5736 branch when ev.repeat). Add a node test with a fake focused slot plus funnel dispatch, asserting that Space dispatches jump only.

verification.reasoning: I re-read the code. hotbar.js:1040 sets `el.tabIndex = 0` and :1064-1066 has `if (ev.key === "Enter" || ev.key === " ") { ev.preventDefault(); if (!ev.repeat) fireSlot(i); }`, with no defaultPrevented check. The same pattern is in target-bar.js:414/439-441 (examineSelected), radar.js:653/729-732 (lockBtn.click()) and status-indicators.js:499/520-525. The funnel installs a document capture listener (input-funnel.js:483). handleKeyDown (:310-381) never calls stopPropagation. isTextEntryTarget (:132-153) only defers for INPUT, TEXTAREA, SELECT and contentEditable, so a focused role=button div goes through. The gameplay raw handler (index.html:5813, __gameplayKeyDown) runs the jump on Space at :5736-5751, calling preventDefault and returning. The event then reaches the focused slot and fires it again. Space therefore jumps and also uses the slot. For Enter, chat-panel.js:1025-1043 is a bubble listener on document that returns on `ev.defaultPrevented`. The slot's target-phase handler calls preventDefault first, so Enter fires the slot and chat does not open. No code in the app blurs these elements: the only focusin listener is hotbar.js:615, which drives the tooltip. Dragging does not prevent focus either (hotbar.js:1082 `el.draggable = true`). Not in any ledger or git log. A problem with the proposed fix: in Chromium, :focus-visible also matches a mouse-focused element once any non-modifier key has been pressed (the 'had keyboard event' heuristic in the spec). So `el.matches(':focus-visible')` may already be true inside the keydown handler and is not a reliable test of keyboard origin. The same weakness probably affects the existing chat-panel guard; this needs a browser check, which this phase does not allow. Calling preventDefault on mousedown is not an option for the hotbar either, because it would cancel the native drag of a draggable slot. The comparer missed one site: emote-panel.js:362-365 rows have the same Enter/Space handler, without even an ev.repeat guard. The Space-autorepeat risk on native <button> elements is plausible: the jump branch preventDefaults only `!ev.repeat`, so a held Space can activate a mouse-focused button when it is released.
verification.corrected_change: HUD fix, no flag needed (HUD-fixes rule). Add a small ui/hud_focus.js with two parts. (1) `releaseMouseFocus(el)`: on `click` with `ev.detail > 0`, and on `dragend`, call `el.blur()`. Keyboard activation of these divs goes through keydown, not click, so Tab-and-Enter accessibility is kept. (2) A pure `hudKeyActivates(ev)` that returns false when `ev.defaultPrevented`, when `ev.repeat` is set, or when the key is not Enter or Space. The funnel already preventDefaults Space (the jump) and every matched action in the capture phase, so a gameplay key never reaches the widget a second time. Apply both in hotbar.js:1061-1066, target-bar.js:438-441, radar.js:729-732, status-indicators.js:519-525 and emote-panel.js:362-365. Do not rely on :focus-visible. As a belt-and-braces step, in __gameplayKeyDown add `if (ev.key === " " && ev.repeat) ev.preventDefault();` so a held Space cannot activate a native <button> on release. Optionally have chat-panel.js:1034-1038 use the same mouse-origin flag in place of :focus-visible.
verification.rynth_risk: none. rynth-hud.js:480 has its own root keydown listener, and the helper is not applied to rynth files.
verification.test_plan: New `node tests/hud_key_activation.test.mjs`. (a) hudKeyActivates returns false for {key:' ', defaultPrevented:true}, for {key:'Enter', repeat:true} and for {key:'a'}, and true for {key:'Enter'}. (b) Build an InputFunnel (gate open) whose bindRaw preventDefaults ' '. Dispatch a fake event through handleKeyDown, then pass the same object to hudKeyActivates: it returns false. (c) Static asserts that hotbar.js, target-bar.js, radar.js, status-indicators.js and emote-panel.js import hud_focus.js and that their keydown handlers call hudKeyActivates. Existing hotbar tests stay unedited.

implementation.summary: This fixes HUD controls firing twice. Clicking a hotbar slot, the toolbar's selected-object field, the radar lock, a clickable status indicator or an emote-palette row left that role=button div focused. After that, every Space (jump) also re-fired it: another potion was drunk, the examine window toggled, or the lock toggled. Enter fired the control instead of opening chat. A new dependency-free ui/hud_focus.js has two parts. hudKeyActivates(ev) accepts only a fresh Enter or Space that nobody has consumed, and the funnel's capture-phase jump preventDefault makes the widget stand down. releaseMouseFocus(el) blurs the control after a pointer click (detail > 0), after dragend or pointercancel, or when a press is released outside the control. A keyboard or synthetic click (detail 0) keeps focus, so Tab plus Enter still works, and the blur never takes focus away from wherever the click moved it. All five widgets now route their keydown through hudKeyActivates and call releaseMouseFocus; that includes the emote-panel rows from the area note, which lacked even a repeat guard. index.html __gameplayKeyDown now also preventDefaults Space autorepeat, so a held Space cannot activate a native <button> on release. The fix does not use :focus-visible, per the verifier and orchestrator notes. Behaviour/HUD fix, default-ON, no flag, and rendering is unchanged.

tests_run.result: PASS 15/15. Covers (a) the hudKeyActivates matrix, (b) the real InputFunnel: Space jump and matched actions consume the key while unclaimed Enter still reaches the widget, (c) releaseMouseFocus semantics, (d) static wiring for the 5 plugins and index.html, and no :focus-visible in the helper.

PASS 7/7. Mounts the real hotbar.js and target-bar.js on a fake DOM with focus tracking and the real funnel installed on the document. With a mutated helper (old behaviour), 6 of 7 checks FAIL, so the test catches the bug.
PASS 15/15 (rynth launcher in the hotbar add-on column unaffected)

finding.title: Spell bars (8 tabs) and spellbook filters are stored per browser in localStorage, not per character; AddSpellFavorite / RemoveSpellFavorite / SpellbookFilter are never sent and the server's SpellLists8 is never shown
finding.description: Retail and ACE keep each character's 8 spell-bar tabs and spellbook filter word in the PlayerModule on the server. Holtburger keeps both under global localStorage keys. As a result, every character on the same browser shares one set of spell bars: an alt mage's bars appear on the main character, and a level-1 character's tabs show spells it does not know. Nothing carries over to another browser or device. Bars built in the retail client (or WebAC) on the same ACE account are invisible here, and edits made here never reach the server. Holtburger already parses the server copy: PlayerDescription SpellLists8 goes to PlayerState.hotbar_spells, and spellbook_filters is parsed too. Neither is exposed to JS. Rust: un-commented GameActionOpcode AddSpellFavorite 0x01E3, RemoveSpellFavorite 0x01E4 and SpellbookFilter 0x0286; added the action data structs, the GameAction pack/unpack arms, the SessionCommand arms (routed to session/commands/character.rs), and five additive SessionHandle exports. If the server lists are empty and the character has never synced, its known spells from the per-browser bars are uploaded once. Every edit (place, combat-bar swap, clear, tab drop) is sent as one microtask-coalesced Remove/Add diff. A spell that leaves the spellbook also leaves every tab (1 Hz poll). The filter word is read from the PlayerDescription and sent whole on every toggle; Level_9 0x1000 is kept. `?serverSpellBars=off` restores the old per-browser path with nothing on the wire, and a stale pkg/ degrades to a per-character local copy.

implementation.eye_test:
This is a behaviour check, not a render check; any GPU works. Use the 1070, off-screen, with `?nosw=1` and a release pkg rebuilt with the new exports, logged in to live ACE.
(1) Log in a character created in ACE. The spell strip, tab I, shows the starting spells, because ACE PlayerFactory files them on bar 0. Before this change it was empty.
(2) Do the following:
  - Drag a spell from the spellbook into an empty cell.
  - Drag one cell onto another (swap).
  - Right-click to clear a cell.
  - Drop a spell on another tab numeral.
  Then log out and back in: every tab shows the same spells in the same order. Gaps close up only if the order changed elsewhere.
(3) Log in a second character on the same browser. Its bars are its own and none of the first character's spells appear.
(4) In the spellbook, untick War, then relog: War stays unticked.
(5) Forget a spell that is on a bar (Delete). Within about 1 s it leaves the bar.
(6) With `?serverSpellBars=off`, the old shared per-browser bars appear and nothing is sent.
Throughout, the console must show no `[spellbook] spell-bar … failed` and no `cmd channel closed`, and chat must show no WeenieError spam.
Expected surprise: on the first login after the update, a character whose server bar 0 already has spells shows the server bars, not the old per-browser ones. This is retail-faithful; `=off` brings the old ones back.
implementation.deviations:
1) "Upload the legacy bars once" is applied once per character, not once per browser. Any character whose server lists are empty and that has never synced gets the known-spell subset of the old shared bars. This mirrors what every character saw before the update. ACE refuses unknown spells, and they are filtered client-side so no refusals are sent.
2) Hydration waits until the known-spell list is non-empty. The world, and with it playerGuid, exists from SelectCharacter on, before the PlayerDescription. Waiting avoids pruning against a missing known list.
3) The diff is one generic Remove/Add planner (keep the longest in-order run; re-add the rest at their final index), run once per microtask. combat-bar.js composes moves from two setSpellBarSlot calls, so per-call ops would churn. The result is still retail's shape: a move is [Remove, Add], an insert is [Add], and Add indices equal the compact index (count of filled cells before the slot).
4) Server entries past the 18 cells are kept as in-memory overflow and stay at the end of the server list, so they are never deleted just because the strip cannot show them.
5) Added a small Rust world mirror (src/spell_favorites.rs, ACE insert rules) and an optimistic spellbook_filters write, so playerSpellBars() and playerSpellbookFilters() stay true after edits. This matches retail updating PlayerModule before sending. It is not in the verifier's change, but it is additive.
6) A new session object or a guid change re-hydrates, so another client's edits between sessions win.
7) The pure helpers live in a new plugins/spellbar_sync.js rather than inside spellbook.js. spellbook.js re-exports nothing new except syncSpellBarsFromServer and sendSpellbookFilters, which are for tests and the console.

finding.title: LockUI (CharacterOption 0x33) is a dead toggle and the radar lock locks only the radar; retail has one server-saved LockUI that every floaty window obeys
finding.description: In retail the radar's lock button, the /lockui command and the PlayerModule bit (options2_ 0x01000000, PlayerOption 51 = 0x33) are a single state. Toggling it broadcasts global UI message 0xD, and every floaty window (chat, vitals, toolbar, power bar, indicators, examination, combat panel, smartbox, radar) re-reads PlayerModule::LockUI. implementation.summary: Retail has one LockUI: PlayerModule::LockUI = BYTE3(options2_)&1, CharacterOption 0x33. Three things write it: the radar lock button (gmRadarUI::ListenToElementMessage), /lockui (ClientCommunicationSystem::DoLockUI, acclient.c:412522) and the Options checkbox. Every gmFloaty*UI::UpdateLockedStatus reads it. The new ui/ui_lock.js holds that state. It is seeded from isCharacterOptionEnabled(0x33) on each playerStatsUpdated, hooked once through window.__pluginClientReady. setGlobalLock sends setCharacterOption(0x33) only when the value changes (like SetLockUI), then notifies its subscribers and dispatches 'hb-ui-global-lock-changed'. A 2 s pending window stops a stale stats snapshot from undoing a click. attachWindowPosition, attachEdgeResizers, attachCornerResizers and attachFloatyFrame accept `obeysGlobalLock`. It defaults to false, so the RynthSuite windows and every other caller behave exactly as before, and the per-window event keeps carrying the per-window flag. A window that obeys is locked when the global lock or its own lock is set. The radar lock button now toggles the global lock and clears any radar-only lock an older build saved. These retail floaties obey it: radar, hotbar, status indicators, vitals, chat (drag plus both resizers), examine (window and frame), main panel (gmFloatyPanelUI, confirmed in the decomp at :258271; window and frame), the combat panel and the spell strip. `/lockui` and `@lockui` toggle it locally and print the retail usage line when given an argument. They reach ui_lock through a `window.__uiLock` seam, because app/slash_commands.js may not gain a static import (the I-27 test pins its imports). The Options 'Lock UI' checkbox now works: it applies at once, follows radar and /lockui toggles, and Cancel restores it. `?globalLockUI=off` brings back the per-window-only behaviour.

It holds 91 (InputAction, MotionCommand) pairs in retail insertion order (InitializeEmoteInputActionHash, acclient.c:436034), and on_action's default arm calls set_motion(cmd, true), so fStart is ignored as in retail (:436010-436018). The verifier asked for effective keys "from LOCAL_ACTIONS or CMD_INTERP_ACTIONS" only. I added two more read-only "fixed" sources, because without them those rows would wrongly read "not available":
- Keys verified in code: combat-hud HEIGHTS/POWER_KEYS (melee + missile Low/Medium/High Attack, Decrease/Increase Power/Accuracy), the index.html backquote combat toggle, chat-panel Enter (Begin Chat Mode), and camera.js PageUp/PageDown zoom.

implementation.follow_ups:
1. input-options-5 (emotes) and -7 (selection) lanes: for their Controls rows to turn rebindable automatically, either key their LOCAL_ACTIONS rows / funnel.bindAction by the retail id in canonical form (`retailActionBindingId(id)`, e.g. "0x10000096"), or add `retailAction: 0x1000xxxx` to their LOCAL_ACTIONS rows. 2. A small UX bug that predates this change, in options-panel buildBindingRow: the Bind click calls startCapture but never refresh(), so the row never shows "Press a key…"/Cancel until a key is pressed. A one-line `refresh()` after startCapture would fix it. I left it out of scope.
3. formatBinding prints raw code names for punctuation ("Semicolon", "Backquote", "Num Subtract"). A friendlier map (";", "`", "Num -") would make the retail hints easier to read.
4. findConflictingBindings matches exact modifier shapes, but the CMD_INTERP movement keys match on ev.key regardless of modifiers: Ctrl+Q still turns left, yet binding Ctrl+Q elsewhere is not reported.
5. Bindings players stored under retail labelHashes before this fix (dead keys, e.g. "0x0A0F7607" for Sit) stay in holtburger_keybindings_v1. They are harmless and are no longer shown, but a one-time cleanup could drop them.

finding.title: The browser context menu can still open over the HUD (for example when a right-drag camera turn is released over a panel); holtburger releases held keys as a workaround instead of suppressing the menu page-wide as WebAC does
finding.description: Holtburger suppresses contextmenu only on the 3D canvas, on the virtual-keyboard buttons and in a few plugins that have their own right-click handlers. Its input funnel notes that on Windows the menu fires on mouse-up over whatever is under the pointer, so a right-drag camera turn released over a HUD element (chat, radar, vitals, toolbar frame) opens the browser's menu. The menu takes the keyboard, so the funnel's workaround releases every held key: a player running with W stops, and must then click to dismiss the menu, which can land on the world and change the selection. Retail had no OS context menu. WebAC calls preventDefault on contextmenu for the whole document except text fields, which removes the root cause. Holtburger's releaseHeld path already returns early on `ev.defaultPrevented`, so it would stay as a safety net. Plugins' own contextmenu handlers, including rynth-hud.js:462, run before a document-level bubble listener and are unaffected.

A text field keeps it, for paste.' → `if (!isKeyboardField(e.target)) e.preventDefault();`. Called in main.ts:1130 `suppressPageContextMenu(document);`.
finding.holtburger_evidence: ui/input-funnel.js:505-515: 'Windows fires `contextmenu` on mouse-up over whatever is under the pointer, so a right-drag camera turn released over a HUD element opens Chrome's menu ... release only when the browser menu really opens.' → `if (ev.defaultPrevented) return; ... this.releaseHeld("contextmenu")`. scene3d/camera.js:1025 suppresses only on `this.domElement` (the canvas). index.html:6166-6167 suppresses only on the virtual-keyboard buttons.

Keep the releaseHeld branch as the fallback, and add an escape flag `?nativeContextMenu=on` for debugging. implementation.deviations:
1) Precedence. The canvas right-press check runs first and overrides the text-field and selection exemptions. The verifier's list does not state an order. A press that began on the 3D canvas is a camera turn, so the menu Windows fires over the chat input, or over a selection left in the chat log, is unwanted. The verifier's four test-plan cases all hold, and the test adds the override cases.
2) The text-field exemption checks `ev.target` only, through the new `isTextEntryElement`, not `isTextEntryTarget`'s union with `document.activeElement`. With the union, a focused chat input would have kept the native menu over all HUD chrome. Checking the target only matches WebAC's `isKeyboardField(e.target)`.
3) The selection exemption is generic, not a hard-coded `.hb-chat-log`. It looks for the nearest ancestor-or-self whose computed `user-select` is `text` and that holds the selection's anchor or focus, or for `Selection.containsNode(target, true)`. This also covers the examine, book, journal, lore, contracts and modal-dialog prose, which are `user-select: text` too.
4) The canvas press is a boolean mark (`noteCanvasRightPress()`), not a timestamp. It is cleared by a document-capture `mousedown`, which runs before camera.js's target-phase handler, and consumed by the next `contextmenu`, so it always belongs to the latest press.
5) Suppression lives in `install()`, as the verifier specified. `?inputFunnelV2=off`, the byte-identical legacy escape, therefore also means no suppression.
6) The comparer's optional suppression of scroll keys outside text fields was not implemented, because the verifier did not include it.

finding.title: Barber is a dead end: StartBarber is only logged, FinishBarber (0x0311) is never sent, and the player's MMD note is lost
finding.description: Vanilla ACE (and the running ~/ace-server) has barber NPCs: LSD weenies 42720-42723 (Ealdred, Nawaf, Haruko, Bertrand), spawned in the Holtburg, Shoushi, Yaraq and Sanamar spawn maps. When the player hands one an MMD note, its emote chain runs TakeItems (type 74, wcid 20630), says 'Hope you enjoy your new look.' and then runs StartBarber (type 101). StartBarber calls Player.StartBarber, which sets BarberActive and sends GameEventStartBarber (0x0075, 16 u32). holtburger parses that event and turns it into a UI_EVENT 'barber', which client_events.js only console.logs. No editor opens. The note is gone, and BarberActive stays set until the next login (Player_Networking.cs:39). There is also no way to send FinishBarber: the opcode is commented out in holtburger-protocol. Retail runs gmBarberUI. RecvNotice_StartBarberNotice calls InitializePage with the 16 fields and shows the page. The page has hair, eyes, nose, mouth and skin rows, a colour wheel, a shade scroll and one heritage option (Empyrean earthbound, Undead no-flame, Shadow no-crown). Apply rebuilds the DIDs with ACCharGenData::GenerateBaseAppearanceData and sends CM_Character::Event_FinishBarber; Cancel only hides the page. ACE's HandleActionFinishBarber checks every DID against the Sex_CG lists and silently does nothing on any mismatch, so the port has to be exact. This is a HUD feature with no world-render risk: the result arrives as ObjDescEvent, which holtburger already applies (session/messages/objects.rs:838).

implementation.deviations:
- **CharGen data is a separate table, not new catalog fields.** The barber's ObjDesc parts (APC/TMC lists for hair, eye, nose and mouth strips, plus the hair-colour, eye-colour and skin PalSets) live in a new `holtburger_content::character_gen::CharacterGenFaceTable` / `CharacterGenFaceSex`. Existing tests in holtburger-core (character_gen tests::test_catalog) and holtburger-cli (selection/creation.rs, input.rs) build CharacterGenHairStyle, EyeStrip, FaceStrip, GenderDefinition, AppearanceOptions and Catalog as struct literals, so a new field would break them, and existing tests may not be edited. The getCharacterGenCatalog and getCharacterGenAppearanceStrips JSON that RynthSuite re-exports is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **barberInit / barberApply are SessionHandle methods returning Promises** (via future_to_promise), not free wasm exports. Plugins reach the wasm only through `window.__sessionHandle`; `window.__hbWasm` is a curated list in index.html, which is outside this lane.
- **The panel listens on a new `startBarber` bus event** ({rest, u32, u32b}), emitted by client_events.js for the "barber" tag. Subscribing to `uiEvent` directly would make scripts/lint-event-consumers.mjs report its KNOWN_GAPS uiEvent entry as stale (that entry also covers channellist and houses). Parsing and the `?barber` check live in the plugin, so client_events.js gets no new import and the modulepreload block does not drift.
- **Local effects run only when the request is actually sent.** Retail runs SetMotionTableID / destroy_particle_manager / play_script before GenerateBaseAppearanceData and even when nothing is sent. Here a self-check refusal or an unbuildable face sends nothing and runs nothing.
- **Effects behind two flags.** The PES part is under `?barber` (default ON), per the orchestrator. The Empyrean motion-table swap animates the player, so it is behind a default-OFF `?barberMotionTable=on`.
- **PES DIDs re-derived from acclient.c**, not copied from WebAC. UNDEAD_*_NOFLAME_PES and PENUMBRAEN_*_NOCROWN_PES are confirmed 0 (.bss) in the 2013 pseudo-C image, so no AGPL attribution was needed.
- **Plugin sinks touch EntityManager internals.** They reuse `em._attachParticleChainForEntity` and the despawn teardown (`_particleEmittersForGuid` plus `ownerRegistry.destroyAllForOwner`), because scene3d/entities.js is not in this lane.
- **No gmCG3DView 3D preview.** The verifier accepted this for a first cut.
- **Retail labels.** Gearknight/Olthoi row labels and the option labels use the retail tokens (StringTable 0x23000001/0x23000002 via computeStrHash, English fallbacks taken from client_local_English.dat). The normal Hair/Eyes/Nose/Mouth/Skin labels are hard-coded English.

finding.title: 0xF643 chargen rejection: an unknown code drops the message (the wizard hangs in Submitting) and known codes show raw enum names instead of retail ID_Character_Err_* texts
finding.description: This re-raises a deferred item. HANDOFF §6c.2 lists '0xF643 CharGenVerificationResponse texts (not verified)', and round 5 noted 'an unknown code fails the unpack'. There is new evidence: I read the decomp and confirmed the mapping, and WebAC has a ready implementation. In holtburger, CharacterCreateResponseData::unpack ends with `from_repr(...)?`. Any code outside 0..8 makes the whole message unpack to None, so no kind=6 event is raised. renderSubmitting has no buttons, so the wizard waits forever. Known rejections pass the enum label ('NameInUse', 'Pending', 'Corrupt') straight into the Failed page and the status line. ACE sends Pending (2) for Olthoi when olthoi_play_disabled is set, NameInUse when the name is taken, and Corrupt for most validation failures. Retail shows exactly four texts from string table 0x23000002 and leaves the player on the page they were on. holtburger's Failed page also offers 'Back to skills', even though the name (the usual fix) is on page 1.

finding.holtburger_evidence: crates/holtburger-protocol/src/messages/character/types.rs:436-438: `let response = CharacterGenerationVerificationResponse::from_repr(LittleEndian::read_u32(...))?;`. app/client_events.js:436-447 sets `const label = evt.stringPayload || "<unknown>"` and emits characterCreateFailed {code, reason: label}. plugins/character-creation.js:884 sets `state.errorMessage = detail?.reason || detail?.code || ...`; :1662-1680 renderFailed shows it, with buttons 'Back to skills' (edit) and 'Start over'. A reusable pattern already exists: app/login_ui_rules.js:44-76 (round-4 login-2) maps CharacterError codes to retail texts behind `?retailCharErrors=off`.
finding.decomp_evidence: acclient.c:278557 gmCharGenMainUI::RecvNotice_CharGenVerificationResponse: case 1 closes the wait dialog (success); case 3 uses compute_str_hash("ID_Character_Err_NameReserved"); case 4 uses ID_Character_Err_NameBanned; case 7 uses ID_Character_Err_NameAdminDenied; the default uses ID_Character_Err_NameDBDown. Every case calls SetStringIDandTableEnum(.., 268435458 = 0x10000002, which maps to table 0x23000002) and then MakeErrorMessageDialog. ACE CharacterHandler.cs:66-75 sends NameInUse, and Pending for disabled Olthoi.
finding.proposed_change: Make the unpack tolerant: keep the raw u32 and fall back to an `Unknown(u32)` or Undef response instead of `?`, so a kind=6 event always fires. Add the retail code-to-token table next to characterErrorInfo in app/login_ui_rules.js. Resolve the texts either through ui/ac_strings.js loadStringTable(0x23000002) plus a wasm export of holtburger-dat utils::ac_string_hash, or with hard-coded English texts as login-2 did. Show the text in the Failed view. For name errors (3, 4, 7), make the primary button go back to page 1 (the name field), not Skills. Gate it with the existing `?retailCharErrors` flag.

What I weakened:

finding.title: Chargen Appearance has no colour wheel or shade (hair colour, eye colour, skin, hair shade) and no shirt, trouser or footwear style or colour choice; all of these are rolled at random
finding.description: Retail gmCGAppearancePage has nine parts: hair, eyes, nose, mouth, skin, headgear, shirt, trousers and footwear. Each has a style choice where it applies, plus a colour wheel of up to 9 spots and a shade scroll. Spot colours are averaged over the part's PalSet, sampled at palette entry 208 for hair, 176 for skin/nose/mouth, 1312 for clothing and 259 for eyes. holtburger's wizard has swatch strips only for hair/eye/nose/mouth style and hat style. hairColor, eyeColor, skinHue and hairHue, all clothing colours and hues, and shirt/pants/footwear style come only from randomizeAppearance or the 'Randomize appearance' button. The player cannot pick a skin tone or hair colour, although the wasm already exports hairColors, eyeColors, clothingColors, shirts, pants and footwear for that purpose. A clothing colour picker brings back the deferred 'per-gear StoreColorInformation order' item, which matters as soon as colours are chosen rather than random. Retail's spot list for each gear is that gear's ClothingTable CloPaletteTemplate keys that are also in the Sex_CG ClothingColorsList, in table order. holtburger maps the colour index into the whole gender list, and its ClothingTable parse is a HashMap, which loses the DAT order.

finding.title: Attribute page lacks retail lock and auto-balance: + is a no-op once credits are spent (every template), where retail takes the points from unlocked attributes
finding.description: Retail gmCGProfessionPage::SetAttribValue caps a rise at GetAbsRemainingCredits(i). That is the total minus the sum of the locked attributes and attribute i, counting every unlocked other attribute at its floor of 10. It then calls Set<Attr>(value, balance=1). BalanceAttributes removes the overspend one point at a time from unlocked attributes above 10, round-robin from a static start slot. So the player can drag Strength up and the other stats go down, and a per-row lock pins the stats they want to keep. holtburger's applyAttributeDelta caps a rise at the sum-based remaining credits. Every profession template spends all its credits, so after picking a template the + buttons do nothing until the player lowers another attribute by hand. There are also no locks. This is a UX gap only; the server rules (sum ≤ credits, 10..100) are unchanged.
finding.webac_evidence: packages/renderer/src/ui/ChargenAttributeSliders.ts:1-30 (decomp-cited rules: GetAbsRemainingCredits @005c3b20, BalanceAttributes @005c3df0 with the static startAtrb, SetAttribValue @00482890, SetLock @00482000), :187 absRemainingCredits, :225 balanceAttributes, :269 setAttributeSlot.
finding.holtburger_evidence: plugins/character-creation.js:418-432 applyAttributeDelta: `if (delta > 0 && remaining < delta) { const safeDesired = (current|0) + remaining; ...}`, where remaining is the global sum-based remainder. The comment at :405-407 says it 'mirrors gmCGProfessionPage::SetAttribValue ... which clamps to remaining credits', but retail clamps to the lock-aware absolute remainder and then rebalances. Call sites are at :1393, :1407 and :1428. There is no lock state anywhere in the wizard.
finding.decomp_evidence: acclient.c:190600 gmCGProfessionPage::SetAttribValue: `if (v7 >= 0 && v7 > CharGenState::GetAbsRemainingCredits(v4, v5)) v6 = GetAbsRemainingCredits + GetAttribute` and then `CharGenState::SetStrength(v4, v6, 1)`. acclient.c:495274 GetAbsRemainingCredits: `v5 = 10; if (bAttribLocked[i] == 1 || i == _curAtrb) v5 = value;` then `result -= v5`. acclient.c:495469 BalanceAttributes: over = Σ − totalAtrbCredits; it decrements unlocked attributes >10 other than _fixedAtrb, starting at the static startAtrb.
finding.proposed_change: Add pure helpers absRemainingCredits(attrs, locks, i) and balanceAttributes(attrs, locks, moved, startSlotRef) to character-creation.js. Keep startAtrb at module scope, as retail keeps it static. Route the +/−/slider handlers through them: clamp, set, then balance. Add a lock toggle per row; picking a template clears the locks, as ApplyTemplate does. Unit-test the decomp's round-robin order (Str, End, Coord, Quick, Focus, Self). HUD-only.

verification.reasoning:
- Decomp gmCGProfessionPage::SetAttribValue (acclient.c:190600-190650) clamps a rise to GetAbsRemainingCredits(i) + current, then calls Set<Attr>(v, balance=1).
- GetAbsRemainingCredits (:495274) subtracts each locked attribute and attribute i at their value, and every other attribute at 10.
- BalanceAttributes (:495469) removes the overspend one point at a time from unlocked attributes above 10 other than _fixedAtrb. It goes round-robin in the order Str(1), End(2), Coord(4), Quick(3), Focus(5), Self(6), resuming at the static startAtrb.
- SetLock exists (:190167). Set<Attr> refuses a rise when GetAbsRemainingCredits(i) is 0 (:496032).
- holtburger's applyAttributeDelta (character-creation.js:418-432) only clamps to the sum-based remainder. Its doc comment (:401-406) claims to mirror SetAttribValue, which is inaccurate. The '+' button is disabled when remainingGlobalIncl <= 0 (:1421-1422).
- There is no lock state anywhere in the plugin.
- It is not a duplicate: round 5 changed skill costs and unspent credits, not attribute balancing.

In plugins/character-creation.js add pure exported helpers:
- absRemainingCredits(attrs, locks, i), as in the decomp.

Route the −, + and slider handlers through setAttribute. Add a per-row lock toggle; applying a template clears the locks. Enable '+' when absRemaining > 0, not when the global remainder > 0. Fix the doc comment.

implementation.summary: The Attributes page now follows retail's lock-aware auto-balance. implementation.deviations:
- **Name:** the verifier called the Set<Attr> wrapper setAttribute(attrs, locks, i, v, balance). I named it setAttribValue(attributes, locks, key, value, totalCredits), after retail SetAttribValue, which is the function the page drives. - **Loop guard:** balanceAttributes returns a new object and stops after a full pass that drains nothing. Retail would loop forever there, but its caller's clamp makes that unreachable.
- **Lock button:** it is a text toggle ('Lock'/'Locked'), not retail's padlock media.
- **Escape flag:** none was added. The verifier proposed none, and HUD fixes skip URL-flag gating.

finding.title: No dungeon map: underground, the map only says 'Underground'. WebAC derives a floor-layered map from EnvCell physics polygons
finding.description: This is not a retail feature. Retail has no dungeon map; it is UtilityBelt's (MIT) DungeonMaps, the de-facto standard in late-retail and emulator play. holtburger's own inventory lists it as a TODO. In a dungeon, holtburger's map shows 'Underground' with the last outdoor position dimmed, which is no help for navigation. WebAC builds the map from the cell DAT itself, without UB's lifestoned tile PNGs. It places each EnvCell's CellStruct physics polygons by the cell frame and classifies each by its normal: up-facing near the cell floor is floor, otherwise stairs; standing polygons are wall, inner or ramped; ceilings are dropped. Cells are bucketed into UB floors at ⌊(z+3)/6⌋·6, and other floors are drawn with UB's tint (grey wash above, darkened below, hidden beyond +10/−24 m). holtburger already has every input in Rust: CellStruct physics_polygons, the EnvCell SeenOutside flag and a per-landblock EnvCell fetch. WorldBuilder.Terminal's CellFootprintExtractor and DungeonRenderer (convex-hull footprints with ClusterByCellZ floors) is a second in-repo reference.

finding.title: Rust CI and cargo-tests.mjs run `--lib` only, so 74 protocol integration tests (incl. the self-described 'CI gate') and 8 GPU shader smokes run in no gate
finding.description:
The root CI job runs `cargo test -p holtburger-common -p holtburger-protocol -p holtburger-core --lib`. `--lib` restricts cargo to the library's unit-test target, so integration targets under crates/holtburger-protocol/tests/ are never compiled or run. That covers opcode_parity.rs (3 #[test], including `opcode_parity_categorization_gate`, whose header says it is 'the CI gate, always on') and generated_parity.rs (71 #[test]: codegen vs ACE wire parity, e.g. the Wave 6.A f32→f64 Qualities float override, opcode index sanity). Both are DAT-free. They need only the tracked chorizite JSON and protocol.xml, which the job already fetches. The nested external/holtburger/.github/workflows/rust-ci.yml used `--workspace --all-targets`, but the root workflow's own comment says those workflows never ran. Since 2026-10-05 nothing has run these tests. Locally, harness/cargo-tests.mjs hardcodes `--lib` too.

The JS COVERAGE_GUARD was written for exactly this 'exists but never executes' failure, but it only scans JS. It also misses the 8 root `test_*_gpu.cjs` SwiftShader shader smokes (particle FX tier1/2, weapon FX, moon FX, FX decals, lifestone FX, far-bake shared textures). Its root pattern is `test_*.mjs`, and no runner invokes them; only HANDOFF docs say to run them by hand. A shader or GL regression in those paths is therefore caught by nothing.
