finding.title: No machine-wide lock, free-memory gate or per-child heap cap on the heavy runners; the 2026-10-05 one-heavy-job rule is enforced only by prompt text
finding.description:
~/CLAUDE.md says to run at most one heavy job at a time and to require at least 2.5 GB available. The rule came from 2026-10-05, when four parallel agents each ran `node harness/run-js-headless.mjs` and froze the 8 GB laptop for about 20 minutes. Nothing in the tooling enforces it:
- run-js-headless.mjs main() starts spawning at once.
- Each child is `spawnSync(process.execPath, [entry.file])` with no `--max-old-space-size`, although several suites load real client_portal.dat bytes (e.g. test_hidefx_lifecycle).
- cargo-tests.mjs only prefixes capped-build.
- capped-build has no lock. Every job joins the same 3.5 GB `builds` cgroup with oom.group, so two capped gates started together get OOM-killed together instead of serialising.
- moving-bench, perf-walk and lib/boot.mjs launch headless Chrome with no check on other launches.
WebAC had the same incident (2026-09-30: 8 concurrent full runs crashed a 36 GB Mac) and fixed it mechanically. It added an atomic lock dir, stale-PID and orphan reclaim, a MemAvailable wait with a deadline and a clear error, and per-worker heap caps.
finding.webac_evidence:
tests/_harness/suite-guard.ts:2-20 ("one test run per machine, and only with memory to spare").
- :62 `mkdirSync(LOCK_DIR)` takes the lock atomically.
- :54-73: an owner PID that is gone, or an ownerless dir older than `ORPHAN_LOCK_MS = 30_000`, is reclaimed.
- :29-41 `availableMemoryBytes()` reads Linux `MemAvailable` from /proc/meminfo.

implementation.summary: The one-heavy-job rule in ~/CLAUDE.md is now enforced by the tooling, not just written down. The new harness/lib/heavy_lock.mjs takes a machine-wide lock (the directory /tmp/hb-heavy.lock, created atomically) and records who holds it in owner.json. A second job waits and prints who it is waiting for every 15 s. A lock whose owner has died, whose pid now belongs to a different process, or that has no owner.json and is over 30 s old is taken over; a separate lock directory serialises the takeovers so two waiters cannot both take it. Once it holds the lock, a job also waits until at least HB_MIN_FREE_MB of memory is free (default 2560). If memory is still short after HB_MEM_WAIT_MIN (default 10 min), it releases the lock and stops with a clear message. CI=true, HB_HEAVY_LOCK=0, or an HB_HEAVY_LOCK_HELD value inherited from a parent skips it; inside one process the lock can be taken again without waiting. These entry points now take it: run-js-headless main() (after --list and the empty-plan exit, exit code 2 on refusal); cargo-tests, only when it really runs cargo; moving-bench main(), never at module scope; perf-walk main(); and lib/boot.mjs launchAndEnter, which releases in helpers.close() or if chromium.launch throws. I also added a two-line lock preamble to each of the 8 test_*_gpu.cjs runners. Every gate child now starts with --max-old-space-size=HB_TEST_HEAP_MB (default 1536, 0 = no cap). Running a single test with plain `node <file>` never takes the lock.

implementation.deviations:
1. No SIGINT/SIGTERM listeners. Releasing on those signals is handled by the lock module's takeover of a lock whose owner has died, plus release on 'exit'. A JS signal listener would break two things:
- run-js-headless runs its tests in a spawnSync loop that never yields, so Ctrl-C would kill only the current child and the gate would go on to the next suite.
- Playwright's own SIGINT handler closes the browser gracefully; our listener would run first and skip that.
A job killed by a signal leaves the lock dir with a dead pid, and the next job takes it over at once (test 2d). Every other exit releases through process.on('exit').
2. Additions beyond the corrected change:
- HB_LOCK_WAIT_MIN puts a time limit on the wait for the lock (default: unset or 0 = wait forever). It makes test case 1 deterministic and gives agents a bound.
- Pid-reuse detection compares the /proc/<pid>/stat start time, so a lock left before a reboot cannot block forever.
- A takeover mutex (`<dir>.reclaim`) re-checks the owner under the mutex. Otherwise two waiters could both see a dead owner, and one would delete the lock the other had just taken.
- owner.json is written to a temp file and renamed into place.
3. Lock messages go to stderr. run-js-headless exits 2 when the lock or memory check refuses to start; other mains throw a coded Error (HB_HEAVY_LOCK_MEM or HB_HEAVY_LOCK_WAIT) into their existing fatal handler.
4. In the 8 test_*_gpu.cjs runners I added only a 2-line lock preamble at the top of the async IIFE, before server.listen and chromium.launch; no assertions changed. The verifier's corrected change names these runners. The brief's 'never edit existing tests' rule could be read to cover them. If you prefer that reading, revert those 8 two-line hunks and delete the matching loop in test_heavy_lock.mjs section 8.
5. perf-walk-1070.mjs is not locked. It drives the 1070's remote Firefox over HTTP, so the laptop only runs a light node process.

1. Optional capped-build flock (outside the repo, not edited). A plain `flock /tmp/hb-heavy.flock` would serialise wasm-pack and cargo, but it is a different lock from the mkdir lock, and it must be re-entrant. If it is not, `capped-build node harness/cargo-tests.mjs` deadlocks: the inner `capped-build cargo test` opens a new file description and blocks on the outer flock. finding.title: Packet-replay corpus test: reuse oracle_pcap::decode_pcap over committed ACE captures and assert zero undecodable or short-read messages plus a histogram snapshot
finding.description:
Holtburger already has the whole offline server-to-client pipeline: apps/holtburger-tools/src/oracle_pcap.rs goes pcap → UDP → PacketHeader → optional headers → fragments → Reassembler → GameMessage::unpack. It also has committed captures of a real vanilla-ACE session: harness/fixtures/oracle/retail-run-jump.pcap, 23.8 KB, whose server-to-client side is ACE output. But that pipeline serves only the movement oracle:
- message_json records `"parsed": msg.is_some()` only under keep_all.
- decode_pcap silently `continue`s past messages it cannot turn into a record.
- Summary counts messages and opcodes but not undecodable or short-read messages.
- No test replays a corpus.
Protocol coverage is otherwise per-message: 85 .bin fixtures plus 251 assert_pack_unpack_parity calls. Those cannot catch a decode regression in a message type no fixture covers, or a cross-message one (fragment reassembly, sequence state). WebAC's corpus test replays a real ACE session through the real connection and handler. It asserts the handshake completes, zero parse errors occur, the login milestones appear, and the opcode and event histograms match a snapshot. It is also the test that would have caught their FAITHFUL.331–337 alignment-bug class.

finding.title: No create/release/relink ledger for shader programs: flat program counts can hide release→recompile churn, a known p99 cause WebAC fixed with a 30-line ProgramRetention
finding.description: Holtburger counts compiled programs in three places: ?renderDiag, the stall probe, and an eviction-time snapshot. The link probe also times links: linkProgramCalls and LINK_STATUS ms. But nothing records WHICH key was created or released, and nothing notices when a key is compiled a second time. three.js destroys a WebGLProgram when the last material with its key is disposed, and the next material with that key links it again on first draw. Holtburger disposes per-landblock materials on eviction and entity materials on despawn. The 2026-10-04 perf comparison measured 332 adds / 329 removes in 30 s and named 'first-sight programs' as p99 cause #1. On the 1070, one lit pixel-shader link was measured at 2.9 s D3DCompile (1070 handoff 2026-10-06), so every relink is expensive. The 1070-only coldboot script (academy.mjs --linkmap/--progdump) dumps keys for a cold boot but has no relink detection. WebAC's hitch-probe logs + and − per program id with its cacheKey every 50 ms. It found 14 of 63 keys relinked during play, and holding one extra reference per program cut link-stall time in long play frames from 5,351 to 945 ms with nothing drawn differently.
finding.webac_evidence: tools/hitch-probe.ts:41-47: a 50 ms scan of `r.info.programs` that pushes `{op:'+', id, name, key: p.cacheKey...}` for new ids (:44) and `op:'-'` for released ones (:45). docs/performance-budgets.md:379-398 "14 of the 63 program keys were **relinked**: three.js destroys a program when its last material is disposed ... link-stall time inside long play-phase frames 5,351 → 945 ms". packages/renderer/src/scene/ProgramRetention.ts:29-56 retainNew() does `p.usedTimes++` once per program, guarded by a WeakSet.
finding.holtburger_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/scene3d/shader_prewarm.js:166 installLinkProbe. :201-202 wraps gl.linkProgram with `stats.linkProgramCalls += 1`, with no program identity. scene3d/index.js:599 `programs: Array.isArray(info.programs) ? info.programs.length : 0`. scene3d/stall_probe.js:303 `s.programs = _num(info.programs && info.programs.length)`. scene3d/landblock_lru.js:2522-2549 _recordProgramSnapshot stores `programs: programCount` only. Material disposal on eviction is at landblock_lru.js:1888-1892 `try { m.dispose && m.dispose(); }`, and entities.js has dispose sites at :3157, :3723 and :12754. `rg -i 'releaseProgram|relink|usedTimes'` finds only shader_prewarm.js:317-321 treating `usedTimes <= 0` as deleted.
finding.decomp_evidence: n/a (WebGL measurement; retail D3D has no runtime program link)
finding.proposed_change: In scene3d/shader_prewarm.js installLinkProbe (or stall_probe.js), add a ledger that can be armed with ?linkProbe=on. On each recordRenderDiag or render wrap, or every 50 ms, diff renderer.info.programs by `id` and push {t, op:'+'|'-', id, name, key: cacheKey.slice(0,400)} into a ring of 2,000 entries. Keep a `keysSeen` Set: a '+' whose key was already seen counts as a relink and is added to `relinkedKeys`. Expose `__linkProbe.ledger()` and add `relinks=N keys=M` to summary(). moving-bench and flag-bench then record `programsRelinked@moving` and `programs@resident`. If relinks are greater than 0 at Holtburg or on a hop tour, port ProgramRetention as the follow-on: in the render-perf area, behind a `?programRetention` escape, with zero visual change. Attribution: WebAC (AGPL). It also stops prewarmed programs from being freed between landblock churns.

implementation.summary: `installLinkProbe` in scene3d/shader_prewarm.js now also keeps a program create/release ledger. It is on only when the probe is: `?linkProbe=on`, or `{force:true}` from stall_probe. Every 50 ms and on every ledger read, it compares `renderer.info.programs` by `id`, not by length, so a release and a create in the same tick both show up. Each change goes into a 2,000-entry ring as {t, op:'+'|'-', id, name, type, key = first 400 chars of cacheKey, relink}. A '+' whose full cacheKey was resident earlier in the session counts as a relink. Keys are stored as a 64-bit hash, so released shader source text is not kept in memory. Programs already resident when the probe installs are recorded as a baseline and not logged, so if one of them is created again later it counts as a relink. New methods on `__linkProbe`: `ledger()`, `ledgerStats()`, `relinkedKeys()`, `ledgerTick()` and `stopLedger()`. The counters live in `stats.ledger` and `reset()` clears them, but the record of keys seen this session is kept, so a relink after a reset still counts. `summary()` now ends with `programs relinks=N distinctKeys=M released=R created=C resident=P`. moving-bench gets a `--linkProbe` switch that adds `?linkProbe=on` without changing the arm label. The in-page rig takes the difference in the ledger's counters across the measure lap. `toResultsV2` emits `programsRelinked@moving` and `programs@resident` (both tags already exist in the S1 vocabulary) and adds `linkProbe` to the header taint. When the probe is absent, neither key is emitted. The diag_schema `__linkProbe` entry gets an updated evidence line and the four new `stats.ledger.*` count fields. Without the flag the client behaves exactly as before (the early `return null` is unchanged), and it draws nothing differently.

implementation.deviations:
- **Tick cadence:** a 50 ms `setInterval` plus a tick on every ledger read (`ledger`/`ledgerStats`/`relinkedKeys`/`summary`). shader_prewarm has no render wrap to hang it on. The timer is unref'd in node so tests never hang. `stopLedger()` clears it; the probe has no uninstall, so there was nothing to tie it to. `opts.ledgerMs: 0` gives a timer-less install for tests.
- **Entry shape:** entries also carry `type` (three's shaderType, since `name` is `material.name` and often empty), and '+' entries carry `relink: boolean`.
- **Key identity:** relinks are matched on a 64-bit hash (cyrb53 mixing) of the FULL cacheKey, not by storing every key. A ShaderMaterial key embeds its whole shader source, and the ledger should not keep released keys alive. The 400-char truncation is only for display. A test confirms that two keys sharing a 400-char prefix are not a false relink.
- **Counter location:** the counters live in `stats.ledger`, so the existing `reset()` (which stall_probe calls) zeroes them with the other stats. `reset()` keeps the session key memory and the resident baseline, so a relink after a reset still counts.
- **Install baseline:** programs already resident at install, as in a stall_probe arm mid-session, are seeded silently rather than logged as creates.
- **moving-bench:**

implementation.summary:
Added scripts/lint-event-consumers.mjs, a sibling of lint-url-flags, and run it in the holtburger-ci.yml js job right after the URL-flag lint. It masks comments, strings and regexes and keeps offsets intact. It then sweeps app/, scene3d/, plugins/, ui/, rynth/ and index.html's inline scripts for three things: literal plugin-bus emits (plain strings and ternaries of two strings), subscriptions (`.on(`, `.on?.(`, `.once(`, `.addEventListener(`, `onBus(`, and the `["name", fn]` tuple loop in plugins/inventory.js), and bus handlers. It fails on three kinds of finding:
- NO-CONSUMER: a name is emitted and nothing subscribes.
- STALE-ALLOWLIST: an entry in EXTENSION_POINTS, KNOWN_GAPS or DETAIL_KNOWN_BUGS gained a subscriber, is no longer emitted, or stopped firing. All three lists can only shrink.
- DETAIL-UNREAD: a bus handler reads payload fields off the CustomEvent instead of `.detail`. This is the bug class behind buffs-hud.js and salvage-panel.js.

KNOWN_GAPS names the retail handler for each missing consumer: allegianceInfo goes to ClientAllegianceSystem::Handle_Allegiance__AllegianceInfoResponseEvent, and uiEvent's barber, channellist, channelindex, har and houses tags each map to their ClientUISystem, Communication or Housing handler. EXTENSION_POINTS holds the 6 plugin-API events the verifier listed, plus 5 that its grep missed: portalSpaceExited (emitted with single quotes), serverConfirmRequest and serverConfirmDone, and raiseVitalFailed and raiseAttributeFailed (all four emitted through ternaries).

On its first run the DETAIL check found 5 real handlers that never fire in production, and they are listed in DETAIL_KNOWN_BUGS:
- blood_decals.js: the playEffect and damageDealt handlers.
- carnage.js: the playEffect and damageDealt handlers. Its test's fake bus passes the raw payload, which hid the bug.
- rynth/webhost.js: the selectionChanged handler.

Fixing them would change visuals or rynth, so it is left to follow-ups. With the initial lists, the lint exits 0 on the tree and also on a git-tracked-only file set, which is what CI sees. It parses 132 of 137 bus handlers; the other 5 are built by factory functions and get no verdict. New suite tests/lint_event_consumers.test.mjs passes all 16 tests.

implementation.summary: Added harness/test_suite_hygiene.mjs, a shrink-only ratchet on PURE-PIN suites, and its baseline harness/source-pin-baseline.json. The ratchet design and comment-stripping scanner follow WebAC tests/verify-test-suite-hygiene.ts (AGPL-3.0), with the verifier's more lenient rule. A suite is PURE-PIN when it reads app source text and executes no app code. Reading means an fs read plus a non-import literal naming scene3d/, app/, src/, plugins/, ui/ or rynth/ code, join-style split segments, index.html, or harness/app_source.cjs / wasm_source.cjs. Executing means an import of app modules or pkg*/, splice_module, import_edited, lib/boot.mjs, new Function, vm, eval, Worker, WebAssembly, a browser driver, or a computed import() (loading three alone does not count). The scanner skips comments and is aware of regex and template literals, so quotes inside a regex cannot hide a read or invent one. The suite fails on (a) a pure-pin suite not in the baseline, with guidance to use splice_module.mjs, import_edited.mjs or an extracted module; (b) a baseline entry that no longer qualifies (HB_REGEN_SOURCE_PIN=1 rewrites the baseline as baseline ∩ current pins, so it can only shrink); and (c) a baseline that is unsorted or has duplicates. It also runs 23 detector self-checks on synthetic sources and checks that the scan is live. Run against the current tree: 649 suites scanned, 260 read app source, 23 are pure pins and seeded into the baseline (all git-tracked and unmodified, so nothing from other lanes was grandfathered). As INFO only, it lists 5 suites that say they re-implement the logic and execute none of it, including Tier-1 jump_charge_parity and remote_interp_ownership. No existing suite was edited, and there is no runtime or visual change.

implementation.summary:
Added harness/perf-ratchet.mjs, a pure-node library and CLI that keeps an append-only history.jsonl and checks each new run against its own recent past. History lives under --history=DIR, else $HB_PERF_HISTORY, else /mnt/wbterminal2/hb-perf-history, and the directory is only created on the first append. The rules follow the verifier and are adapted from WebAC perf-ratchet-lib.ts (AGPL-3.0, credited in the file):
- Runs are comparable only when they share renderer, bench, protocol, wasmProfile, arm, spec (anchor, mode, frames, laps), page query (credentials dropped), taint[] and pathChecksum. commit and distGeneratedAt are recorded and shown as taint notes, never used in the key.
- The baseline is the per-metric median of the last 3 USABLE comparable runs whose own verdict was not "regression".
- A regression must be worse than tolerance (10% for counts, 25% for *Ms) AND worse than every baseline value; anything inside the baselines' spread is noise.
- On SwiftShader or an unknown renderer, only *@submitted and *@resident counts are compared.

implementation.deviations:
Where this departs from the verifier's corrected_change, and why:

1. **Key is stricter than the listed fields.** It also includes the normalized page query (account/password dropped), header taint[] and the arm's pathChecksum. Without the query, renderOnDemand and rAF runs (WebAC's renderSampling rule), --linkProbe and --url overrides would share a key. pathChecksum covers the other path parameters (dist, el, hops, dwell).

2. **Renderer handling.**
   - An unknown or null renderer is treated as software, so only counts are compared.
   - The software list also covers softpipe, swrast, "software" and Microsoft Basic Render Driver (WARP).

3. **How metrics are compared.**
   - *Ms stat objects are compared on p50 and p95.
   - Count stat objects are compared on their mean.
   - A zero-baseline count uses an absolute slack of 2, like WebAC's hitch rule.
   - Names ending in Fps/fps/Rate and the metric `frames` are higher-is-better.

4. **Added an operator rebase (`--accept` in the CLI, `--historyAccept` in moving-bench).** Without it, an intended cost increase stays red forever, because regression runs never become baselines. An accepted run ends the baseline window.

5. **wasmProfile is probed in the page.** The page fetches its own loaded wasm (the Resource Timing URL, force-cache) and walks it with the self-contained section walker. I did not fetch from node: on the 1070, node's view of BASE can differ from Chrome's.

6. **programs@resident is now emitted on every run.** The rig adds a bare renderer.info.programs.length count. When the --linkProbe ledger is present, its count still wins, and its existing tests still pass.

7. **No diag-schema change was needed.** The tags `resident` and `moving` are already in SCALE_TAGS, and programs@resident / programsRelinked@moving already validate.

8. **S0 label renamed** from FAIL-dev-sized to FAIL-dev-wasm. No consumers of the old label were found.

9. **New moving-bench exit code 3** means a USABLE run that the ratchet calls a regression. It only happens with --history; exit 1 still means REJECT.

10. **commit** comes from `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` of the harness checkout, best effort, and is null if git is unavailable.

implementation.summary: I checked the finding against the current code and it holds. In carnage.js and blood_decals.js, the playEffect and damageDealt bus handlers read payload fields directly off the CustomEvent. Real bus traffic therefore never reaches the splatter or crit logic. The fix sits behind a new strict opt-in, `?combatFxBus=on` (`=== "on"`). Each module now has a `combatFxBusEnabled()` helper written like its existing `carnageEnabled`/`bloodEnabled` helpers, and reads the flag once at install time into `_busDetail`. Inside `_bind()`, a local `onBus(name, fn)` helper subscribes either `(ev) => fn(ev?.detail ?? ev ?? {})` when the flag is on, or the unchanged handler `fn` when it is off. So the default path registers exactly the same function as before. The `?? ev` fallback keeps the raw-payload fake bus in carnage_hit_guard working under the flag. A one-line console.info is logged only when the flag is on. Because the handler text still reads off the Event and the default path really does, the lint still detects all four DETAIL_KNOWN_BUGS entries; only their text changed, to say the fix exists behind `?combatFxBus=on` pending the owner's eye-test. The lint still exits 0 and reports 5 known bugs with 0 findings. The new test tests/combat_fx_bus_detail.test.mjs uses a real EventTarget/CustomEvent bus built the same way plugins/api.js builds it. It covers: flag polarity; carnage and blood with the flag off (real events do nothing, raw-payload calls behave as before); and carnage and blood with the flag on (a real event lands a hit, and a real crit sets the latch — it doubles the leg hit in carnage and widens blood's ray fan from 3 to 6). I confirmed the test fails when the unwrap is removed.

implementation.summary: I fixed the `selectionChanged` handler in `selectionClock()` (rynth/webhost.js). The plugin bus delivers `CustomEvent{detail}` (plugins/api.js `events.emit`), but the handler read guid, lodRespawn and prevGuid straight off the Event. So guid was always 0, the LOD-respawn filter never matched, and every event stamped `c.worldAt`. The handler now reads `const d = (e && e.detail) ?? e;` and uses d.guid, d.lodRespawn and d.prevGuid, so a bus that passes the raw payload (as the existing rynth_vt_layer fake does) still works. The clock has one consumer: `RynthWebHost.GetSelectedItemId`, which compares worldAt with invAt. That is called by the VT "Add selected" button (rynth/vt/bridge/bridge_lists.js:253) and by VT command target resolution (rynth/vt/cmd/compat_commands.js:277,290 and rynth/vt/cmd/stdlib_host.js:320,566). The one behaviour change: when the selected world object is swapped to another level of detail (LOD) — entities.js releases it with `lodRespawn:true`, then `_tickSelectionRules` re-selects the same guid — that release/re-select pair no longer stamps the world clock. An inventory item the player clicked after their last real world pick now stays the "most recent" selection, where before a LOD swap (up to ~2/s near a band edge) made the world target win. Real picks, real deselects, re-picks of the same guid after a real delete, `SelectObject` and social-panel emits all stamp exactly as before. I removed the now-fixed `rynth/webhost.js:selectionChanged` entry from DETAIL_KNOWN_BUGS in scripts/lint-event-consumers.mjs (known bugs 5 → 4, no STALE or DETAIL-UNREAD findings). The new test tests/rynth_selclock_detail.test.mjs (7 checks) uses the real `createClient().events` bus and the real EntityManager emitters. I ran it against a pre-fix copy of webhost.js and the S1 LOD-swap check and the S2 end-to-end check fail there as expected.
